  .IX Item "text"
  The text string to be drawn. The text must be a sequence of \s-1UTF-8\s0
  encoded characters.
  This parameter is mandatory if no file is specified with the parameter
  _textfile_.
* **textfile**  
  .IX Item "textfile"
  A text file containing text to be drawn. The text must be a sequence
  of \s-1UTF-8\s0 encoded characters.
  .Sp
  This parameter is mandatory if no text string is specified with the
  parameter _text_.
  .Sp
  If both _text_ and _textfile_ are specified, an error is thrown.
* **reload**  
  .IX Item "reload"
  If set to 1, the _textfile_ will be reloaded before each frame.
  Be sure to update it atomically, or it may be read partially, or even fail.
* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  The expressions which specify the offsets where text will be drawn
  within the video frame. They are relative to the top/left border of the
  output image.
  .Sp
  The default value of _x_ and _y_ is 0\*(R".
  .Sp
  See below for the list of accepted constants and functions.

The parameters for _x_ and _y_ are expressions containing the
following constants and functions:

* **dar**  
  .IX Item "dar"
  input display aspect ratio, it is the same as (_w_ / _h_) * _sar_
* **hsub**  
  .IX Item "hsub"
* **vsub**  
  .IX Item "vsub"
  horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values. For example for the
  pixel format yuv422p\*(R" _hsub_ is 2 and _vsub_ is 1.
* **line_h, lh**  
  .IX Item "line_h, lh"
  the height of each text line
* **main_h, h, H**  
  .IX Item "main_h, h, H"
  the input height
* **main_w, w, W**  
  .IX Item "main_w, w, W"
  the input width
* **max_glyph_a, ascent**  
  .IX Item "max_glyph_a, ascent"
  the maximum distance from the baseline to the highest/upper grid
  coordinate used to place a glyph outline point, for all the rendered
  glyphs.
  It is a positive value, due to the grid's orientation with the Y axis
  upwards.
* **max_glyph_d, descent**  
  .IX Item "max_glyph_d, descent"
  the maximum distance from the baseline to the lowest grid coordinate
  used to place a glyph outline point, for all the rendered glyphs.
  This is a negative value, due to the grid's orientation, with the Y axis
  upwards.
* **max\_glyph\_h**  
  .IX Item "max_glyph_h"
  maximum glyph height, that is the maximum height for all the glyphs
  contained in the rendered text, it is equivalent to _ascent_ -
  _descent_.
* **max\_glyph\_w**  
  .IX Item "max_glyph_w"
  maximum glyph width, that is the maximum width for all the glyphs
  contained in the rendered text
* **n**  
  .IX Item "n"
  the number of input frame, starting from 0
* **rand(min, max)**  
  .IX Item "rand(min, max)"
  return a random number included between _min_ and _max_
* **sar**  
  .IX Item "sar"
  The input sample aspect ratio.
* **t**  
  .IX Item "t"
  timestamp expressed in seconds, \s-1NAN\s0 if the input timestamp is unknown
* **text_h, th**  
  .IX Item "text_h, th"
  the height of the rendered text
* **text_w, tw**  
  .IX Item "text_w, tw"
  the width of the rendered text
* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  the x and y offset coordinates where the text is drawn.
  .Sp
  These parameters allow the _x_ and _y_ expressions to refer
  each other, so you can for example specify \f(CW`y=x/dar\*(C'.

_Text expansion_
.IX Subsection "Text expansion"

If **expansion** is set to \f(CW`strftime\*(C',
the filter recognizes **strftime()** sequences in the provided text and
expands them accordingly. Check the documentation of **strftime()**. This
feature is deprecated.

If **expansion** is set to \f(CW`none\*(C', the text is printed verbatim.

If **expansion** is set to \f(CW`normal\*(C' (which is the default),
the following expansion mechanism is used.

The backslash character **\e**, followed by any character, always expands to
the second character.

Sequences of the form \f(CW`%{...}\*(C' are expanded. The text between the
braces is a function name, possibly followed by arguments separated by ':'.
If the arguments contain special characters or delimiters (':' or '}'),
they should be escaped.

Note that they probably must also be escaped as the value for the
**text** option in the filter argument string and as the filter
argument in the filtergraph description, and possibly also for the shell,
that makes up to four levels of escaping; using a text file avoids these
problems.

The following functions are available:

* **expr, e**  
  .IX Item "expr, e"
  The expression evaluation result.
  .Sp
  It must take one argument specifying the expression to be evaluated,
  which accepts the same constants and functions as the _x_ and
  _y_ values. Note that not all constants should be used, for
  example the text size is not known when evaluating the expression, so
  the constants _text\_w_ and _text\_h_ will have an undefined
  value.
* **expr_int_format, eif**  
  .IX Item "expr_int_format, eif"
  Evaluate the expression's value and output as formatted integer.
  .Sp
  The first argument is the expression to be evaluated, just as for the _expr_ function.
  The second argument specifies the output format. Allowed values are **x**,
  **X**, **d** and **u**. They are treated exactly as in the
  \f(CW`printf\*(C' function.
  The third parameter is optional and sets the number of positions taken by the output.
  It can be used to add padding with zeros from the left.
* **gmtime**  
  .IX Item "gmtime"
  The time at which the filter is running, expressed in \s-1UTC.\s0
  It can accept an argument: a **strftime()** format string.
* **localtime**  
  .IX Item "localtime"
  The time at which the filter is running, expressed in the local time zone.
  It can accept an argument: a **strftime()** format string.
* **metadata**  
  .IX Item "metadata"
  Frame metadata. Takes one or two arguments.
  .Sp
  The first argument is mandatory and specifies the metadata key.
  .Sp
  The second argument is optional and specifies a default value, used when the
  metadata key is not found or empty.
* **n, frame\_num**  
  .IX Item "n, frame_num"
  The frame number, starting from 0.
* **pict\_type**  
  .IX Item "pict_type"
  A 1 character description of the current picture type.
* **pts**  
  .IX Item "pts"
  The timestamp of the current frame.
  It can take up to three arguments.
  .Sp
  The first argument is the format of the timestamp; it defaults to \f(CW`flt\*(C'
  for seconds as a decimal number with microsecond accuracy; \f(CW`hms\*(C' stands
  for a formatted _[-]HH:MM:SS.mmm_ timestamp with millisecond accuracy.
  \f(CW`gmtime\*(C' stands for the timestamp of the frame formatted as \s-1UTC\s0 time;
  \f(CW`localtime\*(C' stands for the timestamp of the frame formatted as
  local time zone time.
  .Sp
  The second argument is an offset added to the timestamp.
  .Sp
  If the format is set to \f(CW`hms\*(C', a third argument \f(CW\*(C\`24HH\*(C' may be
  supplied to present the hour part of the formatted timestamp in 24h format
  (00-23).
  .Sp
  If the format is set to \f(CW`localtime\*(C' or \f(CW\*(C\`gmtime\*(C',
  a third argument may be supplied: a **strftime()** format string.
  By default, _YYYY-MM-DD \s-1HH:MM:SS\s0_ format will be used.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Draw Test Text\*(R" with font FreeSerif, using the default values for the
  optional parameters.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          drawtext="fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/freefont/FreeSerif.ttf: text=Test Text\*(Aq"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Draw 'Test Text' with font FreeSerif of size 24 at position x=100
  and y=50 (counting from the top-left corner of the screen), text is
  yellow with a red box around it. Both the text and the box have an
  opacity of 20%.
  .Sp
  .Vb 2
          drawtext="fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/freefont/FreeSerif.ttf: text=Test Text\*(Aq:\e
                    x=100: y=50: fontsize=24: fontcolor=yellow@0.2: box=1: boxcolor=red@0.2"
  .Ve
  .Sp
  Note that the double quotes are not necessary if spaces are not used
  within the parameter list.
* ·  
  Show the text at the center of the video frame:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          drawtext="fontsize=30:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:text=hello world\*(Aq:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Show the text at a random position, switching to a new position every 30 seconds:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          drawtext="fontsize=30:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:text=hello world\*(Aq:x=if(eq(mod(t\e,30)\e,0)\e,rand(0\e,(w-text_w))\e,x):y=if(eq(mod(t\e,30)\e,0)\e,rand(0\e,(h-text_h))\e,y)"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Show a text line sliding from right to left in the last row of the video
  frame. The file _\s-1LONG\_LINE\s0_ is assumed to contain a single line
  with no newlines.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          drawtext="fontsize=15:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:text=LONG_LINE:y=h-line_h:x=-50*t"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Show the content of file _\s-1CREDITS\s0_ off the bottom of the frame and scroll up.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          drawtext="fontsize=20:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:textfile=CREDITS:y=h-20*t"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Draw a single green letter g\*(R", at the center of the input video.
  The glyph baseline is placed at half screen height.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          drawtext="fontsize=60:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:fontcolor=green:text=g:x=(w-max_glyph_w)/2:y=h/2-ascent"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Show text for 1 second every 3 seconds:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          drawtext="fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:fontcolor=white:x=100:y=x/dar:enable=lt(mod(t\e,3)\e,1):text=blink\*(Aq"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Use fontconfig to set the font. Note that the colons need to be escaped.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          drawtext=fontfile=Linux Libertine O-40\e:style=Semibold:text=FFmpeg\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Print the date of a real-time encoding (see **strftime**\|(3)):
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          drawtext=fontfile=FreeSans.ttf:text=%{localtime\e:%a %b %d %Y}\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Show text fading in and out (appearing/disappearing):
  .Sp
  .Vb 6
          #!/bin/sh
          DS=1.0 # display start
          DE=10.0 # display end
          FID=1.5 # fade in duration
          FOD=5 # fade out duration
          ffplay -f lavfi "color,drawtext=text=TEST:fontsize=50:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:fontcolor_expr=ff0000%{eif\e\e\e\e: clip(255*(1*between(t\e\e, $DS + $FID\e\e, $DE - $FOD) + ((t - $DS)/$FID)*between(t\e\e, $DS\e\e, $DS + $FID) + (-(t - $DE)/$FOD)*between(t\e\e, $DE - $FOD\e\e, $DE) )\e\e, 0\e\e, 255) \e\e\e\e: x\e\e\e\e: 2 }"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Horizontally align multiple separate texts. Note that **max\_glyph\_a**
  and the **fontsize** value are included in the **y** offset.
  .Sp
  .Vb 2
          drawtext=fontfile=FreeSans.ttf:text=DOG:fontsize=24:x=10:y=20+24-max_glyph_a,
          drawtext=fontfile=FreeSans.ttf:text=cow:fontsize=24:x=80:y=20+24-max_glyph_a
  .Ve

For more information about libfreetype, check:
&lt;**http://www.freetype.org/**&gt;.

For more information about fontconfig, check:
&lt;**http://freedesktop.org/software/fontconfig/fontconfig-user.html**&gt;.

For more information about libfribidi, check:
&lt;**http://fribidi.org/**&gt;.

<a name="edgedetect"></a>

### edgedetect

.IX Subsection "edgedetect"
Detect and draw edges. The filter uses the Canny Edge Detection algorithm.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **low**  
  .IX Item "low"
* **high**  
  .IX Item "high"
  Set low and high threshold values used by the Canny thresholding
  algorithm.
  .Sp
  The high threshold selects the strong\*(R" edge pixels, which are then
  connected through 8-connectivity with the weak\*(R" edge pixels selected
  by the low threshold.
  .Sp
  _low_ and _high_ threshold values must be chosen in the range
  [0,1], and _low_ should be lesser or equal to _high_.
  .Sp
  Default value for _low_ is \f(CW`20/255\*(C', and default value for _high_
  is \f(CW`50/255\*(C'.
* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Define the drawing mode.
    * **wires**  
      .IX Item "wires"
      Draw white/gray wires on black background.
    * **colormix**  
      .IX Item "colormix"
      Mix the colors to create a paint/cartoon effect.
    * **canny**  
      .IX Item "canny"
      Apply Canny edge detector on all selected planes.
      .Sp
      Default value is _wires_.
* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Select planes for filtering. By default all available planes are filtered.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Standard edge detection with custom values for the hysteresis thresholding:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          edgedetect=low=0.1:high=0.4
  .Ve
* ·  
  Painting effect without thresholding:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          edgedetect=mode=colormix:high=0
  .Ve

<a name="eq"></a>

### eq

.IX Subsection "eq"
Set brightness, contrast, saturation and approximate gamma adjustment.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **contrast**  
  .IX Item "contrast"
  Set the contrast expression. The value must be a float value in range
  \f(CW`-2.0\*(C' to \f(CW2.0. The default value is \*(L"1\*(R".
* **brightness**  
  .IX Item "brightness"
  Set the brightness expression. The value must be a float value in
  range \f(CW`-1.0\*(C' to \f(CW1.0. The default value is \*(L"0\*(R".
* **saturation**  
  .IX Item "saturation"
  Set the saturation expression. The value must be a float in
  range \f(CW0.0 to \f(CW3.0. The default value is 1\*(R".
* **gamma**  
  .IX Item "gamma"
  Set the gamma expression. The value must be a float in range
  \f(CW0.1 to \f(CW10.0.  The default value is 1\*(R".
* **gamma\_r**  
  .IX Item "gamma_r"
  Set the gamma expression for red. The value must be a float in
  range \f(CW0.1 to \f(CW10.0. The default value is 1\*(R".
* **gamma\_g**  
  .IX Item "gamma_g"
  Set the gamma expression for green. The value must be a float in range
  \f(CW0.1 to \f(CW10.0. The default value is 1\*(R".
* **gamma\_b**  
  .IX Item "gamma_b"
  Set the gamma expression for blue. The value must be a float in range
  \f(CW0.1 to \f(CW10.0. The default value is 1\*(R".
* **gamma\_weight**  
  .IX Item "gamma_weight"
  Set the gamma weight expression. It can be used to reduce the effect
  of a high gamma value on bright image areas, e.g. keep them from
  getting overamplified and just plain white. The value must be a float
  in range \f(CW0.0 to \f(CW1.0. A value of \f(CW0.0 turns the
  gamma correction all the way down while \f(CW1.0 leaves it at its
  full strength. Default is 1\*(R".
* **eval**  
  .IX Item "eval"
  Set when the expressions for brightness, contrast, saturation and
  gamma expressions are evaluated.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **init**  
      .IX Item "init"
      only evaluate expressions once during the filter initialization or
      when a command is processed
    * **frame**  
      .IX Item "frame"
      evaluate expressions for each incoming frame
      .Sp
      Default value is **init**.

The expressions accept the following parameters:

* **n**  
  .IX Item "n"
  frame count of the input frame starting from 0
* **pos**  
  .IX Item "pos"
  byte position of the corresponding packet in the input file, \s-1NAN\s0 if
  unspecified
* **r**  
  .IX Item "r"
  frame rate of the input video, \s-1NAN\s0 if the input frame rate is unknown
* **t**  
  .IX Item "t"
  timestamp expressed in seconds, \s-1NAN\s0 if the input timestamp is unknown

_Commands_
.IX Subsection "Commands"

The filter supports the following commands:

* **contrast**  
  .IX Item "contrast"
  Set the contrast expression.
* **brightness**  
  .IX Item "brightness"
  Set the brightness expression.
* **saturation**  
  .IX Item "saturation"
  Set the saturation expression.
* **gamma**  
  .IX Item "gamma"
  Set the gamma expression.
* **gamma\_r**  
  .IX Item "gamma_r"
  Set the gamma_r expression.
* **gamma\_g**  
  .IX Item "gamma_g"
  Set gamma_g expression.
* **gamma\_b**  
  .IX Item "gamma_b"
  Set gamma_b expression.
* **gamma\_weight**  
  .IX Item "gamma_weight"
  Set gamma_weight expression.
  .Sp
  The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option.
  .Sp
  If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current
  value.

<a name="erosion"></a>

### erosion

.IX Subsection "erosion"
Apply erosion effect to the video.

This filter replaces the pixel by the local(3x3) minimum.

It accepts the following options:

* **threshold0**  
  .IX Item "threshold0"
* **threshold1**  
  .IX Item "threshold1"
* **threshold2**  
  .IX Item "threshold2"
* **threshold3**  
  .IX Item "threshold3"
  Limit the maximum change for each plane, default is 65535.
  If 0, plane will remain unchanged.
* **coordinates**  
  .IX Item "coordinates"
  Flag which specifies the pixel to refer to. Default is 255 i.e. all eight
  pixels are used.
  .Sp
  Flags to local 3x3 coordinates maps like this:
  .Sp
  .Vb 3
      1 2 3
      4   5
      6 7 8
  .Ve

<a name="extractplanes"></a>

### extractplanes

.IX Subsection "extractplanes"
Extract color channel components from input video stream into
separate grayscale video streams.

The filter accepts the following option:

* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Set plane(s) to extract.
  .Sp
  Available values for planes are:
    * **y**  
      .IX Item "y"
    * **u**  
      .IX Item "u"
    * **v**  
      .IX Item "v"
    * **a**  
      .IX Item "a"
    * **r**  
      .IX Item "r"
    * **g**  
      .IX Item "g"
    * **b**  
      .IX Item "b"
      .Sp
      Choosing planes not available in the input will result in an error.
      That means you cannot select \f(CW`r\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`g\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`b\*(C' planes
      with \f(CW`y\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`u\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`v\*(C' planes at same time.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Extract luma, u and v color channel component from input video frame
  into 3 grayscale outputs:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i video.avi -filter_complex extractplanes=y+u+v[y][u][v]\*(Aq -map \*(Aq[y]\*(Aq y.avi -map \*(Aq[u]\*(Aq u.avi -map \*(Aq[v]\*(Aq v.avi
  .Ve

<a name="elbg"></a>

### elbg

.IX Subsection "elbg"
Apply a posterize effect using the \s-1ELBG\s0 (Enhanced \s-1LBG\s0) algorithm.

For each input image, the filter will compute the optimal mapping from
the input to the output given the codebook length, that is the number
of distinct output colors.

This filter accepts the following options.

* **codebook_length, l**  
  .IX Item "codebook_length, l"
  Set codebook length. The value must be a positive integer, and
  represents the number of distinct output colors. Default value is 256.
* **nb_steps, n**  
  .IX Item "nb_steps, n"
  Set the maximum number of iterations to apply for computing the optimal
  mapping. The higher the value the better the result and the higher the
  computation time. Default value is 1.
* **seed, s**  
  .IX Item "seed, s"
  Set a random seed, must be an integer included between 0 and
  \s-1UINT32_MAX.\s0 If not specified, or if explicitly set to -1, the filter
  will try to use a good random seed on a best effort basis.
* **pal8**  
  .IX Item "pal8"
  Set pal8 output pixel format. This option does not work with codebook
  length greater than 256.

<a name="entropy"></a>

### entropy

.IX Subsection "entropy"
Measure graylevel entropy in histogram of color channels of video frames.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Can be either _normal_ or _diff_. Default is _normal_.
  .Sp
  _diff_ mode measures entropy of histogram delta values, absolute differences
  between neighbour histogram values.

<a name="fade"></a>

### fade

.IX Subsection "fade"
Apply a fade-in/out effect to the input video.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **type, t**  
  .IX Item "type, t"
  The effect type can be either in\*(R" for a fade-in, or \*(L"out\*(R" for a fade-out
  effect.
  Default is \f(CW`in\*(C'.
* **start_frame, s**  
  .IX Item "start_frame, s"
  Specify the number of the frame to start applying the fade
  effect at. Default is 0.
* **nb_frames, n**  
  .IX Item "nb_frames, n"
  The number of frames that the fade effect lasts. At the end of the
  fade-in effect, the output video will have the same intensity as the input video.
  At the end of the fade-out transition, the output video will be filled with the
  selected **color**.
  Default is 25.
* **alpha**  
  .IX Item "alpha"
  If set to 1, fade only alpha channel, if one exists on the input.
  Default value is 0.
* **start_time, st**  
  .IX Item "start_time, st"
  Specify the timestamp (in seconds) of the frame to start to apply the fade
  effect. If both start_frame and start_time are specified, the fade will start at
  whichever comes last.  Default is 0.
* **duration, d**  
  .IX Item "duration, d"
  The number of seconds for which the fade effect has to last. At the end of the
  fade-in effect the output video will have the same intensity as the input video,
  at the end of the fade-out transition the output video will be filled with the
  selected **color**.
  If both duration and nb_frames are specified, duration is used. Default is 0
  (nb_frames is used by default).
* **color, c**  
  .IX Item "color, c"
  Specify the color of the fade. Default is black\*(R".

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Fade in the first 30 frames of video:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fade=in:0:30
  .Ve
  .Sp
  The command above is equivalent to:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fade=t=in:s=0:n=30
  .Ve
* ·  
  Fade out the last 45 frames of a 200-frame video:
  .Sp
  .Vb 2
          fade=out:155:45
          fade=type=out:start_frame=155:nb_frames=45
  .Ve
* ·  
  Fade in the first 25 frames and fade out the last 25 frames of a 1000-frame video:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fade=in:0:25, fade=out:975:25
  .Ve
* ·  
  Make the first 5 frames yellow, then fade in from frame 5-24:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fade=in:5:20:color=yellow
  .Ve
* ·  
  Fade in alpha over first 25 frames of video:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fade=in:0:25:alpha=1
  .Ve
* ·  
  Make the first 5.5 seconds black, then fade in for 0.5 seconds:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fade=t=in:st=5.5:d=0.5
  .Ve

<a name="fftfilt"></a>

### fftfilt

.IX Subsection "fftfilt"
Apply arbitrary expressions to samples in frequency domain

* **dc\_Y**  
  .IX Item "dc_Y"
  Adjust the dc value (gain) of the luma plane of the image. The filter
  accepts an integer value in range \f(CW0 to \f(CW1000. The default
  value is set to \f(CW0.
* **dc\_U**  
  .IX Item "dc_U"
  Adjust the dc value (gain) of the 1st chroma plane of the image. The
  filter accepts an integer value in range \f(CW0 to \f(CW1000. The
  default value is set to \f(CW0.
* **dc\_V**  
  .IX Item "dc_V"
  Adjust the dc value (gain) of the 2nd chroma plane of the image. The
  filter accepts an integer value in range \f(CW0 to \f(CW1000. The
  default value is set to \f(CW0.
* **weight\_Y**  
  .IX Item "weight_Y"
  Set the frequency domain weight expression for the luma plane.
* **weight\_U**  
  .IX Item "weight_U"
  Set the frequency domain weight expression for the 1st chroma plane.
* **weight\_V**  
  .IX Item "weight_V"
  Set the frequency domain weight expression for the 2nd chroma plane.
* **eval**  
  .IX Item "eval"
  Set when the expressions are evaluated.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **init**  
      .IX Item "init"
      Only evaluate expressions once during the filter initialization.
    * **frame**  
      .IX Item "frame"
      Evaluate expressions for each incoming frame.
      .Sp
      Default value is **init**.
      .Sp
      The filter accepts the following variables:
* **X**  
  .IX Item "X"
* **Y**  
  .IX Item "Y"
  The coordinates of the current sample.
* **W**  
  .IX Item "W"
* **H**  
  .IX Item "H"
  The width and height of the image.
* **N**  
  .IX Item "N"
  The number of input frame, starting from 0.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  High-pass:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fftfilt=dc_Y=128:weight_Y=squish(1-(Y+X)/100)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Low-pass:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fftfilt=dc_Y=0:weight_Y=squish((Y+X)/100-1)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Sharpen:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fftfilt=dc_Y=0:weight_Y=1+squish(1-(Y+X)/100)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Blur:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fftfilt=dc_Y=0:weight_Y=exp(-4 * ((Y+X)/(W+H)))\*(Aq
  .Ve

<a name="fftdnoiz"></a>

### fftdnoiz

.IX Subsection "fftdnoiz"
Denoise frames using 3D \s-1FFT\s0 (frequency domain filtering).

The filter accepts the following options:

* **sigma**  
  .IX Item "sigma"
  Set the noise sigma constant. This sets denoising strength.
  Default value is 1. Allowed range is from 0 to 30.
  Using very high sigma with low overlap may give blocking artifacts.
* **amount**  
  .IX Item "amount"
  Set amount of denoising. By default all detected noise is reduced.
  Default value is 1. Allowed range is from 0 to 1.
* **block**  
  .IX Item "block"
  Set size of block, Default is 4, can be 3, 4, 5 or 6.
  Actual size of block in pixels is 2 to power of _block_, so by default
  block size in pixels is 2^4 which is 16.
* **overlap**  
  .IX Item "overlap"
  Set block overlap. Default is 0.5. Allowed range is from 0.2 to 0.8.
* **prev**  
  .IX Item "prev"
  Set number of previous frames to use for denoising. By default is set to 0.
* **next**  
  .IX Item "next"
  Set number of next frames to to use for denoising. By default is set to 0.
* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Set planes which will be filtered, by default are all available filtered
  except alpha.

<a name="field"></a>

### field

.IX Subsection "field"
Extract a single field from an interlaced image using stride
arithmetic to avoid wasting \s-1CPU\s0 time. The output frames are marked as
non-interlaced.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **type**  
  .IX Item "type"
  Specify whether to extract the top (if the value is \f(CW0 or
  \f(CW`top\*(C') or the bottom field (if the value is \f(CW1 or
  \f(CW`bottom\*(C').

<a name="fieldhint"></a>

### fieldhint

.IX Subsection "fieldhint"
Create new frames by copying the top and bottom fields from surrounding frames
supplied as numbers by the hint file.

* **hint**  
  .IX Item "hint"
  Set file containing hints: absolute/relative frame numbers.
  .Sp
  There must be one line for each frame in a clip. Each line must contain two
  numbers separated by the comma, optionally followed by \f(CW`-\*(C' or \f(CW\*(C\`+\*(C'.
  Numbers supplied on each line of file can not be out of [N-1,N+1] where N
  is current frame number for \f(CW`absolute\*(C' mode or out of [-1, 1] range
  for \f(CW`relative\*(C' mode. First number tells from which frame to pick up top
  field and second number tells from which frame to pick up bottom field.
  .Sp
  If optionally followed by \f(CW`+\*(C' output frame will be marked as interlaced,
  else if followed by \f(CW`-\*(C' output frame will be marked as progressive, else
  it will be marked same as input frame.
  If line starts with \f(CW`#\*(C' or \f(CW\*(C\`;\*(C' that line is skipped.
* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Can be item \f(CW`absolute\*(C' or \f(CW\*(C\`relative\*(C'. Default is \f(CW\*(C\`absolute\*(C'.

Example of first several lines of \f(CW`hint\*(C' file for \f(CW\*(C\`relative\*(C' mode:

.Vb 10
        0,0 - # first frame
        1,0 - # second frame, use thirds frame top field and second\*(Aqs frame bottom field
        1,0 - # third frame, use fourths frame top field and third\*(Aqs frame bottom field
        1,0 -
        0,0 -
        0,0 -
        1,0 -
        1,0 -
        1,0 -
        0,0 -
        0,0 -
        1,0 -
        1,0 -
        1,0 -
        0,0 -
.Ve

<a name="fieldmatch"></a>

### fieldmatch

.IX Subsection "fieldmatch"
Field matching filter for inverse telecine. It is meant to reconstruct the
progressive frames from a telecined stream. The filter does not drop duplicated
frames, so to achieve a complete inverse telecine \f(CW`fieldmatch\*(C' needs to be
followed by a decimation filter such as **decimate** in the filtergraph.

The separation of the field matching and the decimation is notably motivated by
the possibility of inserting a de-interlacing filter fallback between the two.
If the source has mixed telecined and real interlaced content,
\f(CW`fieldmatch\*(C' will not be able to match fields for the interlaced parts.
But these remaining combed frames will be marked as interlaced, and thus can be
de-interlaced by a later filter such as **yadif** before decimation.

In addition to the various configuration options, \f(CW`fieldmatch\*(C' can take an
optional second stream, activated through the **ppsrc** option. If
enabled, the frames reconstruction will be based on the fields and frames from
this second stream. This allows the first input to be pre-processed in order to
help the various algorithms of the filter, while keeping the output lossless
(assuming the fields are matched properly). Typically, a field-aware denoiser,
or brightness/contrast adjustments can help.

Note that this filter uses the same algorithms as \s-1TIVTC/TFM\s0 (AviSynth project)
and \s-1VIVTC/VFM\s0 (VapourSynth project). The later is a light clone of \s-1TFM\s0 from
which \f(CW`fieldmatch\*(C' is based on. While the semantic and usage are very
close, some behaviour and options names can differ.

The **decimate** filter currently only works for constant frame rate input.
If your input has mixed telecined (30fps) and progressive content with a lower
framerate like 24fps use the following filterchain to produce the necessary cfr
stream: \f(CW`dejudder,fps=30000/1001,fieldmatch,decimate\*(C'.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **order**  
  .IX Item "order"
  Specify the assumed field order of the input stream. Available values are:
    * **auto**  
      .IX Item "auto"
      Auto detect parity (use FFmpeg's internal parity value).
    * **bff**  
      .IX Item "bff"
      Assume bottom field first.
    * **tff**  
      .IX Item "tff"
      Assume top field first.
      .Sp
      Note that it is sometimes recommended not to trust the parity announced by the
      stream.
      .Sp
      Default value is _auto_.
* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Set the matching mode or strategy to use. **pc** mode is the safest in the
  sense that it won't risk creating jerkiness due to duplicate frames when
  possible, but if there are bad edits or blended fields it will end up
  outputting combed frames when a good match might actually exist. On the other
  hand, **pcn\_ub** mode is the most risky in terms of creating jerkiness,
  but will almost always find a good frame if there is one. The other values are
  all somewhere in between **pc** and **pcn\_ub** in terms of risking
  jerkiness and creating duplicate frames versus finding good matches in sections
  with bad edits, orphaned fields, blended fields, etc.
  .Sp
  More details about p/c/n/u/b are available in **p/c/n/u/b meaning** section.
  .Sp
  Available values are:
    * **pc**  
      .IX Item "pc"
      2-way matching (p/c)
    * **pc\_n**  
      .IX Item "pc_n"
      2-way matching, and trying 3rd match if still combed (p/c + n)
    * **pc\_u**  
      .IX Item "pc_u"
      2-way matching, and trying 3rd match (same order) if still combed (p/c + u)
    * **pc\_n\_ub**  
      .IX Item "pc_n_ub"
      2-way matching, trying 3rd match if still combed, and trying 4th/5th matches if
      still combed (p/c + n + u/b)
    * **pcn**  
      .IX Item "pcn"
      3-way matching (p/c/n)
    * **pcn\_ub**  
      .IX Item "pcn_ub"
      3-way matching, and trying 4th/5th matches if all 3 of the original matches are
      detected as combed (p/c/n + u/b)
      .Sp
      The parenthesis at the end indicate the matches that would be used for that
      mode assuming **order**=_tff_ (and **field** on _auto_ or
      _top_).
      .Sp
      In terms of speed **pc** mode is by far the fastest and **pcn\_ub** is
      the slowest.
      .Sp
      Default value is _pc\_n_.
* **ppsrc**  
  .IX Item "ppsrc"
  Mark the main input stream as a pre-processed input, and enable the secondary
  input stream as the clean source to pick the fields from. See the filter
  introduction for more details. It is similar to the **clip2** feature from
  \s-1VFM/TFM.\s0
  .Sp
  Default value is \f(CW0 (disabled).
* **field**  
  .IX Item "field"
  Set the field to match from. It is recommended to set this to the same value as
  **order** unless you experience matching failures with that setting. In
  certain circumstances changing the field that is used to match from can have a
  large impact on matching performance. Available values are:
    * **auto**  
      .IX Item "auto"
      Automatic (same value as **order**).
    * **bottom**  
      .IX Item "bottom"
      Match from the bottom field.
    * **top**  
      .IX Item "top"
      Match from the top field.
      .Sp
      Default value is _auto_.
* **mchroma**  
  .IX Item "mchroma"
  Set whether or not chroma is included during the match comparisons. In most
  cases it is recommended to leave this enabled. You should set this to \f(CW0
  only if your clip has bad chroma problems such as heavy rainbowing or other
  artifacts. Setting this to \f(CW0 could also be used to speed things up at
  the cost of some accuracy.
  .Sp
  Default value is \f(CW1.
* **y0**  
  .IX Item "y0"
* **y1**  
  .IX Item "y1"
  These define an exclusion band which excludes the lines between **y0** and
  **y1** from being included in the field matching decision. An exclusion
  band can be used to ignore subtitles, a logo, or other things that may
  interfere with the matching. **y0** sets the starting scan line and
  **y1** sets the ending line; all lines in between **y0** and
  **y1** (including **y0** and **y1**) will be ignored. Setting
  **y0** and **y1** to the same value will disable the feature.
  **y0** and **y1** defaults to \f(CW0.
* **scthresh**  
  .IX Item "scthresh"
  Set the scene change detection threshold as a percentage of maximum change on
  the luma plane. Good values are in the \f(CW`[8.0, 14.0]\*(C' range. Scene change
  detection is only relevant in case **combmatch**=_sc_.  The range for
  **scthresh** is \f(CW`[0.0, 100.0]\*(C'.
  .Sp
  Default value is \f(CW12.0.
* **combmatch**  
  .IX Item "combmatch"
  When **combatch** is not _none_, \f(CW`fieldmatch\*(C' will take into
  account the combed scores of matches when deciding what match to use as the
  final match. Available values are:
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      No final matching based on combed scores.
    * **sc**  
      .IX Item "sc"
      Combed scores are only used when a scene change is detected.
    * **full**  
      .IX Item "full"
      Use combed scores all the time.
      .Sp
      Default is _sc_.
* **combdbg**  
  .IX Item "combdbg"
  Force \f(CW`fieldmatch\*(C' to calculate the combed metrics for certain matches and
  print them. This setting is known as **micout** in \s-1TFM/VFM\s0 vocabulary.
  Available values are:
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      No forced calculation.
    * **pcn**  
      .IX Item "pcn"
      Force p/c/n calculations.
    * **pcnub**  
      .IX Item "pcnub"
      Force p/c/n/u/b calculations.
      .Sp
      Default value is _none_.
* **cthresh**  
  .IX Item "cthresh"
  This is the area combing threshold used for combed frame detection. This
  essentially controls how strong\*(R" or \*(L"visible\*(R" combing must be to be detected.
  Larger values mean combing must be more visible and smaller values mean combing
  can be less visible or strong and still be detected. Valid settings are from
  \f(CW`-1\*(C' (every pixel will be detected as combed) to \f(CW255 (no pixel will
  be detected as combed). This is basically a pixel difference value. A good
  range is \f(CW`[8, 12]\*(C'.
  .Sp
  Default value is \f(CW9.
* **chroma**  
  .IX Item "chroma"
  Sets whether or not chroma is considered in the combed frame decision.  Only
  disable this if your source has chroma problems (rainbowing, etc.) that are
  causing problems for the combed frame detection with chroma enabled. Actually,
  using **chroma**=_0_ is usually more reliable, except for the case
  where there is chroma only combing in the source.
  .Sp
  Default value is \f(CW0.
* **blockx**  
  .IX Item "blockx"
* **blocky**  
  .IX Item "blocky"
  Respectively set the x-axis and y-axis size of the window used during combed
  frame detection. This has to do with the size of the area in which
  **combpel** pixels are required to be detected as combed for a frame to be
  declared combed. See the **combpel** parameter description for more info.
  Possible values are any number that is a power of 2 starting at 4 and going up
  to 512.
  .Sp
  Default value is \f(CW16.
* **combpel**  
  .IX Item "combpel"
  The number of combed pixels inside any of the **blocky** by
  **blockx** size blocks on the frame for the frame to be detected as
  combed. While **cthresh** controls how visible\*(R" the combing must be, this
  setting controls how much\*(R" combing there must be in any localized area (a
  window defined by the **blockx** and **blocky** settings) on the
  frame. Minimum value is \f(CW0 and maximum is \f(CW`blocky x blockx\*(C' (at
  which point no frames will ever be detected as combed). This setting is known
  as **\s-1MI\s0** in \s-1TFM/VFM\s0 vocabulary.
  .Sp
  Default value is \f(CW80.

_p/c/n/u/b meaning_
.IX Subsection "p/c/n/u/b meaning"

p/c/n
.IX Subsection "p/c/n"

We assume the following telecined stream:

.Vb 2
        Top fields:     1 2 2 3 4
        Bottom fields:  1 2 3 4 4
.Ve

The numbers correspond to the progressive frame the fields relate to. Here, the
first two frames are progressive, the 3rd and 4th are combed, and so on.

When \f(CW`fieldmatch\*(C' is configured to run a matching from bottom
(**field**=_bottom_) this is how this input stream get transformed:

.Vb 3
        Input stream:
                        T     1 2 2 3 4
                        B     1 2 3 4 4   &lt;-- matching reference
        
        Matches:              c c n n c
        
        Output stream:
                        T     1 2 3 4 4
                        B     1 2 3 4 4
.Ve

As a result of the field matching, we can see that some frames get duplicated.
To perform a complete inverse telecine, you need to rely on a decimation filter
after this operation. See for instance the **decimate** filter.

The same operation now matching from top fields (**field**=_top_)
looks like this:

.Vb 3
        Input stream:
                        T     1 2 2 3 4   &lt;-- matching reference
                        B     1 2 3 4 4
        
        Matches:              c c p p c
        
        Output stream:
                        T     1 2 2 3 4
                        B     1 2 2 3 4
.Ve

In these examples, we can see what _p_, _c_ and _n_ mean;
basically, they refer to the frame and field of the opposite parity:

* *&lt;_p_ matches the field of the opposite parity in the previous frame&gt;  
  .IX Item "*&lt;p matches the field of the opposite parity in the previous frame&gt;"
* *&lt;_c_ matches the field of the opposite parity in the current frame&gt;  
  .IX Item "*&lt;c matches the field of the opposite parity in the current frame&gt;"
* *&lt;_n_ matches the field of the opposite parity in the next frame&gt;  
  .IX Item "*&lt;n matches the field of the opposite parity in the next frame&gt;"

u/b
.IX Subsection "u/b"

The _u_ and _b_ matching are a bit special in the sense that they match
from the opposite parity flag. In the following examples, we assume that we are
currently matching the 2nd frame (Top:2, bottom:2). According to the match, a
'x' is placed above and below each matched fields.

With bottom matching (**field**=_bottom_):

.Vb 1
        Match:           c         p           n          b          u
        
                         x       x               x        x          x
          Top          1 2 2     1 2 2       1 2 2      1 2 2      1 2 2
          Bottom       1 2 3     1 2 3       1 2 3      1 2 3      1 2 3
                         x         x           x        x              x
        
        Output frames:
                         2          1          2          2          2
                         2          2          2          1          3
.Ve

With top matching (**field**=_top_):

.Vb 1
        Match:           c         p           n          b          u
        
                         x         x           x        x              x
          Top          1 2 2     1 2 2       1 2 2      1 2 2      1 2 2
          Bottom       1 2 3     1 2 3       1 2 3      1 2 3      1 2 3
                         x       x               x        x          x
        
        Output frames:
                         2          2          2          1          2
                         2          1          3          2          2
.Ve

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

Simple \s-1IVTC\s0 of a top field first telecined stream:

.Vb 1
        fieldmatch=order=tff:combmatch=none, decimate
.Ve

Advanced \s-1IVTC,\s0 with fallback on **yadif** for still combed frames:

.Vb 1
        fieldmatch=order=tff:combmatch=full, yadif=deint=interlaced, decimate
.Ve

<a name="fieldorder"></a>

### fieldorder

.IX Subsection "fieldorder"
Transform the field order of the input video.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **order**  
  .IX Item "order"
  The output field order. Valid values are _tff_ for top field first or _bff_
  for bottom field first.

The default value is **tff**.

The transformation is done by shifting the picture content up or down
by one line, and filling the remaining line with appropriate picture content.
This method is consistent with most broadcast field order converters.

If the input video is not flagged as being interlaced, or it is already
flagged as being of the required output field order, then this filter does
not alter the incoming video.

It is very useful when converting to or from \s-1PAL DV\s0 material,
which is bottom field first.

For example:

.Vb 1
        ffmpeg -i in.vob -vf "fieldorder=bff" out.dv
.Ve

<a name="fifo-afifo"></a>

### fifo, afifo

.IX Subsection "fifo, afifo"
Buffer input images and send them when they are requested.

It is mainly useful when auto-inserted by the libavfilter
framework.

It does not take parameters.

<a name="fillborders"></a>

### fillborders

.IX Subsection "fillborders"
Fill borders of the input video, without changing video stream dimensions.
Sometimes video can have garbage at the four edges and you may not want to
crop video input to keep size multiple of some number.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **left**  
  .IX Item "left"
  Number of pixels to fill from left border.
* **right**  
  .IX Item "right"
  Number of pixels to fill from right border.
* **top**  
  .IX Item "top"
  Number of pixels to fill from top border.
* **bottom**  
  .IX Item "bottom"
  Number of pixels to fill from bottom border.
* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Set fill mode.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **smear**  
      .IX Item "smear"
      fill pixels using outermost pixels
    * **mirror**  
      .IX Item "mirror"
      fill pixels using mirroring
    * **fixed**  
      .IX Item "fixed"
      fill pixels with constant value
      .Sp
      Default is _smear_.
* **color**  
  .IX Item "color"
  Set color for pixels in fixed mode. Default is _black_.

<a name="find_rect"></a>

### find_rect

.IX Subsection "find_rect"
Find a rectangular object

It accepts the following options:

* **object**  
  .IX Item "object"
  Filepath of the object image, needs to be in gray8.
* **threshold**  
  .IX Item "threshold"
  Detection threshold, default is 0.5.
* **mipmaps**  
  .IX Item "mipmaps"
  Number of mipmaps, default is 3.
* **xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax**  
  .IX Item "xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax"
  Specifies the rectangle in which to search.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Generate a representative palette of a given video using **ffmpeg**:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i file.ts -vf find_rect=newref.pgm,cover_rect=cover.jpg:mode=cover new.mkv
  .Ve

<a name="cover_rect"></a>

### cover_rect

.IX Subsection "cover_rect"
Cover a rectangular object

It accepts the following options:

* **cover**  
  .IX Item "cover"
  Filepath of the optional cover image, needs to be in yuv420.
* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Set covering mode.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **cover**  
      .IX Item "cover"
      cover it by the supplied image
    * **blur**  
      .IX Item "blur"
      cover it by interpolating the surrounding pixels
      .Sp
      Default value is _blur_.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Generate a representative palette of a given video using **ffmpeg**:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i file.ts -vf find_rect=newref.pgm,cover_rect=cover.jpg:mode=cover new.mkv
  .Ve

<a name="floodfill"></a>

### floodfill

.IX Subsection "floodfill"
Flood area with values of same pixel components with another values.

It accepts the following options:

* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
  Set pixel x coordinate.
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  Set pixel y coordinate.
* **s0**  
  .IX Item "s0"
  Set source #0 component value.
* **s1**  
  .IX Item "s1"
  Set source #1 component value.
* **s2**  
  .IX Item "s2"
  Set source #2 component value.
* **s3**  
  .IX Item "s3"
  Set source #3 component value.
* **d0**  
  .IX Item "d0"
  Set destination #0 component value.
* **d1**  
  .IX Item "d1"
  Set destination #1 component value.
* **d2**  
  .IX Item "d2"
  Set destination #2 component value.
* **d3**  
  .IX Item "d3"
  Set destination #3 component value.

<a name="format"></a>

### format

.IX Subsection "format"
Convert the input video to one of the specified pixel formats.
Libavfilter will try to pick one that is suitable as input to
the next filter.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **pix\_fmts**  
  .IX Item "pix_fmts"
  A '|'-separated list of pixel format names, such as
  pix_fmts=yuv420p|monow|rgb24\*(R".

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Convert the input video to the _yuv420p_ format
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          format=pix_fmts=yuv420p
  .Ve
  .Sp
  Convert the input video to any of the formats in the list
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          format=pix_fmts=yuv420p|yuv444p|yuv410p
  .Ve

<a name="fps"></a>

### fps

.IX Subsection "fps"
Convert the video to specified constant frame rate by duplicating or dropping
frames as necessary.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **fps**  
  .IX Item "fps"
  The desired output frame rate. The default is \f(CW25.
* **start\_time**  
  .IX Item "start_time"
  Assume the first \s-1PTS\s0 should be the given value, in seconds. This allows for
  padding/trimming at the start of stream. By default, no assumption is made
  about the first frame's expected \s-1PTS,\s0 so no padding or trimming is done.
  For example, this could be set to 0 to pad the beginning with duplicates of
  the first frame if a video stream starts after the audio stream or to trim any
  frames with a negative \s-1PTS.\s0
* **round**  
  .IX Item "round"
  Timestamp (\s-1PTS\s0) rounding method.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * **zero**  
      .IX Item "zero"
      round towards 0
    * **inf**  
      .IX Item "inf"
      round away from 0
    * **down**  
      .IX Item "down"
      round towards -infinity
    * **up**  
      .IX Item "up"
      round towards +infinity
    * **near**  
      .IX Item "near"
      round to nearest
      .Sp
      The default is \f(CW`near\*(C'.
* **eof\_action**  
  .IX Item "eof_action"
  Action performed when reading the last frame.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * **round**  
      .IX Item "round"
      Use same timestamp rounding method as used for other frames.
    * **pass**  
      .IX Item "pass"
      Pass through last frame if input duration has not been reached yet.
      .Sp
      The default is \f(CW`round\*(C'.

Alternatively, the options can be specified as a flat string:
_fps_[:_start\_time_[:_round_]].

See also the **setpts** filter.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  A typical usage in order to set the fps to 25:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fps=fps=25
  .Ve
* ·  
  Sets the fps to 24, using abbreviation and rounding method to round to nearest:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          fps=fps=film:round=near
  .Ve

<a name="framepack"></a>

### framepack

.IX Subsection "framepack"
Pack two different video streams into a stereoscopic video, setting proper
metadata on supported codecs. The two views should have the same size and
framerate and processing will stop when the shorter video ends. Please note
that you may conveniently adjust view properties with the **scale** and
**fps** filters.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **format**  
  .IX Item "format"
  The desired packing format. Supported values are:
    * **sbs**  
      .IX Item "sbs"
      The views are next to each other (default).
    * **tab**  
      .IX Item "tab"
      The views are on top of each other.
    * **lines**  
      .IX Item "lines"
      The views are packed by line.
    * **columns**  
      .IX Item "columns"
      The views are packed by column.
    * **frameseq**  
      .IX Item "frameseq"
      The views are temporally interleaved.

Some examples:

.Vb 2
        # Convert left and right views into a frame-sequential video
        ffmpeg -i LEFT -i RIGHT -filter_complex framepack=frameseq OUTPUT
        
        # Convert views into a side-by-side video with the same output resolution as the input
        ffmpeg -i LEFT -i RIGHT -filter_complex [0:v]scale=w=iw/2[left],[1:v]scale=w=iw/2[right],[left][right]framepack=sbs OUTPUT
.Ve

<a name="framerate"></a>

### framerate

.IX Subsection "framerate"
Change the frame rate by interpolating new video output frames from the source
frames.

This filter is not designed to function correctly with interlaced media. If
you wish to change the frame rate of interlaced media then you are required
to deinterlace before this filter and re-interlace after this filter.

A description of the accepted options follows.

* **fps**  
  .IX Item "fps"
  Specify the output frames per second. This option can also be specified
  as a value alone. The default is \f(CW50.
* **interp\_start**  
  .IX Item "interp_start"
  Specify the start of a range where the output frame will be created as a
  linear interpolation of two frames. The range is [\f(CW0-\f(CW255],
  the default is \f(CW15.
* **interp\_end**  
  .IX Item "interp_end"
  Specify the end of a range where the output frame will be created as a
  linear interpolation of two frames. The range is [\f(CW0-\f(CW255],
  the default is \f(CW240.
* **scene**  
  .IX Item "scene"
  Specify the level at which a scene change is detected as a value between
  0 and 100 to indicate a new scene; a low value reflects a low
  probability for the current frame to introduce a new scene, while a higher
  value means the current frame is more likely to be one.
  The default is \f(CW8.2.
* **flags**  
  .IX Item "flags"
  Specify flags influencing the filter process.
  .Sp
  Available value for _flags_ is:
    * **scene_change_detect, scd**  
      .IX Item "scene_change_detect, scd"
      Enable scene change detection using the value of the option _scene_.
      This flag is enabled by default.

<a name="framestep"></a>

### framestep

.IX Subsection "framestep"
Select one frame every N-th frame.

This filter accepts the following option:

* **step**  
  .IX Item "step"
  Select frame after every \f(CW`step\*(C' frames.
  Allowed values are positive integers higher than 0. Default value is \f(CW1.

<a name="frei0r"></a>

### frei0r

.IX Subsection "frei0r"
Apply a frei0r effect to the input video.

To enable the compilation of this filter, you need to install the frei0r
header and configure FFmpeg with \f(CW`--enable-frei0r\*(C'.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **filter\_name**  
  .IX Item "filter_name"
  The name of the frei0r effect to load. If the environment variable
  **\s-1FREI0R\_PATH\s0** is defined, the frei0r effect is searched for in each of the
  directories specified by the colon-separated list in **\s-1FREI0R\_PATH\s0**.
  Otherwise, the standard frei0r paths are searched, in this order:
  _\s-1HOME/\s0.frei0r-1/lib/_, _/usr/local/lib/frei0r-1/_,
  _/usr/lib/frei0r-1/_.
* **filter\_params**  
  .IX Item "filter_params"
  A '|'-separated list of parameters to pass to the frei0r effect.

A frei0r effect parameter can be a boolean (its value is either
y\*(R" or \*(L"n\*(R"), a double, a color (specified as
_R_/_G_/_B_, where _R_, _G_, and _B_ are floating point
numbers between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive) or a color description as specified in the
**Color\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**,
a position (specified as _X_/_Y_, where
_X_ and _Y_ are floating point numbers) and/or a string.

The number and types of parameters depend on the loaded effect. If an
effect parameter is not specified, the default value is set.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Apply the distort0r effect, setting the first two double parameters:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          frei0r=filter_name=distort0r:filter_params=0.5|0.01
  .Ve
* ·  
  Apply the colordistance effect, taking a color as the first parameter:
  .Sp
  .Vb 3
          frei0r=colordistance:0.2/0.3/0.4
          frei0r=colordistance:violet
          frei0r=colordistance:0x112233
  .Ve
* ·  
  Apply the perspective effect, specifying the top left and top right image
  positions:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          frei0r=perspective:0.2/0.2|0.8/0.2
  .Ve

For more information, see
&lt;**http://frei0r.dyne.org**&gt;

<a name="fspp"></a>

### fspp

.IX Subsection "fspp"
Apply fast and simple postprocessing. It is a faster version of **spp**.

It splits (I)DCT into horizontal/vertical passes. Unlike the simple post-
processing filter, one of them is performed once per block, not per pixel.
This allows for much higher speed.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **quality**  
  .IX Item "quality"
  Set quality. This option defines the number of levels for averaging. It accepts
  an integer in the range 4-5. Default value is \f(CW4.
* **qp**  
  .IX Item "qp"
  Force a constant quantization parameter. It accepts an integer in range 0-63.
  If not set, the filter will use the \s-1QP\s0 from the video stream (if available).
* **strength**  
  .IX Item "strength"
  Set filter strength. It accepts an integer in range -15 to 32. Lower values mean
  more details but also more artifacts, while higher values make the image smoother
  but also blurrier. Default value is \f(CW0 X \s-1PSNR\s0 optimal.
* **use\_bframe\_qp**  
  .IX Item "use_bframe_qp"
  Enable the use of the \s-1QP\s0 from the B-Frames if set to \f(CW1. Using this
  option may cause flicker since the B-Frames have often larger \s-1QP.\s0 Default is
  \f(CW0 (not enabled).

<a name="gblur"></a>

### gblur

.IX Subsection "gblur"
Apply Gaussian blur filter.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **sigma**  
  .IX Item "sigma"
  Set horizontal sigma, standard deviation of Gaussian blur. Default is \f(CW0.5.
* **steps**  
  .IX Item "steps"
  Set number of steps for Gaussian approximation. Defauls is \f(CW1.
* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Set which planes to filter. By default all planes are filtered.
* **sigmaV**  
  .IX Item "sigmaV"
  Set vertical sigma, if negative it will be same as \f(CW`sigma\*(C'.
  Default is \f(CW`-1\*(C'.

<a name="geq"></a>

### geq

.IX Subsection "geq"
Apply generic equation to each pixel.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **lum_expr, lum**  
  .IX Item "lum_expr, lum"
  Set the luminance expression.
* **cb_expr, cb**  
  .IX Item "cb_expr, cb"
  Set the chrominance blue expression.
* **cr_expr, cr**  
  .IX Item "cr_expr, cr"
  Set the chrominance red expression.
* **alpha_expr, a**  
  .IX Item "alpha_expr, a"
  Set the alpha expression.
* **red_expr, r**  
  .IX Item "red_expr, r"
  Set the red expression.
* **green_expr, g**  
  .IX Item "green_expr, g"
  Set the green expression.
* **blue_expr, b**  
  .IX Item "blue_expr, b"
  Set the blue expression.

The colorspace is selected according to the specified options. If one
of the **lum\_expr**, **cb\_expr**, or **cr\_expr**
options is specified, the filter will automatically select a YCbCr
colorspace. If one of the **red\_expr**, **green\_expr**, or
**blue\_expr** options is specified, it will select an \s-1RGB\s0
colorspace.

If one of the chrominance expression is not defined, it falls back on the other
one. If no alpha expression is specified it will evaluate to opaque value.
If none of chrominance expressions are specified, they will evaluate
to the luminance expression.

The expressions can use the following variables and functions:

* **N**  
  .IX Item "N"
  The sequential number of the filtered frame, starting from \f(CW0.
* **X**  
  .IX Item "X"
* **Y**  
  .IX Item "Y"
  The coordinates of the current sample.
* **W**  
  .IX Item "W"
* **H**  
  .IX Item "H"
  The width and height of the image.
* **\s-1SW\s0**  
  .IX Item "SW"
* **\s-1SH\s0**  
  .IX Item "SH"
  Width and height scale depending on the currently filtered plane. It is the
  ratio between the corresponding luma plane number of pixels and the current
  plane ones. E.g. for \s-1YUV4:2:0\s0 the values are \f(CW`1,1\*(C' for the luma plane, and
  \f(CW`0.5,0.5\*(C' for chroma planes.
* **T**  
  .IX Item "T"
  Time of the current frame, expressed in seconds.
* **p(x, y)**  
  .IX Item "p(x, y)"
  Return the value of the pixel at location (_x_,_y_) of the current
  plane.
* **lum(x, y)**  
  .IX Item "lum(x, y)"
  Return the value of the pixel at location (_x_,_y_) of the luminance
  plane.
* **cb(x, y)**  
  .IX Item "cb(x, y)"
  Return the value of the pixel at location (_x_,_y_) of the
  blue-difference chroma plane. Return 0 if there is no such plane.
* **cr(x, y)**  
  .IX Item "cr(x, y)"
  Return the value of the pixel at location (_x_,_y_) of the
  red-difference chroma plane. Return 0 if there is no such plane.
* **r(x, y)**  
  .IX Item "r(x, y)"
* **g(x, y)**  
  .IX Item "g(x, y)"
* **b(x, y)**  
  .IX Item "b(x, y)"
  Return the value of the pixel at location (_x_,_y_) of the
  red/green/blue component. Return 0 if there is no such component.
* **alpha(x, y)**  
  .IX Item "alpha(x, y)"
  Return the value of the pixel at location (_x_,_y_) of the alpha
  plane. Return 0 if there is no such plane.

For functions, if _x_ and _y_ are outside the area, the value will be
automatically clipped to the closer edge.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Flip the image horizontally:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          geq=p(W-X\e,Y)
  .Ve
* ·  
  Generate a bidimensional sine wave, with angle \f(CW`PI/3\*(C' and a
  wavelength of 100 pixels:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          geq=128 + 100*sin(2*(PI/100)*(cos(PI/3)*(X-50*T) + sin(PI/3)*Y)):128:128
  .Ve
* ·  
  Generate a fancy enigmatic moving light:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          nullsrc=s=256x256,geq=random(1)/hypot(X-cos(N*0.07)*W/2-W/2\e,Y-sin(N*0.09)*H/2-H/2)^2*1000000*sin(N*0.02):128:128
  .Ve
* ·  
  Generate a quick emboss effect:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          format=gray,geq=lum_expr=(p(X,Y)+(256-p(X-4,Y-4)))/2\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Modify \s-1RGB\s0 components depending on pixel position:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          geq=r=X/W*r(X,Y)\*(Aq:g=\*(Aq(1-X/W)*g(X,Y)\*(Aq:b=\*(Aq(H-Y)/H*b(X,Y)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Create a radial gradient that is the same size as the input (also see
  the **vignette** filter):
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          geq=lum=255*gauss((X/W-0.5)*3)*gauss((Y/H-0.5)*3)/gauss(0)/gauss(0),format=gray
  .Ve

<a name="gradfun"></a>

### gradfun

.IX Subsection "gradfun"
Fix the banding artifacts that are sometimes introduced into nearly flat
regions by truncation to 8-bit color depth.
Interpolate the gradients that should go where the bands are, and
dither them.

It is designed for playback only.  Do not use it prior to
lossy compression, because compression tends to lose the dither and
bring back the bands.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **strength**  
  .IX Item "strength"
  The maximum amount by which the filter will change any one pixel. This is also
  the threshold for detecting nearly flat regions. Acceptable values range from
  .51 to 64; the default value is 1.2. Out-of-range values will be clipped to the
  valid range.
* **radius**  
  .IX Item "radius"
  The neighborhood to fit the gradient to. A larger radius makes for smoother
  gradients, but also prevents the filter from modifying the pixels near detailed
  regions. Acceptable values are 8-32; the default value is 16. Out-of-range
  values will be clipped to the valid range.

Alternatively, the options can be specified as a flat string:
_strength_[:_radius_]

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Apply the filter with a \f(CW3.5 strength and radius of \f(CW8:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          gradfun=3.5:8
  .Ve
* ·  
  Specify radius, omitting the strength (which will fall-back to the default
  value):
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          gradfun=radius=8
  .Ve

<a name="graphmonitor-agraphmonitor"></a>

### graphmonitor, agraphmonitor

.IX Subsection "graphmonitor, agraphmonitor"
Show various filtergraph stats.

With this filter one can debug complete filtergraph.
Especially issues with links filling with queued frames.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Set video output size. Default is _hd720_.
* **opacity, o**  
  .IX Item "opacity, o"
  Set video opacity. Default is _0.9_. Allowed range is from _0_ to _1_.
* **mode, m**  
  .IX Item "mode, m"
  Set output mode, can be _fulll_ or _compact_.
  In _compact_ mode only filters with some queued frames have displayed stats.
* **flags, f**  
  .IX Item "flags, f"
  Set flags which enable which stats are shown in video.
  .Sp
  Available values for flags are:
    * **queue**  
      .IX Item "queue"
      Display number of queued frames in each link.
    * **frame\_count\_in**  
      .IX Item "frame_count_in"
      Display number of frames taken from filter.
    * **frame\_count\_out**  
      .IX Item "frame_count_out"
      Display number of frames given out from filter.
    * **pts**  
      .IX Item "pts"
      Display current filtered frame pts.
    * **time**  
      .IX Item "time"
      Display current filtered frame time.
    * **timebase**  
      .IX Item "timebase"
      Display time base for filter link.
    * **format**  
      .IX Item "format"
      Display used format for filter link.
    * **size**  
      .IX Item "size"
      Display video size or number of audio channels in case of audio used by filter link.
    * **rate**  
      .IX Item "rate"
      Display video frame rate or sample rate in case of audio used by filter link.
* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Set upper limit for video rate of output stream, Default value is _25_.
  This guarantee that output video frame rate will not be higher than this value.

<a name="greyedge"></a>

### greyedge

.IX Subsection "greyedge"
A color constancy variation filter which estimates scene illumination via grey edge algorithm
and corrects the scene colors accordingly.

See: &lt;**https://staff.science.uva.nl/th.gevers/pub/GeversTIP07.pdf**&gt;

The filter accepts the following options:

* **difford**  
  .IX Item "difford"
  The order of differentiation to be applied on the scene. Must be chosen in the range
  [0,2] and default value is 1.
* **minknorm**  
  .IX Item "minknorm"
  The Minkowski parameter to be used for calculating the Minkowski distance. Must
  be chosen in the range [0,20] and default value is 1. Set to 0 for getting
  max value instead of calculating Minkowski distance.
* **sigma**  
  .IX Item "sigma"
  The standard deviation of Gaussian blur to be applied on the scene. Must be
  chosen in the range [0,1024.0] and default value = 1. floor( _sigma_ * **break\_off\_sigma**\|(3) )
  can't be euqal to 0 if _difford_ is greater than 0.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Grey Edge:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          greyedge=difford=1:minknorm=5:sigma=2
  .Ve
* ·  
  Max Edge:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          greyedge=difford=1:minknorm=0:sigma=2
  .Ve

<a name="haldclut"></a>

### haldclut

.IX Subsection "haldclut"
Apply a Hald \s-1CLUT\s0 to a video stream.

First input is the video stream to process, and second one is the Hald \s-1CLUT.\s0
The Hald \s-1CLUT\s0 input can be a simple picture or a complete video stream.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **shortest**  
  .IX Item "shortest"
  Force termination when the shortest input terminates. Default is \f(CW0.
* **repeatlast**  
  .IX Item "repeatlast"
  Continue applying the last \s-1CLUT\s0 after the end of the stream. A value of
  \f(CW0 disable the filter after the last frame of the \s-1CLUT\s0 is reached.
  Default is \f(CW1.

\f(CW`haldclut\*(C' also has the same interpolation options as **lut3d** (both
filters share the same internals).

More information about the Hald \s-1CLUT\s0 can be found on Eskil Steenberg's website
(Hald \s-1CLUT\s0 author) at &lt;**http://www.quelsolaar.com/technology/clut.html**&gt;.

_Workflow examples_
.IX Subsection "Workflow examples"

Hald \s-1CLUT\s0 video stream
.IX Subsection "Hald CLUT video stream"

Generate an identity Hald \s-1CLUT\s0 stream altered with various effects:

.Vb 1
        ffmpeg -f lavfi -i B&lt;haldclutsrc&gt;=8 -vf "hue=H=2*PI*t:s=sin(2*PI*t)+1, curves=cross_process" -t 10 -c:v ffv1 clut.nut
.Ve

Note: make sure you use a lossless codec.

Then use it with \f(CW`haldclut\*(C' to apply it on some random stream:

.Vb 1
        ffmpeg -f lavfi -i mandelbrot -i clut.nut -filter_complex [0][1] haldclut\*(Aq -t 20 mandelclut.mkv
.Ve

The Hald \s-1CLUT\s0 will be applied to the 10 first seconds (duration of
_clut.nut_), then the latest picture of that \s-1CLUT\s0 stream will be applied
to the remaining frames of the \f(CW`mandelbrot\*(C' stream.

Hald \s-1CLUT\s0 with preview
.IX Subsection "Hald CLUT with preview"

A Hald \s-1CLUT\s0 is supposed to be a squared image of \f(CW`Level*Level*Level\*(C' by
\f(CW`Level*Level*Level\*(C' pixels. For a given Hald \s-1CLUT,\s0 FFmpeg will select the
biggest possible square starting at the top left of the picture. The remaining
padding pixels (bottom or right) will be ignored. This area can be used to add
a preview of the Hald \s-1CLUT.\s0

Typically, the following generated Hald \s-1CLUT\s0 will be supported by the
\f(CW`haldclut\*(C' filter:

.Vb 5
        ffmpeg -f lavfi -i B&lt;haldclutsrc&gt;=8 -vf "
           pad=iw+320 [padded_clut];
           smptebars=s=320x256, split [a][b];
           [padded_clut][a] overlay=W-320:h, curves=color_negative [main];
           [main][b] overlay=W-320" -frames:v 1 clut.png
.Ve

It contains the original and a preview of the effect of the \s-1CLUT: SMPTE\s0 color
bars are displayed on the right-top, and below the same color bars processed by
the color changes.

Then, the effect of this Hald \s-1CLUT\s0 can be visualized with:

.Vb 1
        ffplay input.mkv -vf "movie=clut.png, [in] haldclut"
.Ve

<a name="hflip"></a>

### hflip

.IX Subsection "hflip"
Flip the input video horizontally.

For example, to horizontally flip the input video with **ffmpeg**:

.Vb 1
        ffmpeg -i in.avi -vf "hflip" out.avi
.Ve

<a name="histeq"></a>

### histeq

.IX Subsection "histeq"
This filter applies a global color histogram equalization on a
per-frame basis.

It can be used to correct video that has a compressed range of pixel
intensities.  The filter redistributes the pixel intensities to
equalize their distribution across the intensity range. It may be
viewed as an automatically adjusting contrast filter\*(R". This filter is
useful only for correcting degraded or poorly captured source
video.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **strength**  
  .IX Item "strength"
  Determine the amount of equalization to be applied.  As the strength
  is reduced, the distribution of pixel intensities more-and-more
  approaches that of the input frame. The value must be a float number
  in the range [0,1] and defaults to 0.200.
* **intensity**  
  .IX Item "intensity"
  Set the maximum intensity that can generated and scale the output
  values appropriately.  The strength should be set as desired and then
  the intensity can be limited if needed to avoid washing-out. The value
  must be a float number in the range [0,1] and defaults to 0.210.
* **antibanding**  
  .IX Item "antibanding"
  Set the antibanding level. If enabled the filter will randomly vary
  the luminance of output pixels by a small amount to avoid banding of
  the histogram. Possible values are \f(CW`none\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`weak\*(C' or
  \f(CW`strong\*(C'. It defaults to \f(CW\*(C\`none\*(C'.

<a name="histogram"></a>

### histogram

.IX Subsection "histogram"
Compute and draw a color distribution histogram for the input video.

The computed histogram is a representation of the color component
distribution in an image.

Standard histogram displays the color components distribution in an image.
Displays color graph for each color component. Shows distribution of
the Y, U, V, A or R, G, B components, depending on input format, in the
current frame. Below each graph a color component scale meter is shown.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **level\_height**  
  .IX Item "level_height"
  Set height of level. Default value is \f(CW200.
  Allowed range is [50, 2048].
* **scale\_height**  
  .IX Item "scale_height"
  Set height of color scale. Default value is \f(CW12.
  Allowed range is [0, 40].
* **display\_mode**  
  .IX Item "display_mode"
  Set display mode.
  It accepts the following values:
    * **stack**  
      .IX Item "stack"
      Per color component graphs are placed below each other.
    * **parade**  
      .IX Item "parade"
      Per color component graphs are placed side by side.
    * **overlay**  
      .IX Item "overlay"
      Presents information identical to that in the \f(CW`parade\*(C', except
      that the graphs representing color components are superimposed directly
      over one another.
      .Sp
      Default is \f(CW`stack\*(C'.
* **levels\_mode**  
  .IX Item "levels_mode"
  Set mode. Can be either \f(CW`linear\*(C', or \f(CW\*(C\`logarithmic\*(C'.
  Default is \f(CW`linear\*(C'.
* **components**  
  .IX Item "components"
  Set what color components to display.
  Default is \f(CW7.
* **fgopacity**  
  .IX Item "fgopacity"
  Set foreground opacity. Default is \f(CW0.7.
* **bgopacity**  
  .IX Item "bgopacity"
  Set background opacity. Default is \f(CW0.5.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Calculate and draw histogram:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffplay -i input -vf histogram
  .Ve

<a name="hqdn3d"></a>

### hqdn3d

.IX Subsection "hqdn3d"
This is a high precision/quality 3d denoise filter. It aims to reduce
image noise, producing smooth images and making still images really
still. It should enhance compressibility.

It accepts the following optional parameters:

* **luma\_spatial**  
  .IX Item "luma_spatial"
  A non-negative floating point number which specifies spatial luma strength.
  It defaults to 4.0.
* **chroma\_spatial**  
  .IX Item "chroma_spatial"
  A non-negative floating point number which specifies spatial chroma strength.
  It defaults to 3.0*_luma\_spatial_/4.0.
* **luma\_tmp**  
  .IX Item "luma_tmp"
  A floating point number which specifies luma temporal strength. It defaults to
  6.0*_luma\_spatial_/4.0.
* **chroma\_tmp**  
  .IX Item "chroma_tmp"
  A floating point number which specifies chroma temporal strength. It defaults to
  _luma\_tmp_*_chroma\_spatial_/_luma\_spatial_.

<a name="hwdownload"></a>

### hwdownload

.IX Subsection "hwdownload"
Download hardware frames to system memory.

The input must be in hardware frames, and the output a non-hardware format.
Not all formats will be supported on the output - it may be necessary to insert
an additional **format** filter immediately following in the graph to get
the output in a supported format.

<a name="hwmap"></a>

### hwmap

.IX Subsection "hwmap"
Map hardware frames to system memory or to another device.

This filter has several different modes of operation; which one is used depends
on the input and output formats:

* ·  
  Hardware frame input, normal frame output
  .Sp
  Map the input frames to system memory and pass them to the output.  If the
  original hardware frame is later required (for example, after overlaying
  something else on part of it), the **hwmap** filter can be used again
  in the next mode to retrieve it.
* ·  
  Normal frame input, hardware frame output
  .Sp
  If the input is actually a software-mapped hardware frame, then unmap it -
  that is, return the original hardware frame.
  .Sp
  Otherwise, a device must be provided.  Create new hardware surfaces on that
  device for the output, then map them back to the software format at the input
  and give those frames to the preceding filter.  This will then act like the
  **hwupload** filter, but may be able to avoid an additional copy when
  the input is already in a compatible format.
* ·  
  Hardware frame input and output
  .Sp
  A device must be supplied for the output, either directly or with the
  **derive\_device** option.  The input and output devices must be of
  different types and compatible - the exact meaning of this is
  system-dependent, but typically it means that they must refer to the same
  underlying hardware context (for example, refer to the same graphics card).
  .Sp
  If the input frames were originally created on the output device, then unmap
  to retrieve the original frames.
  .Sp
  Otherwise, map the frames to the output device - create new hardware frames
  on the output corresponding to the frames on the input.

The following additional parameters are accepted:

* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Set the frame mapping mode.  Some combination of:
    * _read_  
      .IX Item "read"
      The mapped frame should be readable.
    * _write_  
      .IX Item "write"
      The mapped frame should be writeable.
    * _overwrite_  
      .IX Item "overwrite"
      The mapping will always overwrite the entire frame.
      .Sp
      This may improve performance in some cases, as the original contents of the
      frame need not be loaded.
    * _direct_  
      .IX Item "direct"
      The mapping must not involve any copying.
      .Sp
      Indirect mappings to copies of frames are created in some cases where either
      direct mapping is not possible or it would have unexpected properties.
      Setting this flag ensures that the mapping is direct and will fail if that is
      not possible.
      .Sp
      Defaults to _read+write_ if not specified.
* **derive\_device** _type_  
  .IX Item "derive_device type"
  Rather than using the device supplied at initialisation, instead derive a new
  device of type _type_ from the device the input frames exist on.
* **reverse**  
  .IX Item "reverse"
  In a hardware to hardware mapping, map in reverse - create frames in the sink
  and map them back to the source.  This may be necessary in some cases where
  a mapping in one direction is required but only the opposite direction is
  supported by the devices being used.
  .Sp
  This option is dangerous - it may break the preceding filter in undefined
  ways if there are any additional constraints on that filter's output.
  Do not use it without fully understanding the implications of its use.

<a name="hwupload"></a>

### hwupload

.IX Subsection "hwupload"
Upload system memory frames to hardware surfaces.

The device to upload to must be supplied when the filter is initialised.  If
using ffmpeg, select the appropriate device with the **-filter\_hw\_device**
option.

<a name="hwupload_cuda"></a>

### hwupload_cuda

.IX Subsection "hwupload_cuda"
Upload system memory frames to a \s-1CUDA\s0 device.

It accepts the following optional parameters:

* **device**  
  .IX Item "device"
  The number of the \s-1CUDA\s0 device to use

<a name="hqx"></a>

### hqx

.IX Subsection "hqx"
Apply a high-quality magnification filter designed for pixel art. This filter
was originally created by Maxim Stepin.

It accepts the following option:

* **n**  
  .IX Item "n"
  Set the scaling dimension: \f(CW2 for \f(CW`hq2x\*(C', \f(CW3 for
  \f(CW`hq3x\*(C' and \f(CW4 for \f(CW\*(C\`hq4x\*(C'.
  Default is \f(CW3.

<a name="hstack"></a>

### hstack

.IX Subsection "hstack"
Stack input videos horizontally.

All streams must be of same pixel format and of same height.

Note that this filter is faster than using **overlay** and **pad** filter
to create same output.

The filter accept the following option:

* **inputs**  
  .IX Item "inputs"
  Set number of input streams. Default is 2.
* **shortest**  
  .IX Item "shortest"
  If set to 1, force the output to terminate when the shortest input
  terminates. Default value is 0.

<a name="hue"></a>

### hue

.IX Subsection "hue"
Modify the hue and/or the saturation of the input.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **h**  
  .IX Item "h"
  Specify the hue angle as a number of degrees. It accepts an expression,
  and defaults to 0\*(R".
* **s**  
  .IX Item "s"
  Specify the saturation in the [-10,10] range. It accepts an expression and
  defaults to 1\*(R".
* **H**  
  .IX Item "H"
  Specify the hue angle as a number of radians. It accepts an
  expression, and defaults to 0\*(R".
* **b**  
  .IX Item "b"
  Specify the brightness in the [-10,10] range. It accepts an expression and
  defaults to 0\*(R".

**h** and **H** are mutually exclusive, and can't be
specified at the same time.

The **b**, **h**, **H** and **s** option values are
expressions containing the following constants:

* **n**  
  .IX Item "n"
  frame count of the input frame starting from 0
* **pts**  
  .IX Item "pts"
  presentation timestamp of the input frame expressed in time base units
* **r**  
  .IX Item "r"
  frame rate of the input video, \s-1NAN\s0 if the input frame rate is unknown
* **t**  
  .IX Item "t"
  timestamp expressed in seconds, \s-1NAN\s0 if the input timestamp is unknown
* **tb**  
  .IX Item "tb"
  time base of the input video

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Set the hue to 90 degrees and the saturation to 1.0:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          hue=h=90:s=1
  .Ve
* ·  
  Same command but expressing the hue in radians:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          hue=H=PI/2:s=1
  .Ve
* ·  
  Rotate hue and make the saturation swing between 0
  and 2 over a period of 1 second:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          hue="H=2*PI*t: s=sin(2*PI*t)+1"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Apply a 3 seconds saturation fade-in effect starting at 0:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          hue="s=min(t/3\e,1)"
  .Ve
  .Sp
  The general fade-in expression can be written as:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          hue="s=min(0\e, max((t-START)/DURATION\e, 1))"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Apply a 3 seconds saturation fade-out effect starting at 5 seconds:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          hue="s=max(0\e, min(1\e, (8-t)/3))"
  .Ve
  .Sp
  The general fade-out expression can be written as:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          hue="s=max(0\e, min(1\e, (START+DURATION-t)/DURATION))"
  .Ve

_Commands_
.IX Subsection "Commands"

This filter supports the following commands:

* **b**  
  .IX Item "b"
* **s**  
  .IX Item "s"
* **h**  
  .IX Item "h"
* **H**  
  .IX Item "H"
  Modify the hue and/or the saturation and/or brightness of the input video.
  The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option.
  .Sp
  If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current
  value.

<a name="hysteresis"></a>

### hysteresis

.IX Subsection "hysteresis"
Grow first stream into second stream by connecting components.
This makes it possible to build more robust edge masks.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Set which planes will be processed as bitmap, unprocessed planes will be
  copied from first stream.
  By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.
* **threshold**  
  .IX Item "threshold"
  Set threshold which is used in filtering. If pixel component value is higher than
  this value filter algorithm for connecting components is activated.
  By default value is 0.

<a name="idet"></a>
