### idet

.IX Subsection "idet"
Detect video interlacing type.

This filter tries to detect if the input frames are interlaced, progressive,
top or bottom field first. It will also try to detect fields that are
repeated between adjacent frames (a sign of telecine).

Single frame detection considers only immediately adjacent frames when classifying each frame.
Multiple frame detection incorporates the classification history of previous frames.

The filter will log these metadata values:

* **single.current\_frame**  
  .IX Item "single.current_frame"
  Detected type of current frame using single-frame detection. One of:
  \`\`tff'' (top field first), \`\`bff'' (bottom field first),
  \`\`progressive'', or \`\`undetermined''
* **single.tff**  
  .IX Item "single.tff"
  Cumulative number of frames detected as top field first using single-frame detection.
* **multiple.tff**  
  .IX Item "multiple.tff"
  Cumulative number of frames detected as top field first using multiple-frame detection.
* **single.bff**  
  .IX Item "single.bff"
  Cumulative number of frames detected as bottom field first using single-frame detection.
* **multiple.current\_frame**  
  .IX Item "multiple.current_frame"
  Detected type of current frame using multiple-frame detection. One of:
  \`\`tff'' (top field first), \`\`bff'' (bottom field first),
  \`\`progressive'', or \`\`undetermined''
* **multiple.bff**  
  .IX Item "multiple.bff"
  Cumulative number of frames detected as bottom field first using multiple-frame detection.
* **single.progressive**  
  .IX Item "single.progressive"
  Cumulative number of frames detected as progressive using single-frame detection.
* **multiple.progressive**  
  .IX Item "multiple.progressive"
  Cumulative number of frames detected as progressive using multiple-frame detection.
* **single.undetermined**  
  .IX Item "single.undetermined"
  Cumulative number of frames that could not be classified using single-frame detection.
* **multiple.undetermined**  
  .IX Item "multiple.undetermined"
  Cumulative number of frames that could not be classified using multiple-frame detection.
* **repeated.current\_frame**  
  .IX Item "repeated.current_frame"
  Which field in the current frame is repeated from the last. One of \`\`neither'', \`\`top'', or \`\`bottom''.
* **repeated.neither**  
  .IX Item "repeated.neither"
  Cumulative number of frames with no repeated field.
* **repeated.top**  
  .IX Item "repeated.top"
  Cumulative number of frames with the top field repeated from the previous frame's top field.
* **repeated.bottom**  
  .IX Item "repeated.bottom"
  Cumulative number of frames with the bottom field repeated from the previous frame's bottom field.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **intl\_thres**  
  .IX Item "intl_thres"
  Set interlacing threshold.
* **prog\_thres**  
  .IX Item "prog_thres"
  Set progressive threshold.
* **rep\_thres**  
  .IX Item "rep_thres"
  Threshold for repeated field detection.
* **half\_life**  
  .IX Item "half_life"
  Number of frames after which a given frame's contribution to the
  statistics is halved (i.e., it contributes only 0.5 to its
  classification). The default of 0 means that all frames seen are given
  full weight of 1.0 forever.
* **analyze\_interlaced\_flag**  
  .IX Item "analyze_interlaced_flag"
  When this is not 0 then idet will use the specified number of frames to determine
  if the interlaced flag is accurate, it will not count undetermined frames.
  If the flag is found to be accurate it will be used without any further
  computations, if it is found to be inaccurate it will be cleared without any
  further computations. This allows inserting the idet filter as a low computational
  method to clean up the interlaced flag

<a name="il"></a>

### il

.IX Subsection "il"
Deinterleave or interleave fields.

This filter allows one to process interlaced images fields without
deinterlacing them. Deinterleaving splits the input frame into 2
fields (so called half pictures). Odd lines are moved to the top
half of the output image, even lines to the bottom half.
You can process (filter) them independently and then re-interleave them.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **luma_mode, l**  
  .IX Item "luma_mode, l"
* **chroma_mode, c**  
  .IX Item "chroma_mode, c"
* **alpha_mode, a**  
  .IX Item "alpha_mode, a"
  Available values for _luma\_mode_, _chroma\_mode_ and
  _alpha\_mode_ are:
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      Do nothing.
    * **deinterleave, d**  
      .IX Item "deinterleave, d"
      Deinterleave fields, placing one above the other.
    * **interleave, i**  
      .IX Item "interleave, i"
      Interleave fields. Reverse the effect of deinterleaving.
      .Sp
      Default value is \f(CW`none\*(C'.
* **luma_swap, ls**  
  .IX Item "luma_swap, ls"
* **chroma_swap, cs**  
  .IX Item "chroma_swap, cs"
* **alpha_swap, as**  
  .IX Item "alpha_swap, as"
  Swap luma/chroma/alpha fields. Exchange even & odd lines. Default value is \f(CW0.

<a name="inflate"></a>

### inflate

.IX Subsection "inflate"
Apply inflate effect to the video.

This filter replaces the pixel by the local(3x3) average by taking into account
only values higher than the pixel.

It accepts the following options:

* **threshold0**  
  .IX Item "threshold0"
* **threshold1**  
  .IX Item "threshold1"
* **threshold2**  
  .IX Item "threshold2"
* **threshold3**  
  .IX Item "threshold3"
  Limit the maximum change for each plane, default is 65535.
  If 0, plane will remain unchanged.

<a name="interlace"></a>

### interlace

.IX Subsection "interlace"
Simple interlacing filter from progressive contents. This interleaves upper (or
lower) lines from odd frames with lower (or upper) lines from even frames,
halving the frame rate and preserving image height.

.Vb 9
           Original        Original             New Frame
           Frame j\*(Aq      Frame \*(Aqj+1\*(Aq             (tff)
          ==========      ===========       ==================
            Line 0  --------------------&gt;    Frame j\*(Aq Line 0
            Line 1          Line 1  ----&gt;   Frame j+1\*(Aq Line 1
            Line 2 ---------------------&gt;    Frame j\*(Aq Line 2
            Line 3          Line 3  ----&gt;   Frame j+1\*(Aq Line 3
             ...             ...                   ...
        New Frame + 1 will be generated by Frame j+2\*(Aq and Frame \*(Aqj+3\*(Aq and so on
.Ve

It accepts the following optional parameters:

* **scan**  
  .IX Item "scan"
  This determines whether the interlaced frame is taken from the even
  (tff - default) or odd (bff) lines of the progressive frame.
* **lowpass**  
  .IX Item "lowpass"
  Vertical lowpass filter to avoid twitter interlacing and
  reduce moire patterns.
    * **0, off**  
      .IX Item "0, off"
      Disable vertical lowpass filter
    * **1, linear**  
      .IX Item "1, linear"
      Enable linear filter (default)
    * **2, complex**  
      .IX Item "2, complex"
      Enable complex filter. This will slightly less reduce twitter and moire
      but better retain detail and subjective sharpness impression.

<a name="kerndeint"></a>

### kerndeint

.IX Subsection "kerndeint"
Deinterlace input video by applying Donald Graft's adaptive kernel
deinterling. Work on interlaced parts of a video to produce
progressive frames.

The description of the accepted parameters follows.

* **thresh**  
  .IX Item "thresh"
  Set the threshold which affects the filter's tolerance when
  determining if a pixel line must be processed. It must be an integer
  in the range [0,255] and defaults to 10. A value of 0 will result in
  applying the process on every pixels.
* **map**  
  .IX Item "map"
  Paint pixels exceeding the threshold value to white if set to 1.
  Default is 0.
* **order**  
  .IX Item "order"
  Set the fields order. Swap fields if set to 1, leave fields alone if
  0. Default is 0.
* **sharp**  
  .IX Item "sharp"
  Enable additional sharpening if set to 1. Default is 0.
* **twoway**  
  .IX Item "twoway"
  Enable twoway sharpening if set to 1. Default is 0.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Apply default values:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          kerndeint=thresh=10:map=0:order=0:sharp=0:twoway=0
  .Ve
* ·  
  Enable additional sharpening:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          kerndeint=sharp=1
  .Ve
* ·  
  Paint processed pixels in white:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          kerndeint=map=1
  .Ve

<a name="lenscorrection"></a>

### lenscorrection

.IX Subsection "lenscorrection"
Correct radial lens distortion

This filter can be used to correct for radial distortion as can result from the use
of wide angle lenses, and thereby re-rectify the image. To find the right parameters
one can use tools available for example as part of opencv or simply trial-and-error.
To use opencv use the calibration sample (under samples/cpp) from the opencv sources
and extract the k1 and k2 coefficients from the resulting matrix.

Note that effectively the same filter is available in the open-source tools Krita and
Digikam from the \s-1KDE\s0 project.

In contrast to the **vignette** filter, which can also be used to compensate lens errors,
this filter corrects the distortion of the image, whereas **vignette** corrects the
brightness distribution, so you may want to use both filters together in certain
cases, though you will have to take care of ordering, i.e. whether vignetting should
be applied before or after lens correction.

_Options_
.IX Subsection "Options"

The filter accepts the following options:

* **cx**  
  .IX Item "cx"
  Relative x-coordinate of the focal point of the image, and thereby the center of the
  distortion. This value has a range [0,1] and is expressed as fractions of the image
  width. Default is 0.5.
* **cy**  
  .IX Item "cy"
  Relative y-coordinate of the focal point of the image, and thereby the center of the
  distortion. This value has a range [0,1] and is expressed as fractions of the image
  height. Default is 0.5.
* **k1**  
  .IX Item "k1"
  Coefficient of the quadratic correction term. This value has a range [-1,1]. 0 means
  no correction. Default is 0.
* **k2**  
  .IX Item "k2"
  Coefficient of the double quadratic correction term. This value has a range [-1,1].
  0 means no correction. Default is 0.

The formula that generates the correction is:

_r\_src_ = _r\_tgt_ * (1 + _k1_ * (_r\_tgt_ / _r\_0_)^2 + _k2_ * (_r\_tgt_ / _r\_0_)^4)

where _r\_0_ is halve of the image diagonal and _r\_src_ and _r\_tgt_ are the
distances from the focal point in the source and target images, respectively.

<a name="lensfun"></a>

### lensfun

.IX Subsection "lensfun"
Apply lens correction via the lensfun library (&lt;**http://lensfun.sourceforge.net/**&gt;).

The \f(CW`lensfun\*(C' filter requires the camera make, camera model, and lens model
to apply the lens correction. The filter will load the lensfun database and
query it to find the corresponding camera and lens entries in the database. As
long as these entries can be found with the given options, the filter can
perform corrections on frames. Note that incomplete strings will result in the
filter choosing the best match with the given options, and the filter will
output the chosen camera and lens models (logged with level info\*(R"). You must
provide the make, camera model, and lens model as they are required.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **make**  
  .IX Item "make"
  The make of the camera (for example, Canon\*(R"). This option is required.
* **model**  
  .IX Item "model"
  The model of the camera (for example, Canon \s-1EOS 100D\*(R"\s0). This option is
  required.
* **lens\_model**  
  .IX Item "lens_model"
  The model of the lens (for example, Canon EF-S 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 \s-1IS STM\*(R"\s0). This
  option is required.
* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  The type of correction to apply. The following values are valid options:
    * **vignetting**  
      .IX Item "vignetting"
      Enables fixing lens vignetting.
    * **geometry**  
      .IX Item "geometry"
      Enables fixing lens geometry. This is the default.
    * **subpixel**  
      .IX Item "subpixel"
      Enables fixing chromatic aberrations.
    * **vig\_geo**  
      .IX Item "vig_geo"
      Enables fixing lens vignetting and lens geometry.
    * **vig\_subpixel**  
      .IX Item "vig_subpixel"
      Enables fixing lens vignetting and chromatic aberrations.
    * **distortion**  
      .IX Item "distortion"
      Enables fixing both lens geometry and chromatic aberrations.
    * **all**  
      .IX Item "all"
      Enables all possible corrections.
* **focal\_length**  
  .IX Item "focal_length"
  The focal length of the image/video (zoom; expected constant for video). For
  example, a 18--55mm lens has focal length range of [18--55], so a value in that
  range should be chosen when using that lens. Default 18.
* **aperture**  
  .IX Item "aperture"
  The aperture of the image/video (expected constant for video). Note that
  aperture is only used for vignetting correction. Default 3.5.
* **focus\_distance**  
  .IX Item "focus_distance"
  The focus distance of the image/video (expected constant for video). Note that
  focus distance is only used for vignetting and only slightly affects the
  vignetting correction process. If unknown, leave it at the default value (which
  is 1000).
* **target\_geometry**  
  .IX Item "target_geometry"
  The target geometry of the output image/video. The following values are valid
  options:
    * **rectilinear (default)**  
      .IX Item "rectilinear (default)"
    * **fisheye**  
      .IX Item "fisheye"
    * **panoramic**  
      .IX Item "panoramic"
    * **equirectangular**  
      .IX Item "equirectangular"
    * **fisheye\_orthographic**  
      .IX Item "fisheye_orthographic"
    * **fisheye\_stereographic**  
      .IX Item "fisheye_stereographic"
    * **fisheye\_equisolid**  
      .IX Item "fisheye_equisolid"
    * **fisheye\_thoby**  
      .IX Item "fisheye_thoby"
* **reverse**  
  .IX Item "reverse"
  Apply the reverse of image correction (instead of correcting distortion, apply
  it).
* **interpolation**  
  .IX Item "interpolation"
  The type of interpolation used when correcting distortion. The following values
  are valid options:
    * **nearest**  
      .IX Item "nearest"
    * **linear (default)**  
      .IX Item "linear (default)"
    * **lanczos**  
      .IX Item "lanczos"

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Apply lens correction with make Canon\*(R", camera model \*(L"Canon \s-1EOS 100D\*(R",\s0 and lens
  model Canon EF-S 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 \s-1IS STM\*(R"\s0 with focal length of \*(L"18\*(R" and
  aperture of 8.0\*(R".
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i input.mov -vf lensfun=make=Canon:model="Canon EOS 100D":lens_model="Canon EF-S 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 IS STM":focal_length=18:aperture=8 -c:v h264 -b:v 8000k output.mov
  .Ve
* ·  
  Apply the same as before, but only for the first 5 seconds of video.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i input.mov -vf lensfun=make=Canon:model="Canon EOS 100D":lens_model="Canon EF-S 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 IS STM":focal_length=18:aperture=8:enable=lte(t\e,5)\*(Aq -c:v h264 -b:v 8000k output.mov
  .Ve

<a name="libvmaf"></a>

### libvmaf

.IX Subsection "libvmaf"
Obtain the \s-1VMAF\s0 (Video Multi-Method Assessment Fusion)
score between two input videos.

The obtained \s-1VMAF\s0 score is printed through the logging system.

It requires Netflix's vmaf library (libvmaf) as a pre-requisite.
After installing the library it can be enabled using:
\f(CW`./configure --enable-libvmaf --enable-version3\*(C'.
If no model path is specified it uses the default model: \f(CW`vmaf\_v0.6.1.pkl\*(C'.

The filter has following options:

* **model\_path**  
  .IX Item "model_path"
  Set the model path which is to be used for \s-1SVM.\s0
  Default value: \f(CW"vmaf\_v0.6.1.pkl"
* **log\_path**  
  .IX Item "log_path"
  Set the file path to be used to store logs.
* **log\_fmt**  
  .IX Item "log_fmt"
  Set the format of the log file (xml or json).
* **enable\_transform**  
  .IX Item "enable_transform"
  Enables transform for computing vmaf.
* **phone\_model**  
  .IX Item "phone_model"
  Invokes the phone model which will generate \s-1VMAF\s0 scores higher than in the
  regular model, which is more suitable for laptop, \s-1TV,\s0 etc. viewing conditions.
* **psnr**  
  .IX Item "psnr"
  Enables computing psnr along with vmaf.
* **ssim**  
  .IX Item "ssim"
  Enables computing ssim along with vmaf.
* **ms\_ssim**  
  .IX Item "ms_ssim"
  Enables computing ms_ssim along with vmaf.
* **pool**  
  .IX Item "pool"
  Set the pool method (mean, min or harmonic mean) to be used for computing vmaf.
* **n\_threads**  
  .IX Item "n_threads"
  Set number of threads to be used when computing vmaf.
* **n\_subsample**  
  .IX Item "n_subsample"
  Set interval for frame subsampling used when computing vmaf.
* **enable\_conf\_interval**  
  .IX Item "enable_conf_interval"
  Enables confidence interval.

This filter also supports the **framesync** options.

On the below examples the input file _main.mpg_ being processed is
compared with the reference file _ref.mpg_.

.Vb 1
        ffmpeg -i main.mpg -i ref.mpg -lavfi libvmaf -f null -
.Ve

Example with options:

.Vb 1
        ffmpeg -i main.mpg -i ref.mpg -lavfi libvmaf="psnr=1:enable-transform=1" -f null -
.Ve

<a name="limiter"></a>

### limiter

.IX Subsection "limiter"
Limits the pixel components values to the specified range [min, max].

The filter accepts the following options:

* **min**  
  .IX Item "min"
  Lower bound. Defaults to the lowest allowed value for the input.
* **max**  
  .IX Item "max"
  Upper bound. Defaults to the highest allowed value for the input.
* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Specify which planes will be processed. Defaults to all available.

<a name="loop"></a>

### loop

.IX Subsection "loop"
Loop video frames.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **loop**  
  .IX Item "loop"
  Set the number of loops. Setting this value to -1 will result in infinite loops.
  Default is 0.
* **size**  
  .IX Item "size"
  Set maximal size in number of frames. Default is 0.
* **start**  
  .IX Item "start"
  Set first frame of loop. Default is 0.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Loop single first frame infinitely:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          loop=loop=-1:size=1:start=0
  .Ve
* ·  
  Loop single first frame 10 times:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          loop=loop=10:size=1:start=0
  .Ve
* ·  
  Loop 10 first frames 5 times:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          loop=loop=5:size=10:start=0
  .Ve

<a name="lut1d"></a>

### lut1d

.IX Subsection "lut1d"
Apply a 1D \s-1LUT\s0 to an input video.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **file**  
  .IX Item "file"
  Set the 1D \s-1LUT\s0 file name.
  .Sp
  Currently supported formats:
    * **cube**  
      .IX Item "cube"
      Iridas
* **interp**  
  .IX Item "interp"
  Select interpolation mode.
  .Sp
  Available values are:
    * **nearest**  
      .IX Item "nearest"
      Use values from the nearest defined point.
    * **linear**  
      .IX Item "linear"
      Interpolate values using the linear interpolation.
    * **cubic**  
      .IX Item "cubic"
      Interpolate values using the cubic interpolation.

<a name="lut3d"></a>

### lut3d

.IX Subsection "lut3d"
Apply a 3D \s-1LUT\s0 to an input video.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **file**  
  .IX Item "file"
  Set the 3D \s-1LUT\s0 file name.
  .Sp
  Currently supported formats:
    * **3dl**  
      .IX Item "3dl"
      AfterEffects
    * **cube**  
      .IX Item "cube"
      Iridas
    * **dat**  
      .IX Item "dat"
      DaVinci
    * **m3d**  
      .IX Item "m3d"
      Pandora
* **interp**  
  .IX Item "interp"
  Select interpolation mode.
  .Sp
  Available values are:
    * **nearest**  
      .IX Item "nearest"
      Use values from the nearest defined point.
    * **trilinear**  
      .IX Item "trilinear"
      Interpolate values using the 8 points defining a cube.
    * **tetrahedral**  
      .IX Item "tetrahedral"
      Interpolate values using a tetrahedron.

This filter also supports the **framesync** options.

<a name="lumakey"></a>

### lumakey

.IX Subsection "lumakey"
Turn certain luma values into transparency.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **threshold**  
  .IX Item "threshold"
  Set the luma which will be used as base for transparency.
  Default value is \f(CW0.
* **tolerance**  
  .IX Item "tolerance"
  Set the range of luma values to be keyed out.
  Default value is \f(CW0.
* **softness**  
  .IX Item "softness"
  Set the range of softness. Default value is \f(CW0.
  Use this to control gradual transition from zero to full transparency.

<a name="lut-lutrgb-lutyuv"></a>

### lut, lutrgb, lutyuv

.IX Subsection "lut, lutrgb, lutyuv"
Compute a look-up table for binding each pixel component input value
to an output value, and apply it to the input video.

_lutyuv_ applies a lookup table to a \s-1YUV\s0 input video, _lutrgb_
to an \s-1RGB\s0 input video.

These filters accept the following parameters:

* **c0**  
  .IX Item "c0"
  set first pixel component expression
* **c1**  
  .IX Item "c1"
  set second pixel component expression
* **c2**  
  .IX Item "c2"
  set third pixel component expression
* **c3**  
  .IX Item "c3"
  set fourth pixel component expression, corresponds to the alpha component
* **r**  
  .IX Item "r"
  set red component expression
* **g**  
  .IX Item "g"
  set green component expression
* **b**  
  .IX Item "b"
  set blue component expression
* **a**  
  .IX Item "a"
  alpha component expression
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  set Y/luminance component expression
* **u**  
  .IX Item "u"
  set U/Cb component expression
* **v**  
  .IX Item "v"
  set V/Cr component expression

Each of them specifies the expression to use for computing the lookup table for
the corresponding pixel component values.

The exact component associated to each of the _c*_ options depends on the
format in input.

The _lut_ filter requires either \s-1YUV\s0 or \s-1RGB\s0 pixel formats in input,
_lutrgb_ requires \s-1RGB\s0 pixel formats in input, and _lutyuv_ requires \s-1YUV.\s0

The expressions can contain the following constants and functions:

* **w**  
  .IX Item "w"
* **h**  
  .IX Item "h"
  The input width and height.
* **val**  
  .IX Item "val"
  The input value for the pixel component.
* **clipval**  
  .IX Item "clipval"
  The input value, clipped to the _minval_-_maxval_ range.
* **maxval**  
  .IX Item "maxval"
  The maximum value for the pixel component.
* **minval**  
  .IX Item "minval"
  The minimum value for the pixel component.
* **negval**  
  .IX Item "negval"
  The negated value for the pixel component value, clipped to the
  _minval_-_maxval_ range; it corresponds to the expression
  maxval-clipval+minval\*(R".
* **clip(val)**  
  .IX Item "clip(val)"
  The computed value in _val_, clipped to the
  _minval_-_maxval_ range.
* **gammaval(gamma)**  
  .IX Item "gammaval(gamma)"
  The computed gamma correction value of the pixel component value,
  clipped to the _minval_-_maxval_ range. It corresponds to the
  expression
  "pow((clipval-minval)/(maxval-minval)\e,_gamma_)*(maxval-minval)+minval"

All expressions default to val\*(R".

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Negate input video:
  .Sp
  .Vb 2
          lutrgb="r=maxval+minval-val:g=maxval+minval-val:b=maxval+minval-val"
          lutyuv="y=maxval+minval-val:u=maxval+minval-val:v=maxval+minval-val"
  .Ve
  .Sp
  The above is the same as:
  .Sp
  .Vb 2
          lutrgb="r=negval:g=negval:b=negval"
          lutyuv="y=negval:u=negval:v=negval"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Negate luminance:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          lutyuv=y=negval
  .Ve
* ·  
  Remove chroma components, turning the video into a graytone image:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          lutyuv="u=128:v=128"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Apply a luma burning effect:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          lutyuv="y=2*val"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Remove green and blue components:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          lutrgb="g=0:b=0"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Set a constant alpha channel value on input:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          format=rgba,lutrgb=a="maxval-minval/2"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Correct luminance gamma by a factor of 0.5:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          lutyuv=y=gammaval(0.5)
  .Ve
* ·  
  Discard least significant bits of luma:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          lutyuv=y=bitand(val, 128+64+32)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Technicolor like effect:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          lutyuv=u=(val-maxval/2)*2+maxval/2\*(Aq:v=\*(Aq(val-maxval/2)*2+maxval/2\*(Aq
  .Ve

<a name="lut2-tlut2"></a>

### lut2, tlut2

.IX Subsection "lut2, tlut2"
The \f(CW`lut2\*(C' filter takes two input streams and outputs one
stream.

The \f(CW`tlut2\*(C' (time lut2) filter takes two consecutive frames
from one single stream.

This filter accepts the following parameters:

* **c0**  
  .IX Item "c0"
  set first pixel component expression
* **c1**  
  .IX Item "c1"
  set second pixel component expression
* **c2**  
  .IX Item "c2"
  set third pixel component expression
* **c3**  
  .IX Item "c3"
  set fourth pixel component expression, corresponds to the alpha component

Each of them specifies the expression to use for computing the lookup table for
the corresponding pixel component values.

The exact component associated to each of the _c*_ options depends on the
format in inputs.

The expressions can contain the following constants:

* **w**  
  .IX Item "w"
* **h**  
  .IX Item "h"
  The input width and height.
* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
  The first input value for the pixel component.
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  The second input value for the pixel component.
* **bdx**  
  .IX Item "bdx"
  The first input video bit depth.
* **bdy**  
  .IX Item "bdy"
  The second input video bit depth.

All expressions default to x\*(R".

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Highlight differences between two \s-1RGB\s0 video streams:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          lut2=ifnot(x-y,0,pow(2,bdx)-1):ifnot(x-y,0,pow(2,bdx)-1):ifnot(x-y,0,pow(2,bdx)-1)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Highlight differences between two \s-1YUV\s0 video streams:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          lut2=ifnot(x-y,0,pow(2,bdx)-1):ifnot(x-y,pow(2,bdx-1),pow(2,bdx)-1):ifnot(x-y,pow(2,bdx-1),pow(2,bdx)-1)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Show max difference between two video streams:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          lut2=if(lt(x,y),0,if(gt(x,y),pow(2,bdx)-1,pow(2,bdx-1))):if(lt(x,y),0,if(gt(x,y),pow(2,bdx)-1,pow(2,bdx-1))):if(lt(x,y),0,if(gt(x,y),pow(2,bdx)-1,pow(2,bdx-1)))\*(Aq
  .Ve

<a name="maskedclamp"></a>

### maskedclamp

.IX Subsection "maskedclamp"
Clamp the first input stream with the second input and third input stream.

Returns the value of first stream to be between second input
stream - \f(CW`undershoot\*(C' and third input stream + \f(CW\*(C\`overshoot\*(C'.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **undershoot**  
  .IX Item "undershoot"
  Default value is \f(CW0.
* **overshoot**  
  .IX Item "overshoot"
  Default value is \f(CW0.
* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Set which planes will be processed as bitmap, unprocessed planes will be
  copied from first stream.
  By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.

<a name="maskedmerge"></a>

### maskedmerge

.IX Subsection "maskedmerge"
Merge the first input stream with the second input stream using per pixel
weights in the third input stream.

A value of 0 in the third stream pixel component means that pixel component
from first stream is returned unchanged, while maximum value (eg. 255 for
8-bit videos) means that pixel component from second stream is returned
unchanged. Intermediate values define the amount of merging between both
input stream's pixel components.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Set which planes will be processed as bitmap, unprocessed planes will be
  copied from first stream.
  By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.

<a name="mcdeint"></a>

### mcdeint

.IX Subsection "mcdeint"
Apply motion-compensation deinterlacing.

It needs one field per frame as input and must thus be used together
with yadif=1/3 or equivalent.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Set the deinterlacing mode.
  .Sp
  It accepts one of the following values:
    * **fast**  
      .IX Item "fast"
    * **medium**  
      .IX Item "medium"
    * **slow**  
      .IX Item "slow"
      use iterative motion estimation
    * **extra\_slow**  
      .IX Item "extra_slow"
      like **slow**, but use multiple reference frames.
      .Sp
      Default value is **fast**.
* **parity**  
  .IX Item "parity"
  Set the picture field parity assumed for the input video. It must be
  one of the following values:
    * **0, tff**  
      .IX Item "0, tff"
      assume top field first
    * **1, bff**  
      .IX Item "1, bff"
      assume bottom field first
      .Sp
      Default value is **bff**.
* **qp**  
  .IX Item "qp"
  Set per-block quantization parameter (\s-1QP\s0) used by the internal
  encoder.
  .Sp
  Higher values should result in a smoother motion vector field but less
  optimal individual vectors. Default value is 1.

<a name="mergeplanes"></a>

### mergeplanes

.IX Subsection "mergeplanes"
Merge color channel components from several video streams.

The filter accepts up to 4 input streams, and merge selected input
planes to the output video.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **mapping**  
  .IX Item "mapping"
  Set input to output plane mapping. Default is \f(CW0.
  .Sp
  The mappings is specified as a bitmap. It should be specified as a
  hexadecimal number in the form 0xAa[Bb[Cc[Dd]]]. 'Aa' describes the
  mapping for the first plane of the output stream. 'A' sets the number of
  the input stream to use (from 0 to 3), and 'a' the plane number of the
  corresponding input to use (from 0 to 3). The rest of the mappings is
  similar, 'Bb' describes the mapping for the output stream second
  plane, 'Cc' describes the mapping for the output stream third plane and
  'Dd' describes the mapping for the output stream fourth plane.
* **format**  
  .IX Item "format"
  Set output pixel format. Default is \f(CW`yuva444p\*(C'.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Merge three gray video streams of same width and height into single video stream:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          [a0][a1][a2]mergeplanes=0x001020:yuv444p
  .Ve
* ·  
  Merge 1st yuv444p stream and 2nd gray video stream into yuva444p video stream:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          [a0][a1]mergeplanes=0x00010210:yuva444p
  .Ve
* ·  
  Swap Y and A plane in yuva444p stream:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          format=yuva444p,mergeplanes=0x03010200:yuva444p
  .Ve
* ·  
  Swap U and V plane in yuv420p stream:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          format=yuv420p,mergeplanes=0x000201:yuv420p
  .Ve
* ·  
  Cast a rgb24 clip to yuv444p:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          format=rgb24,mergeplanes=0x000102:yuv444p
  .Ve

<a name="mestimate"></a>

### mestimate

.IX Subsection "mestimate"
Estimate and export motion vectors using block matching algorithms.
Motion vectors are stored in frame side data to be used by other filters.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **method**  
  .IX Item "method"
  Specify the motion estimation method. Accepts one of the following values:
    * **esa**  
      .IX Item "esa"
      Exhaustive search algorithm.
    * **tss**  
      .IX Item "tss"
      Three step search algorithm.
    * **tdls**  
      .IX Item "tdls"
      Two dimensional logarithmic search algorithm.
    * **ntss**  
      .IX Item "ntss"
      New three step search algorithm.
    * **fss**  
      .IX Item "fss"
      Four step search algorithm.
    * **ds**  
      .IX Item "ds"
      Diamond search algorithm.
    * **hexbs**  
      .IX Item "hexbs"
      Hexagon-based search algorithm.
    * **epzs**  
      .IX Item "epzs"
      Enhanced predictive zonal search algorithm.
    * **umh**  
      .IX Item "umh"
      Uneven multi-hexagon search algorithm.
      .Sp
      Default value is **esa**.
* **mb\_size**  
  .IX Item "mb_size"
  Macroblock size. Default \f(CW16.
* **search\_param**  
  .IX Item "search_param"
  Search parameter. Default \f(CW7.

<a name="midequalizer"></a>

### midequalizer

.IX Subsection "midequalizer"
Apply Midway Image Equalization effect using two video streams.

Midway Image Equalization adjusts a pair of images to have the same
histogram, while maintaining their dynamics as much as possible. It's
useful for e.g. matching exposures from a pair of stereo cameras.

This filter has two inputs and one output, which must be of same pixel format, but
may be of different sizes. The output of filter is first input adjusted with
midway histogram of both inputs.

This filter accepts the following option:

* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Set which planes to process. Default is \f(CW15, which is all available planes.

<a name="minterpolate"></a>

### minterpolate

.IX Subsection "minterpolate"
Convert the video to specified frame rate using motion interpolation.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **fps**  
  .IX Item "fps"
  Specify the output frame rate. This can be rational e.g. \f(CW`60000/1001\*(C'. Frames are dropped if _fps_ is lower than source fps. Default \f(CW60.
* **mi\_mode**  
  .IX Item "mi_mode"
  Motion interpolation mode. Following values are accepted:
    * **dup**  
      .IX Item "dup"
      Duplicate previous or next frame for interpolating new ones.
    * **blend**  
      .IX Item "blend"
      Blend source frames. Interpolated frame is mean of previous and next frames.
    * **mci**  
      .IX Item "mci"
      Motion compensated interpolation. Following options are effective when this mode is selected:
        * **mc\_mode**  
          .IX Item "mc_mode"
          Motion compensation mode. Following values are accepted:
            * **obmc**  
              .IX Item "obmc"
              Overlapped block motion compensation.
            * **aobmc**  
              .IX Item "aobmc"
              Adaptive overlapped block motion compensation. Window weighting coefficients are controlled adaptively according to the reliabilities of the neighboring motion vectors to reduce oversmoothing.
              .Sp
              Default mode is **obmc**.
        * **me\_mode**  
          .IX Item "me_mode"
          Motion estimation mode. Following values are accepted:
            * **bidir**  
              .IX Item "bidir"
              Bidirectional motion estimation. Motion vectors are estimated for each source frame in both forward and backward directions.
            * **bilat**  
              .IX Item "bilat"
              Bilateral motion estimation. Motion vectors are estimated directly for interpolated frame.
              .Sp
              Default mode is **bilat**.
        * **me**  
          .IX Item "me"
          The algorithm to be used for motion estimation. Following values are accepted:
            * **esa**  
              .IX Item "esa"
              Exhaustive search algorithm.
            * **tss**  
              .IX Item "tss"
              Three step search algorithm.
            * **tdls**  
              .IX Item "tdls"
              Two dimensional logarithmic search algorithm.
            * **ntss**  
              .IX Item "ntss"
              New three step search algorithm.
            * **fss**  
              .IX Item "fss"
              Four step search algorithm.
            * **ds**  
              .IX Item "ds"
              Diamond search algorithm.
            * **hexbs**  
              .IX Item "hexbs"
              Hexagon-based search algorithm.
            * **epzs**  
              .IX Item "epzs"
              Enhanced predictive zonal search algorithm.
            * **umh**  
              .IX Item "umh"
              Uneven multi-hexagon search algorithm.
              .Sp
              Default algorithm is **epzs**.
        * **mb\_size**  
          .IX Item "mb_size"
          Macroblock size. Default \f(CW16.
        * **search\_param**  
          .IX Item "search_param"
          Motion estimation search parameter. Default \f(CW32.
        * **vsbmc**  
          .IX Item "vsbmc"
          Enable variable-size block motion compensation. Motion estimation is applied with smaller block sizes at object boundaries in order to make the them less blur. Default is \f(CW0 (disabled).
* **scd**  
  .IX Item "scd"
  Scene change detection method. Scene change leads motion vectors to be in random direction. Scene change detection replace interpolated frames by duplicate ones. May not be needed for other modes. Following values are accepted:
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      Disable scene change detection.
    * **fdiff**  
      .IX Item "fdiff"
      Frame difference. Corresponding pixel values are compared and if it satisfies _scd\_threshold_ scene change is detected.
      .Sp
      Default method is **fdiff**.
* **scd\_threshold**  
  .IX Item "scd_threshold"
  Scene change detection threshold. Default is \f(CW5.0.

<a name="mix"></a>

### mix

.IX Subsection "mix"
Mix several video input streams into one video stream.

A description of the accepted options follows.

* **nb\_inputs**  
  .IX Item "nb_inputs"
  The number of inputs. If unspecified, it defaults to 2.
* **weights**  
  .IX Item "weights"
  Specify weight of each input video stream as sequence.
  Each weight is separated by space. If number of weights
  is smaller than number of _frames_ last specified
  weight will be used for all remaining unset weights.
* **scale**  
  .IX Item "scale"
  Specify scale, if it is set it will be multiplied with sum
  of each weight multiplied with pixel values to give final destination
  pixel value. By default _scale_ is auto scaled to sum of weights.
* **duration**  
  .IX Item "duration"
  Specify how end of stream is determined.
    * **longest**  
      .IX Item "longest"
      The duration of the longest input. (default)
    * **shortest**  
      .IX Item "shortest"
      The duration of the shortest input.
    * **first**  
      .IX Item "first"
      The duration of the first input.

<a name="mpdecimate"></a>

### mpdecimate

.IX Subsection "mpdecimate"
Drop frames that do not differ greatly from the previous frame in
order to reduce frame rate.

The main use of this filter is for very-low-bitrate encoding
(e.g. streaming over dialup modem), but it could in theory be used for
fixing movies that were inverse-telecined incorrectly.

A description of the accepted options follows.

* **max**  
  .IX Item "max"
  Set the maximum number of consecutive frames which can be dropped (if
  positive), or the minimum interval between dropped frames (if
  negative). If the value is 0, the frame is dropped disregarding the
  number of previous sequentially dropped frames.
  .Sp
  Default value is 0.
* **hi**  
  .IX Item "hi"
* **lo**  
  .IX Item "lo"
* **frac**  
  .IX Item "frac"
  Set the dropping threshold values.
  .Sp
  Values for **hi** and **lo** are for 8x8 pixel blocks and
  represent actual pixel value differences, so a threshold of 64
  corresponds to 1 unit of difference for each pixel, or the same spread
  out differently over the block.
  .Sp
  A frame is a candidate for dropping if no 8x8 blocks differ by more
  than a threshold of **hi**, and if no more than **frac** blocks (1
  meaning the whole image) differ by more than a threshold of **lo**.
  .Sp
  Default value for **hi** is 64*12, default value for **lo** is
  64*5, and default value for **frac** is 0.33.

<a name="negate"></a>

### negate

.IX Subsection "negate"
Negate (invert) the input video.

It accepts the following option:

* **negate\_alpha**  
  .IX Item "negate_alpha"
  With value 1, it negates the alpha component, if present. Default value is 0.

<a name="nlmeans"></a>

### nlmeans

.IX Subsection "nlmeans"
Denoise frames using Non-Local Means algorithm.

Each pixel is adjusted by looking for other pixels with similar contexts. This
context similarity is defined by comparing their surrounding patches of size
**p**x**p**. Patches are searched in an area of **r**x**r**
around the pixel.

Note that the research area defines centers for patches, which means some
patches will be made of pixels outside that research area.

The filter accepts the following options.

* **s**  
  .IX Item "s"
  Set denoising strength.
* **p**  
  .IX Item "p"
  Set patch size.
* **pc**  
  .IX Item "pc"
  Same as **p** but for chroma planes.
  .Sp
  The default value is _0_ and means automatic.
* **r**  
  .IX Item "r"
  Set research size.
* **rc**  
  .IX Item "rc"
  Same as **r** but for chroma planes.
  .Sp
  The default value is _0_ and means automatic.

<a name="nnedi"></a>

### nnedi

.IX Subsection "nnedi"
Deinterlace video using neural network edge directed interpolation.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **weights**  
  .IX Item "weights"
  Mandatory option, without binary file filter can not work.
  Currently file can be found here:
  https://github.com/dubhater/vapoursynth-nnedi3/blob/master/src/nnedi3_weights.bin
* **deint**  
  .IX Item "deint"
  Set which frames to deinterlace, by default it is \f(CW`all\*(C'.
  Can be \f(CW`all\*(C' or \f(CW\*(C\`interlaced\*(C'.
* **field**  
  .IX Item "field"
  Set mode of operation.
  .Sp
  Can be one of the following:
    * **af**  
      .IX Item "af"
      Use frame flags, both fields.
    * **a**  
      .IX Item "a"
      Use frame flags, single field.
    * **t**  
      .IX Item "t"
      Use top field only.
    * **b**  
      .IX Item "b"
      Use bottom field only.
    * **tf**  
      .IX Item "tf"
      Use both fields, top first.
    * **bf**  
      .IX Item "bf"
      Use both fields, bottom first.
* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Set which planes to process, by default filter process all frames.
* **nsize**  
  .IX Item "nsize"
  Set size of local neighborhood around each pixel, used by the predictor neural
  network.
  .Sp
  Can be one of the following:
    * **s8x6**  
      .IX Item "s8x6"
    * **s16x6**  
      .IX Item "s16x6"
    * **s32x6**  
      .IX Item "s32x6"
    * **s48x6**  
      .IX Item "s48x6"
    * **s8x4**  
      .IX Item "s8x4"
    * **s16x4**  
      .IX Item "s16x4"
    * **s32x4**  
      .IX Item "s32x4"
* **nns**  
  .IX Item "nns"
  Set the number of neurons in predictor neural network.
  Can be one of the following:
    * **n16**  
      .IX Item "n16"
    * **n32**  
      .IX Item "n32"
    * **n64**  
      .IX Item "n64"
    * **n128**  
      .IX Item "n128"
    * **n256**  
      .IX Item "n256"
* **qual**  
  .IX Item "qual"
  Controls the number of different neural network predictions that are blended
  together to compute the final output value. Can be \f(CW`fast\*(C', default or
  \f(CW`slow\*(C'.
* **etype**  
  .IX Item "etype"
  Set which set of weights to use in the predictor.
  Can be one of the following:
    * **a**  
      .IX Item "a"
      weights trained to minimize absolute error
    * **s**  
      .IX Item "s"
      weights trained to minimize squared error
* **pscrn**  
  .IX Item "pscrn"
  Controls whether or not the prescreener neural network is used to decide
  which pixels should be processed by the predictor neural network and which
  can be handled by simple cubic interpolation.
  The prescreener is trained to know whether cubic interpolation will be
  sufficient for a pixel or whether it should be predicted by the predictor nn.
  The computational complexity of the prescreener nn is much less than that of
  the predictor nn. Since most pixels can be handled by cubic interpolation,
  using the prescreener generally results in much faster processing.
  The prescreener is pretty accurate, so the difference between using it and not
  using it is almost always unnoticeable.
  .Sp
  Can be one of the following:
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
    * **original**  
      .IX Item "original"
    * **new**  
      .IX Item "new"
      .Sp
      Default is \f(CW`new\*(C'.
* **fapprox**  
  .IX Item "fapprox"
  Set various debugging flags.

<a name="noformat"></a>

### noformat

.IX Subsection "noformat"
Force libavfilter not to use any of the specified pixel formats for the
input to the next filter.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **pix\_fmts**  
  .IX Item "pix_fmts"
  A '|'-separated list of pixel format names, such as
  pix_fmts=yuv420p|monow|rgb24".

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Force libavfilter to use a format different from _yuv420p_ for the
  input to the vflip filter:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          noformat=pix_fmts=yuv420p,vflip
  .Ve
* ·  
  Convert the input video to any of the formats not contained in the list:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          noformat=yuv420p|yuv444p|yuv410p
  .Ve

<a name="noise"></a>

### noise

.IX Subsection "noise"
Add noise on video input frame.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **all\_seed**  
  .IX Item "all_seed"
* **c0\_seed**  
  .IX Item "c0_seed"
* **c1\_seed**  
  .IX Item "c1_seed"
* **c2\_seed**  
  .IX Item "c2_seed"
* **c3\_seed**  
  .IX Item "c3_seed"
  Set noise seed for specific pixel component or all pixel components in case
  of _all\_seed_. Default value is \f(CW123457.
* **all_strength, alls**  
  .IX Item "all_strength, alls"
* **c0_strength, c0s**  
  .IX Item "c0_strength, c0s"
* **c1_strength, c1s**  
  .IX Item "c1_strength, c1s"
* **c2_strength, c2s**  
  .IX Item "c2_strength, c2s"
* **c3_strength, c3s**  
  .IX Item "c3_strength, c3s"
  Set noise strength for specific pixel component or all pixel components in case
  _all\_strength_. Default value is \f(CW0. Allowed range is [0, 100].
* **all_flags, allf**  
  .IX Item "all_flags, allf"
* **c0_flags, c0f**  
  .IX Item "c0_flags, c0f"
* **c1_flags, c1f**  
  .IX Item "c1_flags, c1f"
* **c2_flags, c2f**  
  .IX Item "c2_flags, c2f"
* **c3_flags, c3f**  
  .IX Item "c3_flags, c3f"
  Set pixel component flags or set flags for all components if _all\_flags_.
  Available values for component flags are:
    * **a**  
      .IX Item "a"
      averaged temporal noise (smoother)
    * **p**  
      .IX Item "p"
      mix random noise with a (semi)regular pattern
    * **t**  
      .IX Item "t"
      temporal noise (noise pattern changes between frames)
    * **u**  
      .IX Item "u"
      uniform noise (gaussian otherwise)

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

Add temporal and uniform noise to input video:

.Vb 1
        noise=alls=20:allf=t+u
.Ve

<a name="normalize"></a>

### normalize

.IX Subsection "normalize"
Normalize \s-1RGB\s0 video (aka histogram stretching, contrast stretching).
See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normalization_(image_processing)

For each channel of each frame, the filter computes the input range and maps
it linearly to the user-specified output range. The output range defaults
to the full dynamic range from pure black to pure white.

Temporal smoothing can be used on the input range to reduce flickering (rapid
changes in brightness) caused when small dark or bright objects enter or leave
the scene. This is similar to the auto-exposure (automatic gain control) on a
video camera, and, like a video camera, it may cause a period of over- or
under-exposure of the video.

The R,G,B channels can be normalized independently, which may cause some
color shifting, or linked together as a single channel, which prevents
color shifting. Linked normalization preserves hue. Independent normalization
does not, so it can be used to remove some color casts. Independent and linked
normalization can be combined in any ratio.

The normalize filter accepts the following options:

* **blackpt**  
  .IX Item "blackpt"
* **whitept**  
  .IX Item "whitept"
  Colors which define the output range. The minimum input value is mapped to
  the _blackpt_. The maximum input value is mapped to the _whitept_.
  The defaults are black and white respectively. Specifying white for
  _blackpt_ and black for _whitept_ will give color-inverted,
  normalized video. Shades of grey can be used to reduce the dynamic range
  (contrast). Specifying saturated colors here can create some interesting
  effects.
* **smoothing**  
  .IX Item "smoothing"
  The number of previous frames to use for temporal smoothing. The input range
  of each channel is smoothed using a rolling average over the current frame
  and the _smoothing_ previous frames. The default is 0 (no temporal
  smoothing).
* **independence**  
  .IX Item "independence"
  Controls the ratio of independent (color shifting) channel normalization to
  linked (color preserving) normalization. 0.0 is fully linked, 1.0 is fully
  independent. Defaults to 1.0 (fully independent).
* **strength**  
  .IX Item "strength"
  Overall strength of the filter. 1.0 is full strength. 0.0 is a rather
  expensive no-op. Defaults to 1.0 (full strength).

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

Stretch video contrast to use the full dynamic range, with no temporal
smoothing; may flicker depending on the source content:

.Vb 1
        normalize=blackpt=black:whitept=white:smoothing=0
.Ve

As above, but with 50 frames of temporal smoothing; flicker should be
reduced, depending on the source content:

.Vb 1
        normalize=blackpt=black:whitept=white:smoothing=50
.Ve

As above, but with hue-preserving linked channel normalization:

.Vb 1
        normalize=blackpt=black:whitept=white:smoothing=50:independence=0
.Ve

As above, but with half strength:

.Vb 1
        normalize=blackpt=black:whitept=white:smoothing=50:independence=0:strength=0.5
.Ve

Map the darkest input color to red, the brightest input color to cyan:

.Vb 1
        normalize=blackpt=red:whitept=cyan
.Ve

<a name="null"></a>

### null

.IX Subsection "null"
Pass the video source unchanged to the output.

<a name="ocr"></a>

### ocr

.IX Subsection "ocr"
Optical Character Recognition

This filter uses Tesseract for optical character recognition. To enable
compilation of this filter, you need to configure FFmpeg with
\f(CW`--enable-libtesseract\*(C'.

It accepts the following options:

* **datapath**  
  .IX Item "datapath"
  Set datapath to tesseract data. Default is to use whatever was
  set at installation.
* **language**  
  .IX Item "language"
  Set language, default is eng\*(R".
* **whitelist**  
  .IX Item "whitelist"
  Set character whitelist.
* **blacklist**  
  .IX Item "blacklist"
  Set character blacklist.

The filter exports recognized text as the frame metadata \f(CW`lavfi.ocr.text\*(C'.

<a name="ocv"></a>

### ocv

.IX Subsection "ocv"
Apply a video transform using libopencv.

To enable this filter, install the libopencv library and headers and
configure FFmpeg with \f(CW`--enable-libopencv\*(C'.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **filter\_name**  
  .IX Item "filter_name"
  The name of the libopencv filter to apply.
* **filter\_params**  
  .IX Item "filter_params"
  The parameters to pass to the libopencv filter. If not specified, the default
  values are assumed.

Refer to the official libopencv documentation for more precise
information:
&lt;**http://docs.opencv.org/master/modules/imgproc/doc/filtering.html**&gt;

Several libopencv filters are supported; see the following subsections.

_dilate_
.IX Subsection "dilate"

Dilate an image by using a specific structuring element.
It corresponds to the libopencv function \f(CW`cvDilate\*(C'.

It accepts the parameters: _struct\_el_|_nb\_iterations_.

_struct\_el_ represents a structuring element, and has the syntax:
_cols_x_rows_+_anchor\_x_x_anchor\_y_/_shape_

_cols_ and _rows_ represent the number of columns and rows of
the structuring element, _anchor\_x_ and _anchor\_y_ the anchor
point, and _shape_ the shape for the structuring element. _shape_
must be rect\*(R", \*(L"cross\*(R", \*(L"ellipse\*(R", or \*(L"custom\*(R".

If the value for _shape_ is custom\*(R", it must be followed by a
string of the form "=_filename_". The file with name
_filename_ is assumed to represent a binary image, with each
printable character corresponding to a bright pixel. When a custom
_shape_ is used, _cols_ and _rows_ are ignored, the number
or columns and rows of the read file are assumed instead.

The default value for _struct\_el_ is 3x3+0x0/rect\*(R".

_nb\_iterations_ specifies the number of times the transform is
applied to the image, and defaults to 1.

Some examples:

.Vb 2
        # Use the default values
        ocv=dilate
        
        # Dilate using a structuring element with a 5x5 cross, iterating two times
        ocv=filter_name=dilate:filter_params=5x5+2x2/cross|2
        
        # Read the shape from the file diamond.shape, iterating two times.
        # The file diamond.shape may contain a pattern of characters like this
        #   *
        #  ***
        # *****
        #  ***
        #   *
        # The specified columns and rows are ignored
        # but the anchor point coordinates are not
        ocv=dilate:0x0+2x2/custom=diamond.shape|2
.Ve

_erode_
.IX Subsection "erode"

Erode an image by using a specific structuring element.
It corresponds to the libopencv function \f(CW`cvErode\*(C'.

It accepts the parameters: _struct\_el_:_nb\_iterations_,
with the same syntax and semantics as the **dilate** filter.

_smooth_
.IX Subsection "smooth"

Smooth the input video.

The filter takes the following parameters:
_type_|_param1_|_param2_|_param3_|_param4_.

_type_ is the type of smooth filter to apply, and must be one of
the following values: blur\*(R", \*(L"blur_no_scale\*(R", \*(L"median\*(R", \*(L"gaussian\*(R",
or bilateral\*(R". The default value is \*(L"gaussian\*(R".

The meaning of _param1_, _param2_, _param3_, and _param4_
depend on the smooth type. _param1_ and
_param2_ accept integer positive values or 0. _param3_ and
_param4_ accept floating point values.

The default value for _param1_ is 3. The default value for the
other parameters is 0.

These parameters correspond to the parameters assigned to the
libopencv function \f(CW`cvSmooth\*(C'.

<a name="oscilloscope"></a>

### oscilloscope

.IX Subsection "oscilloscope"
2D Video Oscilloscope.

Useful to measure spatial impulse, step responses, chroma delays, etc.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
  Set scope center x position.
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  Set scope center y position.
* **s**  
  .IX Item "s"
  Set scope size, relative to frame diagonal.
* **t**  
  .IX Item "t"
  Set scope tilt/rotation.
* **o**  
  .IX Item "o"
  Set trace opacity.
* **tx**  
  .IX Item "tx"
  Set trace center x position.
* **ty**  
  .IX Item "ty"
  Set trace center y position.
* **tw**  
  .IX Item "tw"
  Set trace width, relative to width of frame.
* **th**  
  .IX Item "th"
  Set trace height, relative to height of frame.
* **c**  
  .IX Item "c"
  Set which components to trace. By default it traces first three components.
* **g**  
  .IX Item "g"
  Draw trace grid. By default is enabled.
* **st**  
  .IX Item "st"
  Draw some statistics. By default is enabled.
* **sc**  
  .IX Item "sc"
  Draw scope. By default is enabled.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Inspect full first row of video frame.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          oscilloscope=x=0.5:y=0:s=1
  .Ve
* ·  
  Inspect full last row of video frame.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          oscilloscope=x=0.5:y=1:s=1
  .Ve
* ·  
  Inspect full 5th line of video frame of height 1080.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          oscilloscope=x=0.5:y=5/1080:s=1
  .Ve
* ·  
  Inspect full last column of video frame.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          oscilloscope=x=1:y=0.5:s=1:t=1
  .Ve

<a name="overlay"></a>

### overlay

.IX Subsection "overlay"
Overlay one video on top of another.

It takes two inputs and has one output. The first input is the main\*(R"
video on which the second input is overlaid.

It accepts the following parameters:

A description of the accepted options follows.

* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  Set the expression for the x and y coordinates of the overlaid video
  on the main video. Default value is 0\*(R" for both expressions. In case
  the expression is invalid, it is set to a huge value (meaning that the
  overlay will not be displayed within the output visible area).
* **eof\_action**  
  .IX Item "eof_action"
  See **framesync**.
* **eval**  
  .IX Item "eval"
  Set when the expressions for **x**, and **y** are evaluated.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **init**  
      .IX Item "init"
      only evaluate expressions once during the filter initialization or
      when a command is processed
    * **frame**  
      .IX Item "frame"
      evaluate expressions for each incoming frame
      .Sp
      Default value is **frame**.
* **shortest**  
  .IX Item "shortest"
  See **framesync**.
* **format**  
  .IX Item "format"
  Set the format for the output video.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **yuv420**  
      .IX Item "yuv420"
      force \s-1YUV420\s0 output
    * **yuv422**  
      .IX Item "yuv422"
      force \s-1YUV422\s0 output
    * **yuv444**  
      .IX Item "yuv444"
      force \s-1YUV444\s0 output
    * **rgb**  
      .IX Item "rgb"
      force packed \s-1RGB\s0 output
    * **gbrp**  
      .IX Item "gbrp"
      force planar \s-1RGB\s0 output
    * **auto**  
      .IX Item "auto"
      automatically pick format
      .Sp
      Default value is **yuv420**.
* **repeatlast**  
  .IX Item "repeatlast"
  See **framesync**.
* **alpha**  
  .IX Item "alpha"
  Set format of alpha of the overlaid video, it can be _straight_ or
  _premultiplied_. Default is _straight_.

The **x**, and **y** expressions can contain the following
parameters.

* **main_w, W**  
  .IX Item "main_w, W"
* **main_h, H**  
  .IX Item "main_h, H"
  The main input width and height.
* **overlay_w, w**  
  .IX Item "overlay_w, w"
* **overlay_h, h**  
  .IX Item "overlay_h, h"
  The overlay input width and height.
* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  The computed values for _x_ and _y_. They are evaluated for
  each new frame.
* **hsub**  
  .IX Item "hsub"
* **vsub**  
  .IX Item "vsub"
  horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values of the output
  format. For example for the pixel format yuv422p\*(R" _hsub_ is 2 and
  _vsub_ is 1.
* **n**  
  .IX Item "n"
  the number of input frame, starting from 0
* **pos**  
  .IX Item "pos"
  the position in the file of the input frame, \s-1NAN\s0 if unknown
* **t**  
  .IX Item "t"
  The timestamp, expressed in seconds. It's \s-1NAN\s0 if the input timestamp is unknown.

This filter also supports the **framesync** options.

Note that the _n_, _pos_, _t_ variables are available only
when evaluation is done _per frame_, and will evaluate to \s-1NAN\s0
when **eval** is set to **init**.

Be aware that frames are taken from each input video in timestamp
order, hence, if their initial timestamps differ, it is a good idea
to pass the two inputs through a _setpts=PTS-STARTPTS_ filter to
have them begin in the same zero timestamp, as the example for
the _movie_ filter does.

You can chain together more overlays but you should test the
efficiency of such approach.

_Commands_
.IX Subsection "Commands"

This filter supports the following commands:

* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  Modify the x and y of the overlay input.
  The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option.
  .Sp
  If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current
  value.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Draw the overlay at 10 pixels from the bottom right corner of the main
  video:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          overlay=main_w-overlay_w-10:main_h-overlay_h-10
  .Ve
  .Sp
  Using named options the example above becomes:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          overlay=x=main_w-overlay_w-10:y=main_h-overlay_h-10
  .Ve
* ·  
  Insert a transparent \s-1PNG\s0 logo in the bottom left corner of the input,
  using the **ffmpeg** tool with the \f(CW`-filter\_complex\*(C' option:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i input -i logo -filter_complex overlay=10:main_h-overlay_h-10\*(Aq output
  .Ve
* ·  
  Insert 2 different transparent \s-1PNG\s0 logos (second logo on bottom
  right corner) using the **ffmpeg** tool:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i input -i logo1 -i logo2 -filter_complex overlay=x=10:y=H-h-10,overlay=x=W-w-10:y=H-h-10\*(Aq output
  .Ve
* ·  
  Add a transparent color layer on top of the main video; \f(CW`WxH\*(C'
  must specify the size of the main input to the overlay filter:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          color=color=red@.3:size=WxH [over]; [in][over] overlay [out]
  .Ve
* ·  
  Play an original video and a filtered version (here with the deshake
  filter) side by side using the **ffplay** tool:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffplay input.avi -vf split[a][b]; [a]pad=iw*2:ih[src]; [b]deshake[filt]; [src][filt]overlay=w\*(Aq
  .Ve
  .Sp
  The above command is the same as:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffplay input.avi -vf split[b], pad=iw*2[src], [b]deshake, [src]overlay=w\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Make a sliding overlay appearing from the left to the right top part of the
  screen starting since time 2:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          overlay=x=if(gte(t,2), -w+(t-2)*20, NAN)\*(Aq:y=0
  .Ve
* ·  
  Compose output by putting two input videos side to side:
  .Sp
  .Vb 7
          ffmpeg -i left.avi -i right.avi -filter_complex "
          nullsrc=size=200x100 [background];
          [0:v] setpts=PTS-STARTPTS, scale=100x100 [left];
          [1:v] setpts=PTS-STARTPTS, scale=100x100 [right];
          [background][left]       overlay=shortest=1       [background+left];
          [background+left][right] overlay=shortest=1:x=100 [left+right]
          "
  .Ve
* ·  
  Mask 10-20 seconds of a video by applying the delogo filter to a section
  .Sp
  .Vb 3
          ffmpeg -i test.avi -codec:v:0 wmv2 -ar 11025 -b:v 9000k
          -vf [in]split[split_main][split_delogo];[split_delogo]trim=start=360:end=371,delogo=0:0:640:480[delogoed];[split_main][delogoed]overlay=eof_action=pass[out]\*(Aq
          masked.avi
  .Ve
* ·  
  Chain several overlays in cascade:
  .Sp
  .Vb 6
          nullsrc=s=200x200 [bg];
          testsrc=s=100x100, split=4 [in0][in1][in2][in3];
          [in0] lutrgb=r=0, [bg]   overlay=0:0     [mid0];
          [in1] lutrgb=g=0, [mid0] overlay=100:0   [mid1];
          [in2] lutrgb=b=0, [mid1] overlay=0:100   [mid2];
          [in3] null,       [mid2] overlay=100:100 [out0]
  .Ve

<a name="owdenoise"></a>

### owdenoise

.IX Subsection "owdenoise"
Apply Overcomplete Wavelet denoiser.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **depth**  
  .IX Item "depth"
  Set depth.
  .Sp
  Larger depth values will denoise lower frequency components more, but
  slow down filtering.
  .Sp
  Must be an int in the range 8-16, default is \f(CW8.
* **luma_strength, ls**  
  .IX Item "luma_strength, ls"
  Set luma strength.
  .Sp
  Must be a double value in the range 0-1000, default is \f(CW1.0.
* **chroma_strength, cs**  
  .IX Item "chroma_strength, cs"
  Set chroma strength.
  .Sp
  Must be a double value in the range 0-1000, default is \f(CW1.0.

<a name="pad"></a>

### pad

.IX Subsection "pad"
Add paddings to the input image, and place the original input at the
provided _x_, _y_ coordinates.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **width, w**  
  .IX Item "width, w"
* **height, h**  
  .IX Item "height, h"
  Specify an expression for the size of the output image with the
  paddings added. If the value for _width_ or _height_ is 0, the
  corresponding input size is used for the output.
  .Sp
  The _width_ expression can reference the value set by the
  _height_ expression, and vice versa.
  .Sp
  The default value of _width_ and _height_ is 0.
* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  Specify the offsets to place the input image at within the padded area,
  with respect to the top/left border of the output image.
  .Sp
  The _x_ expression can reference the value set by the _y_
  expression, and vice versa.
  .Sp
  The default value of _x_ and _y_ is 0.
  .Sp
  If _x_ or _y_ evaluate to a negative number, they'll be changed
  so the input image is centered on the padded area.
* **color**  
  .IX Item "color"
  Specify the color of the padded area. For the syntax of this option,
  check the Color\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils
  manual.
  .Sp
  The default value of _color_ is black\*(R".
* **eval**  
  .IX Item "eval"
  Specify when to evaluate  _width_, _height_, _x_ and _y_ expression.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **init**  
      .IX Item "init"
      Only evaluate expressions once during the filter initialization or when
      a command is processed.
    * **frame**  
      .IX Item "frame"
      Evaluate expressions for each incoming frame.
      .Sp
      Default value is **init**.
* **aspect**  
  .IX Item "aspect"
  Pad to aspect instead to a resolution.

The value for the _width_, _height_, _x_, and _y_
options are expressions containing the following constants:

* **in\_w**  
  .IX Item "in_w"
* **in\_h**  
  .IX Item "in_h"
  The input video width and height.
* **iw**  
  .IX Item "iw"
* **ih**  
  .IX Item "ih"
  These are the same as _in\_w_ and _in\_h_.
* **out\_w**  
  .IX Item "out_w"
* **out\_h**  
  .IX Item "out_h"
  The output width and height (the size of the padded area), as
  specified by the _width_ and _height_ expressions.
* **ow**  
  .IX Item "ow"
* **oh**  
  .IX Item "oh"
  These are the same as _out\_w_ and _out\_h_.
* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  The x and y offsets as specified by the _x_ and _y_
  expressions, or \s-1NAN\s0 if not yet specified.
* **a**  
  .IX Item "a"
  same as _iw_ / _ih_
* **sar**  
  .IX Item "sar"
  input sample aspect ratio
* **dar**  
  .IX Item "dar"
  input display aspect ratio, it is the same as (_iw_ / _ih_) * _sar_
* **hsub**  
  .IX Item "hsub"
* **vsub**  
  .IX Item "vsub"
  The horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values. For example for the
  pixel format yuv422p\*(R" _hsub_ is 2 and _vsub_ is 1.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Add paddings with the color violet\*(R" to the input video. The output video
  size is 640x480, and the top-left corner of the input video is placed at
  column 0, row 40
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          pad=640:480:0:40:violet
  .Ve
  .Sp
  The example above is equivalent to the following command:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          pad=width=640:height=480:x=0:y=40:color=violet
  .Ve
* ·  
  Pad the input to get an output with dimensions increased by 3/2,
  and put the input video at the center of the padded area:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          pad="3/2*iw:3/2*ih:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Pad the input to get a squared output with size equal to the maximum
  value between the input width and height, and put the input video at
  the center of the padded area:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          pad="max(iw\e,ih):ow:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Pad the input to get a final w/h ratio of 16:9:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          pad="ih*16/9:ih:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2"
  .Ve
* ·  
  In case of anamorphic video, in order to set the output display aspect
  correctly, it is necessary to use _sar_ in the expression,
  according to the relation:
  .Sp
  .Vb 2
          (ih * X / ih) * sar = output_dar
          X = output_dar / sar
  .Ve
  .Sp
  Thus the previous example needs to be modified to:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          pad="ih*16/9/sar:ih:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Double the output size and put the input video in the bottom-right
  corner of the output padded area:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          pad="2*iw:2*ih:ow-iw:oh-ih"
  .Ve

<a name="palettegen"></a>

### palettegen

.IX Subsection "palettegen"
Generate one palette for a whole video stream.

It accepts the following options:

* **max\_colors**  
  .IX Item "max_colors"
  Set the maximum number of colors to quantize in the palette.
  Note: the palette will still contain 256 colors; the unused palette entries
  will be black.
* **reserve\_transparent**  
  .IX Item "reserve_transparent"
  Create a palette of 255 colors maximum and reserve the last one for
  transparency. Reserving the transparency color is useful for \s-1GIF\s0 optimization.
  If not set, the maximum of colors in the palette will be 256. You probably want
  to disable this option for a standalone image.
  Set by default.
* **transparency\_color**  
  .IX Item "transparency_color"
  Set the color that will be used as background for transparency.
* **stats\_mode**  
  .IX Item "stats_mode"
  Set statistics mode.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **full**  
      .IX Item "full"
      Compute full frame histograms.
    * **diff**  
      .IX Item "diff"
      Compute histograms only for the part that differs from previous frame. This
      might be relevant to give more importance to the moving part of your input if
      the background is static.
    * **single**  
      .IX Item "single"
      Compute new histogram for each frame.
      .Sp
      Default value is _full_.

The filter also exports the frame metadata \f(CW`lavfi.color\_quant\_ratio\*(C'
(\f(CW`nb_color_in / nb\_color\_out\*(C') which you can use to evaluate the degree of
color quantization of the palette. This information is also visible at
_info_ logging level.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Generate a representative palette of a given video using **ffmpeg**:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i input.mkv -vf palettegen palette.png
  .Ve

<a name="paletteuse"></a>

### paletteuse

.IX Subsection "paletteuse"
Use a palette to downsample an input video stream.

The filter takes two inputs: one video stream and a palette. The palette must
be a 256 pixels image.

It accepts the following options:

* **dither**  
  .IX Item "dither"
  Select dithering mode. Available algorithms are:
    * **bayer**  
      .IX Item "bayer"
      Ordered 8x8 bayer dithering (deterministic)
    * **heckbert**  
      .IX Item "heckbert"
      Dithering as defined by Paul Heckbert in 1982 (simple error diffusion).
      Note: this dithering is sometimes considered wrong\*(R" and is included as a
      reference.
    * **floyd\_steinberg**  
      .IX Item "floyd_steinberg"
      Floyd and Steingberg dithering (error diffusion)
    * **sierra2**  
      .IX Item "sierra2"
      Frankie Sierra dithering v2 (error diffusion)
    * **sierra2\_4a**  
      .IX Item "sierra2_4a"
      Frankie Sierra dithering v2 Lite\*(R" (error diffusion)
      .Sp
      Default is _sierra2\_4a_.
* **bayer\_scale**  
  .IX Item "bayer_scale"
  When _bayer_ dithering is selected, this option defines the scale of the
  pattern (how much the crosshatch pattern is visible). A low value means more
  visible pattern for less banding, and higher value means less visible pattern
  at the cost of more banding.
  .Sp
  The option must be an integer value in the range [0,5]. Default is _2_.
* **diff\_mode**  
  .IX Item "diff_mode"
  If set, define the zone to process
    * **rectangle**  
      .IX Item "rectangle"
      Only the changing rectangle will be reprocessed. This is similar to \s-1GIF\s0
      cropping/offsetting compression mechanism. This option can be useful for speed
      if only a part of the image is changing, and has use cases such as limiting the
      scope of the error diffusal **dither** to the rectangle that bounds the
      moving scene (it leads to more deterministic output if the scene doesn't change
      much, and as a result less moving noise and better \s-1GIF\s0 compression).
      .Sp
      Default is _none_.
* **new**  
  .IX Item "new"
  Take new palette for each output frame.
* **alpha\_threshold**  
  .IX Item "alpha_threshold"
  Sets the alpha threshold for transparency. Alpha values above this threshold
  will be treated as completely opaque, and values below this threshold will be
  treated as completely transparent.
  .Sp
  The option must be an integer value in the range [0,255]. Default is _128_.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Use a palette (generated for example with **palettegen**) to encode a \s-1GIF\s0
  using **ffmpeg**:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i input.mkv -i palette.png -lavfi paletteuse output.gif
  .Ve

<a name="perspective"></a>

### perspective

.IX Subsection "perspective"
Correct perspective of video not recorded perpendicular to the screen.

A description of the accepted parameters follows.

* **x0**  
  .IX Item "x0"
* **y0**  
  .IX Item "y0"
* **x1**  
  .IX Item "x1"
* **y1**  
  .IX Item "y1"
* **x2**  
  .IX Item "x2"
* **y2**  
  .IX Item "y2"
* **x3**  
  .IX Item "x3"
* **y3**  
  .IX Item "y3"
  Set coordinates expression for top left, top right, bottom left and bottom right corners.
  Default values are \f(CW`0:0:W:0:0:H:W:H\*(C' with which perspective will remain unchanged.
  If the \f(CW`sense\*(C' option is set to \f(CW\*(C\`source\*(C', then the specified points will be sent
  to the corners of the destination. If the \f(CW`sense\*(C' option is set to \f(CW\*(C\`destination\*(C',
  then the corners of the source will be sent to the specified coordinates.
  .Sp
  The expressions can use the following variables:
    * **W**  
      .IX Item "W"
    * **H**  
      .IX Item "H"
      the width and height of video frame.
    * **in**  
      .IX Item "in"
      Input frame count.
    * **on**  
      .IX Item "on"
      Output frame count.
* **interpolation**  
  .IX Item "interpolation"
  Set interpolation for perspective correction.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **linear**  
      .IX Item "linear"
    * **cubic**  
      .IX Item "cubic"
      .Sp
      Default value is **linear**.
* **sense**  
  .IX Item "sense"
  Set interpretation of coordinate options.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **0, source**  
      .IX Item "0, source"
      Send point in the source specified by the given coordinates to
      the corners of the destination.
    * **1, destination**  
      .IX Item "1, destination"
      Send the corners of the source to the point in the destination specified
      by the given coordinates.
      .Sp
      Default value is **source**.
* **eval**  
  .IX Item "eval"
  Set when the expressions for coordinates **x0,y0,...x3,y3** are evaluated.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **init**  
      .IX Item "init"
      only evaluate expressions once during the filter initialization or
      when a command is processed
    * **frame**  
      .IX Item "frame"
      evaluate expressions for each incoming frame
      .Sp
      Default value is **init**.

<a name="phase"></a>

### phase

.IX Subsection "phase"
Delay interlaced video by one field time so that the field order changes.

The intended use is to fix \s-1PAL\s0 movies that have been captured with the
opposite field order to the film-to-video transfer.

A description of the accepted parameters follows.

* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Set phase mode.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **t**  
      .IX Item "t"
      Capture field order top-first, transfer bottom-first.
      Filter will delay the bottom field.
    * **b**  
      .IX Item "b"
      Capture field order bottom-first, transfer top-first.
      Filter will delay the top field.
    * **p**  
      .IX Item "p"
      Capture and transfer with the same field order. This mode only exists
      for the documentation of the other options to refer to, but if you
      actually select it, the filter will faithfully do nothing.
    * **a**  
      .IX Item "a"
      Capture field order determined automatically by field flags, transfer
      opposite.
      Filter selects among **t** and **b** modes on a frame by frame
      basis using field flags. If no field information is available,
      then this works just like **u**.
    * **u**  
      .IX Item "u"
      Capture unknown or varying, transfer opposite.
      Filter selects among **t** and **b** on a frame by frame basis by
      analyzing the images and selecting the alternative that produces best
      match between the fields.
    * **T**  
      .IX Item "T"
      Capture top-first, transfer unknown or varying.
      Filter selects among **t** and **p** using image analysis.
    * **B**  
      .IX Item "B"
      Capture bottom-first, transfer unknown or varying.
      Filter selects among **b** and **p** using image analysis.
    * **A**  
      .IX Item "A"
      Capture determined by field flags, transfer unknown or varying.
      Filter selects among **t**, **b** and **p** using field flags and
      image analysis. If no field information is available, then this works just
      like **U**. This is the default mode.
    * **U**  
      .IX Item "U"
      Both capture and transfer unknown or varying.
      Filter selects among **t**, **b** and **p** using image analysis only.

<a name="pixdesctest"></a>

### pixdesctest

.IX Subsection "pixdesctest"
Pixel format descriptor test filter, mainly useful for internal
testing. The output video should be equal to the input video.

For example:

.Vb 1
        format=monow, pixdesctest
.Ve

can be used to test the monowhite pixel format descriptor definition.

<a name="pixscope"></a>

### pixscope

.IX Subsection "pixscope"
Display sample values of color channels. Mainly useful for checking color
and levels. Minimum supported resolution is 640x480.

The filters accept the following options:

* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
  Set scope X position, relative offset on X axis.
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  Set scope Y position, relative offset on Y axis.
* **w**  
  .IX Item "w"
  Set scope width.
* **h**  
  .IX Item "h"
  Set scope height.
* **o**  
  .IX Item "o"
  Set window opacity. This window also holds statistics about pixel area.
* **wx**  
  .IX Item "wx"
  Set window X position, relative offset on X axis.
* **wy**  
  .IX Item "wy"
  Set window Y position, relative offset on Y axis.

<a name="pp"></a>

### pp

.IX Subsection "pp"
Enable the specified chain of postprocessing subfilters using libpostproc. This
library should be automatically selected with a \s-1GPL\s0 build (\f(CW`--enable-gpl\*(C').
Subfilters must be separated by '/' and can be disabled by prepending a '-'.
Each subfilter and some options have a short and a long name that can be used
interchangeably, i.e. dr/dering are the same.

The filters accept the following options:

* **subfilters**  
  .IX Item "subfilters"
  Set postprocessing subfilters string.

All subfilters share common options to determine their scope:

* **a/autoq**  
  .IX Item "a/autoq"
  Honor the quality commands for this subfilter.
* **c/chrom**  
  .IX Item "c/chrom"
  Do chrominance filtering, too (default).
* **y/nochrom**  
  .IX Item "y/nochrom"
  Do luminance filtering only (no chrominance).
* **n/noluma**  
  .IX Item "n/noluma"
  Do chrominance filtering only (no luminance).

These options can be appended after the subfilter name, separated by a '|'.

Available subfilters are:

* **hb/hdeblock[|difference[|flatness]]**  
  .IX Item "hb/hdeblock[|difference[|flatness]]"
  Horizontal deblocking filter
    * **difference**  
      .IX Item "difference"
      Difference factor where higher values mean more deblocking (default: \f(CW32).
    * **flatness**  
      .IX Item "flatness"
      Flatness threshold where lower values mean more deblocking (default: \f(CW39).
* **vb/vdeblock[|difference[|flatness]]**  
  .IX Item "vb/vdeblock[|difference[|flatness]]"
  Vertical deblocking filter
    * **difference**  
      .IX Item "difference"
      Difference factor where higher values mean more deblocking (default: \f(CW32).
    * **flatness**  
      .IX Item "flatness"
      Flatness threshold where lower values mean more deblocking (default: \f(CW39).
* **ha/hadeblock[|difference[|flatness]]**  
  .IX Item "ha/hadeblock[|difference[|flatness]]"
  Accurate horizontal deblocking filter
    * **difference**  
      .IX Item "difference"
      Difference factor where higher values mean more deblocking (default: \f(CW32).
    * **flatness**  
      .IX Item "flatness"
      Flatness threshold where lower values mean more deblocking (default: \f(CW39).
