      .IX Item "aybh"
      anaglyph yellow/blue half colored
      (yellow filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
    * **aybc**  
      .IX Item "aybc"
      anaglyph yellow/blue colored
      (yellow filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
    * **aybd**  
      .IX Item "aybd"
      anaglyph yellow/blue color optimized with the least squares projection of dubois
      (yellow filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
    * **ml**  
      .IX Item "ml"
      mono output (left eye only)
    * **mr**  
      .IX Item "mr"
      mono output (right eye only)
    * **chl**  
      .IX Item "chl"
      checkerboard, left eye first
    * **chr**  
      .IX Item "chr"
      checkerboard, right eye first
    * **icl**  
      .IX Item "icl"
      interleaved columns, left eye first
    * **icr**  
      .IX Item "icr"
      interleaved columns, right eye first
    * **hdmi**  
      .IX Item "hdmi"
      \s-1HDMI\s0 frame pack
      .Sp
      Default value is **arcd**.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Convert input video from side by side parallel to anaglyph yellow/blue dubois:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          stereo3d=sbsl:aybd
  .Ve
* ·  
  Convert input video from above below (left eye above, right eye below) to side by side crosseye.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          stereo3d=abl:sbsr
  .Ve

<a name="streamselect-astreamselect"></a>

### streamselect, astreamselect

.IX Subsection "streamselect, astreamselect"
Select video or audio streams.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **inputs**  
  .IX Item "inputs"
  Set number of inputs. Default is 2.
* **map**  
  .IX Item "map"
  Set input indexes to remap to outputs.

_Commands_
.IX Subsection "Commands"

The \f(CW`streamselect\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`astreamselect\*(C' filter supports the following
commands:

* **map**  
  .IX Item "map"
  Set input indexes to remap to outputs.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Select first 5 seconds 1st stream and rest of time 2nd stream:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          sendcmd=5.0 streamselect map 1\*(Aq,streamselect=inputs=2:map=0
  .Ve
* ·  
  Same as above, but for audio:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          asendcmd=5.0 astreamselect map 1\*(Aq,astreamselect=inputs=2:map=0
  .Ve

<a name="sobel"></a>

### sobel

.IX Subsection "sobel"
Apply sobel operator to input video stream.

The filter accepts the following option:

* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied.
  By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.
* **scale**  
  .IX Item "scale"
  Set value which will be multiplied with filtered result.
* **delta**  
  .IX Item "delta"
  Set value which will be added to filtered result.

<a name="spp"></a>

### spp

.IX Subsection "spp"
Apply a simple postprocessing filter that compresses and decompresses the image
at several (or - in the case of **quality** level \f(CW6 - all) shifts
and average the results.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **quality**  
  .IX Item "quality"
  Set quality. This option defines the number of levels for averaging. It accepts
  an integer in the range 0-6. If set to \f(CW0, the filter will have no
  effect. A value of \f(CW6 means the higher quality. For each increment of
  that value the speed drops by a factor of approximately 2.  Default value is
  \f(CW3.
* **qp**  
  .IX Item "qp"
  Force a constant quantization parameter. If not set, the filter will use the \s-1QP\s0
  from the video stream (if available).
* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Set thresholding mode. Available modes are:
    * **hard**  
      .IX Item "hard"
      Set hard thresholding (default).
    * **soft**  
      .IX Item "soft"
      Set soft thresholding (better de-ringing effect, but likely blurrier).
* **use\_bframe\_qp**  
  .IX Item "use_bframe_qp"
  Enable the use of the \s-1QP\s0 from the B-Frames if set to \f(CW1. Using this
  option may cause flicker since the B-Frames have often larger \s-1QP.\s0 Default is
  \f(CW0 (not enabled).

<a name="sr"></a>

### sr

.IX Subsection "sr"
Scale the input by applying one of the super-resolution methods based on
convolutional neural networks. Supported models:

* ·  
  Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Network model (\s-1SRCNN\s0).
  See &lt;**https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.00092**&gt;.
* ·  
  Efficient Sub-Pixel Convolutional Neural Network model (\s-1ESPCN\s0).
  See &lt;**https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.05158**&gt;.

Training scripts as well as scripts for model generation are provided in
the repository at &lt;**https://github.com/HighVoltageRocknRoll/sr.git**&gt;.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **dnn\_backend**  
  .IX Item "dnn_backend"
  Specify which \s-1DNN\s0 backend to use for model loading and execution. This option accepts
  the following values:
    * **native**  
      .IX Item "native"
      Native implementation of \s-1DNN\s0 loading and execution.
    * **tensorflow**  
      .IX Item "tensorflow"
      TensorFlow backend. To enable this backend you
      need to install the TensorFlow for C library (see
      &lt;**https://www.tensorflow.org/install/install\_c**&gt;) and configure FFmpeg with
      \f(CW`--enable-libtensorflow\*(C'
      .Sp
      Default value is **native**.
* **model**  
  .IX Item "model"
  Set path to model file specifying network architecture and its parameters.
  Note that different backends use different file formats. TensorFlow backend
  can load files for both formats, while native backend can load files for only
  its format.
* **scale\_factor**  
  .IX Item "scale_factor"
  Set scale factor for \s-1SRCNN\s0 model. Allowed values are \f(CW2, \f(CW3 and \f(CW4.
  Default value is \f(CW2. Scale factor is necessary for \s-1SRCNN\s0 model, because it accepts
  input upscaled using bicubic upscaling with proper scale factor.

<a name="subtitles"></a>

### subtitles

.IX Subsection "subtitles"
Draw subtitles on top of input video using the libass library.

To enable compilation of this filter you need to configure FFmpeg with
\f(CW`--enable-libass\*(C'. This filter also requires a build with libavcodec and
libavformat to convert the passed subtitles file to \s-1ASS\s0 (Advanced Substation
Alpha) subtitles format.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **filename, f**  
  .IX Item "filename, f"
  Set the filename of the subtitle file to read. It must be specified.
* **original\_size**  
  .IX Item "original_size"
  Specify the size of the original video, the video for which the \s-1ASS\s0 file
  was composed. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  Due to a misdesign in \s-1ASS\s0 aspect ratio arithmetic, this is necessary to
  correctly scale the fonts if the aspect ratio has been changed.
* **fontsdir**  
  .IX Item "fontsdir"
  Set a directory path containing fonts that can be used by the filter.
  These fonts will be used in addition to whatever the font provider uses.
* **alpha**  
  .IX Item "alpha"
  Process alpha channel, by default alpha channel is untouched.
* **charenc**  
  .IX Item "charenc"
  Set subtitles input character encoding. \f(CW`subtitles\*(C' filter only. Only
  useful if not \s-1UTF-8.\s0
* **stream_index, si**  
  .IX Item "stream_index, si"
  Set subtitles stream index. \f(CW`subtitles\*(C' filter only.
* **force\_style**  
  .IX Item "force_style"
  Override default style or script info parameters of the subtitles. It accepts a
  string containing \s-1ASS\s0 style format \f(CW`KEY=VALUE\*(C' couples separated by \*(L",\*(R".

If the first key is not specified, it is assumed that the first value
specifies the **filename**.

For example, to render the file _sub.srt_ on top of the input
video, use the command:

.Vb 1
        subtitles=sub.srt
.Ve

which is equivalent to:

.Vb 1
        subtitles=filename=sub.srt
.Ve

To render the default subtitles stream from file _video.mkv_, use:

.Vb 1
        subtitles=video.mkv
.Ve

To render the second subtitles stream from that file, use:

.Vb 1
        subtitles=video.mkv:si=1
.Ve

To make the subtitles stream from _sub.srt_ appear in 80% transparent blue
\f(CW`DejaVu Serif\*(C', use:

.Vb 1
        subtitles=sub.srt:force_style=FontName=DejaVu Serif,PrimaryColour=&HCCFF0000\*(Aq
.Ve

<a name="super2xsai"></a>

### super2xsai

.IX Subsection "super2xsai"
Scale the input by 2x and smooth using the Super2xSaI (Scale and
Interpolate) pixel art scaling algorithm.

Useful for enlarging pixel art images without reducing sharpness.

<a name="swaprect"></a>

### swaprect

.IX Subsection "swaprect"
Swap two rectangular objects in video.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **w**  
  .IX Item "w"
  Set object width.
* **h**  
  .IX Item "h"
  Set object height.
* **x1**  
  .IX Item "x1"
  Set 1st rect x coordinate.
* **y1**  
  .IX Item "y1"
  Set 1st rect y coordinate.
* **x2**  
  .IX Item "x2"
  Set 2nd rect x coordinate.
* **y2**  
  .IX Item "y2"
  Set 2nd rect y coordinate.
  .Sp
  All expressions are evaluated once for each frame.

The all options are expressions containing the following constants:

* **w**  
  .IX Item "w"
* **h**  
  .IX Item "h"
  The input width and height.
* **a**  
  .IX Item "a"
  same as _w_ / _h_
* **sar**  
  .IX Item "sar"
  input sample aspect ratio
* **dar**  
  .IX Item "dar"
  input display aspect ratio, it is the same as (_w_ / _h_) * _sar_
* **n**  
  .IX Item "n"
  The number of the input frame, starting from 0.
* **t**  
  .IX Item "t"
  The timestamp expressed in seconds. It's \s-1NAN\s0 if the input timestamp is unknown.
* **pos**  
  .IX Item "pos"
  the position in the file of the input frame, \s-1NAN\s0 if unknown

<a name="swapuv"></a>

### swapuv

.IX Subsection "swapuv"
Swap U & V plane.

<a name="telecine"></a>

### telecine

.IX Subsection "telecine"
Apply telecine process to the video.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **first\_field**  
  .IX Item "first_field"
    * **top, t**  
      .IX Item "top, t"
      top field first
    * **bottom, b**  
      .IX Item "bottom, b"
      bottom field first
      The default value is \f(CW`top\*(C'.
* **pattern**  
  .IX Item "pattern"
  A string of numbers representing the pulldown pattern you wish to apply.
  The default value is \f(CW23.

.Vb 1
        Some typical patterns:
        
        NTSC output (30i):
        27.5p: 32222
        24p: 23 (classic)
        24p: 2332 (preferred)
        20p: 33
        18p: 334
        16p: 3444
        
        PAL output (25i):
        27.5p: 12222
        24p: 222222222223 ("Euro pulldown")
        16.67p: 33
        16p: 33333334
.Ve

<a name="threshold"></a>

### threshold

.IX Subsection "threshold"
Apply threshold effect to video stream.

This filter needs four video streams to perform thresholding.
First stream is stream we are filtering.
Second stream is holding threshold values, third stream is holding min values,
and last, fourth stream is holding max values.

The filter accepts the following option:

* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied.
  By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.

For example if first stream pixel's component value is less then threshold value
of pixel component from 2nd threshold stream, third stream value will picked,
otherwise fourth stream pixel component value will be picked.

Using color source filter one can perform various types of thresholding:

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Binary threshold, using gray color as threshold:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -f lavfi -i color=black -f lavfi -i color=white -lavfi threshold output.avi
  .Ve
* ·  
  Inverted binary threshold, using gray color as threshold:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -f lavfi -i color=white -f lavfi -i color=black -lavfi threshold output.avi
  .Ve
* ·  
  Truncate binary threshold, using gray color as threshold:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -lavfi threshold output.avi
  .Ve
* ·  
  Threshold to zero, using gray color as threshold:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -f lavfi -i color=white -i 320x240.avi -lavfi threshold output.avi
  .Ve
* ·  
  Inverted threshold to zero, using gray color as threshold:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=white -lavfi threshold output.avi
  .Ve

<a name="thumbnail"></a>

### thumbnail

.IX Subsection "thumbnail"
Select the most representative frame in a given sequence of consecutive frames.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **n**  
  .IX Item "n"
  Set the frames batch size to analyze; in a set of _n_ frames, the filter
  will pick one of them, and then handle the next batch of _n_ frames until
  the end. Default is \f(CW100.

Since the filter keeps track of the whole frames sequence, a bigger _n_
value will result in a higher memory usage, so a high value is not recommended.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Extract one picture each 50 frames:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          thumbnail=50
  .Ve
* ·  
  Complete example of a thumbnail creation with **ffmpeg**:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i in.avi -vf thumbnail,scale=300:200 -frames:v 1 out.png
  .Ve

<a name="tile"></a>

### tile

.IX Subsection "tile"
Tile several successive frames together.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **layout**  
  .IX Item "layout"
  Set the grid size (i.e. the number of lines and columns). For the syntax of
  this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
* **nb\_frames**  
  .IX Item "nb_frames"
  Set the maximum number of frames to render in the given area. It must be less
  than or equal to _w_x_h_. The default value is \f(CW0, meaning all
  the area will be used.
* **margin**  
  .IX Item "margin"
  Set the outer border margin in pixels.
* **padding**  
  .IX Item "padding"
  Set the inner border thickness (i.e. the number of pixels between frames). For
  more advanced padding options (such as having different values for the edges),
  refer to the pad video filter.
* **color**  
  .IX Item "color"
  Specify the color of the unused area. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Color\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  The default value of _color_ is black\*(R".
* **overlap**  
  .IX Item "overlap"
  Set the number of frames to overlap when tiling several successive frames together.
  The value must be between \f(CW0 and _nb_frames - 1_.
* **init\_padding**  
  .IX Item "init_padding"
  Set the number of frames to initially be empty before displaying first output frame.
  This controls how soon will one get first output frame.
  The value must be between \f(CW0 and _nb_frames - 1_.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Produce 8x8 \s-1PNG\s0 tiles of all keyframes (**-skip_frame nokey**) in a movie:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -skip_frame nokey -i file.avi -vf scale=128:72,tile=8x8\*(Aq -an -vsync 0 keyframes%03d.png
  .Ve
  .Sp
  The **-vsync 0** is necessary to prevent **ffmpeg** from
  duplicating each output frame to accommodate the originally detected frame
  rate.
* ·  
  Display \f(CW5 pictures in an area of \f(CW`3x2\*(C' frames,
  with \f(CW7 pixels between them, and \f(CW2 pixels of initial margin, using
  mixed flat and named options:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          tile=3x2:nb_frames=5:padding=7:margin=2
  .Ve

<a name="tinterlace"></a>

### tinterlace

.IX Subsection "tinterlace"
Perform various types of temporal field interlacing.

Frames are counted starting from 1, so the first input frame is
considered odd.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Specify the mode of the interlacing. This option can also be specified
  as a value alone. See below for a list of values for this option.
  .Sp
  Available values are:
    * **merge, 0**  
      .IX Item "merge, 0"
      Move odd frames into the upper field, even into the lower field,
      generating a double height frame at half frame rate.
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
               ------&gt; time
              Input:
              Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
              
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              
              Output:
              11111                           33333
              22222                           44444
              11111                           33333
              22222                           44444
              11111                           33333
              22222                           44444
              11111                           33333
              22222                           44444
      .Ve
    * **drop_even, 1**  
      .IX Item "drop_even, 1"
      Only output odd frames, even frames are dropped, generating a frame with
      unchanged height at half frame rate.
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
               ------&gt; time
              Input:
              Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
              
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              
              Output:
              11111                           33333
              11111                           33333
              11111                           33333
              11111                           33333
      .Ve
    * **drop_odd, 2**  
      .IX Item "drop_odd, 2"
      Only output even frames, odd frames are dropped, generating a frame with
      unchanged height at half frame rate.
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
               ------&gt; time
              Input:
              Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
              
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              
              Output:
                              22222                           44444
                              22222                           44444
                              22222                           44444
                              22222                           44444
      .Ve
    * **pad, 3**  
      .IX Item "pad, 3"
      Expand each frame to full height, but pad alternate lines with black,
      generating a frame with double height at the same input frame rate.
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
               ------&gt; time
              Input:
              Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
              
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              
              Output:
              11111           .....           33333           .....
              .....           22222           .....           44444
              11111           .....           33333           .....
              .....           22222           .....           44444
              11111           .....           33333           .....
              .....           22222           .....           44444
              11111           .....           33333           .....
              .....           22222           .....           44444
      .Ve
    * **interleave_top, 4**  
      .IX Item "interleave_top, 4"
      Interleave the upper field from odd frames with the lower field from
      even frames, generating a frame with unchanged height at half frame rate.
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
               ------&gt; time
              Input:
              Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
              
              11111&lt;-         22222           33333&lt;-         44444
              11111           22222&lt;-         33333           44444&lt;-
              11111&lt;-         22222           33333&lt;-         44444
              11111           22222&lt;-         33333           44444&lt;-
              
              Output:
              11111                           33333
              22222                           44444
              11111                           33333
              22222                           44444
      .Ve
    * **interleave_bottom, 5**  
      .IX Item "interleave_bottom, 5"
      Interleave the lower field from odd frames with the upper field from
      even frames, generating a frame with unchanged height at half frame rate.
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
               ------&gt; time
              Input:
              Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
              
              11111           22222&lt;-         33333           44444&lt;-
              11111&lt;-         22222           33333&lt;-         44444
              11111           22222&lt;-         33333           44444&lt;-
              11111&lt;-         22222           33333&lt;-         44444
              
              Output:
              22222                           44444
              11111                           33333
              22222                           44444
              11111                           33333
      .Ve
    * **interlacex2, 6**  
      .IX Item "interlacex2, 6"
      Double frame rate with unchanged height. Frames are inserted each
      containing the second temporal field from the previous input frame and
      the first temporal field from the next input frame. This mode relies on
      the top_field_first flag. Useful for interlaced video displays with no
      field synchronisation.
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
               ------&gt; time
              Input:
              Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
              
              11111           22222           33333           44444
               11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
               11111           22222           33333           44444
              
              Output:
              11111   22222   22222   33333   33333   44444   44444
               11111   11111   22222   22222   33333   33333   44444
              11111   22222   22222   33333   33333   44444   44444
               11111   11111   22222   22222   33333   33333   44444
      .Ve
    * **mergex2, 7**  
      .IX Item "mergex2, 7"
      Move odd frames into the upper field, even into the lower field,
      generating a double height frame at same frame rate.
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
               ------&gt; time
              Input:
              Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
              
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              11111           22222           33333           44444
              
              Output:
              11111           33333           33333           55555
              22222           22222           44444           44444
              11111           33333           33333           55555
              22222           22222           44444           44444
              11111           33333           33333           55555
              22222           22222           44444           44444
              11111           33333           33333           55555
              22222           22222           44444           44444
      .Ve
      .Sp
      Numeric values are deprecated but are accepted for backward
      compatibility reasons.
      .Sp
      Default mode is \f(CW`merge\*(C'.
* **flags**  
  .IX Item "flags"
  Specify flags influencing the filter process.
  .Sp
  Available value for _flags_ is:
    * **low_pass_filter, vlfp**  
      .IX Item "low_pass_filter, vlfp"
      Enable linear vertical low-pass filtering in the filter.
      Vertical low-pass filtering is required when creating an interlaced
      destination from a progressive source which contains high-frequency
      vertical detail. Filtering will reduce interlace 'twitter' and Moire
      patterning.
    * **complex_filter, cvlfp**  
      .IX Item "complex_filter, cvlfp"
      Enable complex vertical low-pass filtering.
      This will slightly less reduce interlace 'twitter' and Moire
      patterning but better retain detail and subjective sharpness impression.
      .Sp
      Vertical low-pass filtering can only be enabled for **mode**
      _interleave\_top_ and _interleave\_bottom_.

<a name="tmix"></a>

### tmix

.IX Subsection "tmix"
Mix successive video frames.

A description of the accepted options follows.

* **frames**  
  .IX Item "frames"
  The number of successive frames to mix. If unspecified, it defaults to 3.
* **weights**  
  .IX Item "weights"
  Specify weight of each input video frame.
  Each weight is separated by space. If number of weights is smaller than
  number of _frames_ last specified weight will be used for all remaining
  unset weights.
* **scale**  
  .IX Item "scale"
  Specify scale, if it is set it will be multiplied with sum
  of each weight multiplied with pixel values to give final destination
  pixel value. By default _scale_ is auto scaled to sum of weights.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Average 7 successive frames:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          tmix=frames=7:weights="1 1 1 1 1 1 1"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Apply simple temporal convolution:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          tmix=frames=3:weights="-1 3 -1"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Similar as above but only showing temporal differences:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          tmix=frames=3:weights="-1 2 -1":scale=1
  .Ve

<a name="tonemap"></a>

### tonemap

.IX Subsection "tonemap"
Tone map colors from different dynamic ranges.

This filter expects data in single precision floating point, as it needs to
operate on (and can output) out-of-range values. Another filter, such as
**zscale**, is needed to convert the resulting frame to a usable format.

The tonemapping algorithms implemented only work on linear light, so input
data should be linearized beforehand (and possibly correctly tagged).

.Vb 1
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf zscale=transfer=linear,tonemap=clip,zscale=transfer=bt709,format=yuv420p OUTPUT
.Ve

_Options_
.IX Subsection "Options"

The filter accepts the following options.

* **tonemap**  
  .IX Item "tonemap"
  Set the tone map algorithm to use.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * _none_  
      .IX Item "none"
      Do not apply any tone map, only desaturate overbright pixels.
    * _clip_  
      .IX Item "clip"
      Hard-clip any out-of-range values. Use it for perfect color accuracy for
      in-range values, while distorting out-of-range values.
    * _linear_  
      .IX Item "linear"
      Stretch the entire reference gamut to a linear multiple of the display.
    * _gamma_  
      .IX Item "gamma"
      Fit a logarithmic transfer between the tone curves.
    * _reinhard_  
      .IX Item "reinhard"
      Preserve overall image brightness with a simple curve, using nonlinear
      contrast, which results in flattening details and degrading color accuracy.
    * _hable_  
      .IX Item "hable"
      Preserve both dark and bright details better than _reinhard_, at the cost
      of slightly darkening everything. Use it when detail preservation is more
      important than color and brightness accuracy.
    * _mobius_  
      .IX Item "mobius"
      Smoothly map out-of-range values, while retaining contrast and colors for
      in-range material as much as possible. Use it when color accuracy is more
      important than detail preservation.
      .Sp
      Default is none.
* **param**  
  .IX Item "param"
  Tune the tone mapping algorithm.
  .Sp
  This affects the following algorithms:
    * _none_  
      .IX Item "none"
      Ignored.
    * _linear_  
      .IX Item "linear"
      Specifies the scale factor to use while stretching.
      Default to 1.0.
    * _gamma_  
      .IX Item "gamma"
      Specifies the exponent of the function.
      Default to 1.8.
    * _clip_  
      .IX Item "clip"
      Specify an extra linear coefficient to multiply into the signal before clipping.
      Default to 1.0.
    * _reinhard_  
      .IX Item "reinhard"
      Specify the local contrast coefficient at the display peak.
      Default to 0.5, which means that in-gamut values will be about half as bright
      as when clipping.
    * _hable_  
      .IX Item "hable"
      Ignored.
    * _mobius_  
      .IX Item "mobius"
      Specify the transition point from linear to mobius transform. Every value
      below this point is guaranteed to be mapped 1:1. The higher the value, the
      more accurate the result will be, at the cost of losing bright details.
      Default to 0.3, which due to the steep initial slope still preserves in-range
      colors fairly accurately.
* **desat**  
  .IX Item "desat"
  Apply desaturation for highlights that exceed this level of brightness. The
  higher the parameter, the more color information will be preserved. This
  setting helps prevent unnaturally blown-out colors for super-highlights, by
  (smoothly) turning into white instead. This makes images feel more natural,
  at the cost of reducing information about out-of-range colors.
  .Sp
  The default of 2.0 is somewhat conservative and will mostly just apply to
  skies or directly sunlit surfaces. A setting of 0.0 disables this option.
  .Sp
  This option works only if the input frame has a supported color tag.
* **peak**  
  .IX Item "peak"
  Override signal/nominal/reference peak with this value. Useful when the
  embedded peak information in display metadata is not reliable or when tone
  mapping from a lower range to a higher range.

<a name="transpose"></a>

### transpose

.IX Subsection "transpose"
Transpose rows with columns in the input video and optionally flip it.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **dir**  
  .IX Item "dir"
  Specify the transposition direction.
  .Sp
  Can assume the following values:
    * **0, 4, cclock\_flip**  
      .IX Item "0, 4, cclock_flip"
      Rotate by 90 degrees counterclockwise and vertically flip (default), that is:
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
              L.R     L.l
              . . -&gt;  . .
              l.r     R.r
      .Ve
    * **1, 5, clock**  
      .IX Item "1, 5, clock"
      Rotate by 90 degrees clockwise, that is:
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
              L.R     l.L
              . . -&gt;  . .
              l.r     r.R
      .Ve
    * **2, 6, cclock**  
      .IX Item "2, 6, cclock"
      Rotate by 90 degrees counterclockwise, that is:
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
              L.R     R.r
              . . -&gt;  . .
              l.r     L.l
      .Ve
    * **3, 7, clock\_flip**  
      .IX Item "3, 7, clock_flip"
      Rotate by 90 degrees clockwise and vertically flip, that is:
      .Sp
      .Vb 3
              L.R     r.R
              . . -&gt;  . .
              l.r     l.L
      .Ve
      .Sp
      For values between 4-7, the transposition is only done if the input
      video geometry is portrait and not landscape. These values are
      deprecated, the \f(CW`passthrough\*(C' option should be used instead.
      .Sp
      Numerical values are deprecated, and should be dropped in favor of
      symbolic constants.
* **passthrough**  
  .IX Item "passthrough"
  Do not apply the transposition if the input geometry matches the one
  specified by the specified value. It accepts the following values:
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      Always apply transposition.
    * **portrait**  
      .IX Item "portrait"
      Preserve portrait geometry (when _height_ &gt;= _width_).
    * **landscape**  
      .IX Item "landscape"
      Preserve landscape geometry (when _width_ &gt;= _height_).
      .Sp
      Default value is \f(CW`none\*(C'.

For example to rotate by 90 degrees clockwise and preserve portrait
layout:

.Vb 1
        transpose=dir=1:passthrough=portrait
.Ve

The command above can also be specified as:

.Vb 1
        transpose=1:portrait
.Ve

<a name="transpose_npp"></a>

### transpose_npp

.IX Subsection "transpose_npp"
Transpose rows with columns in the input video and optionally flip it.
For more in depth examples see the **transpose** video filter, which shares mostly the same options.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **dir**  
  .IX Item "dir"
  Specify the transposition direction.
  .Sp
  Can assume the following values:
    * **cclock\_flip**  
      .IX Item "cclock_flip"
      Rotate by 90 degrees counterclockwise and vertically flip. (default)
    * **clock**  
      .IX Item "clock"
      Rotate by 90 degrees clockwise.
    * **cclock**  
      .IX Item "cclock"
      Rotate by 90 degrees counterclockwise.
    * **clock\_flip**  
      .IX Item "clock_flip"
      Rotate by 90 degrees clockwise and vertically flip.
* **passthrough**  
  .IX Item "passthrough"
  Do not apply the transposition if the input geometry matches the one
  specified by the specified value. It accepts the following values:
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      Always apply transposition. (default)
    * **portrait**  
      .IX Item "portrait"
      Preserve portrait geometry (when _height_ &gt;= _width_).
    * **landscape**  
      .IX Item "landscape"
      Preserve landscape geometry (when _width_ &gt;= _height_).

<a name="trim"></a>

### trim

.IX Subsection "trim"
Trim the input so that the output contains one continuous subpart of the input.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **start**  
  .IX Item "start"
  Specify the time of the start of the kept section, i.e. the frame with the
  timestamp _start_ will be the first frame in the output.
* **end**  
  .IX Item "end"
  Specify the time of the first frame that will be dropped, i.e. the frame
  immediately preceding the one with the timestamp _end_ will be the last
  frame in the output.
* **start\_pts**  
  .IX Item "start_pts"
  This is the same as _start_, except this option sets the start timestamp
  in timebase units instead of seconds.
* **end\_pts**  
  .IX Item "end_pts"
  This is the same as _end_, except this option sets the end timestamp
  in timebase units instead of seconds.
* **duration**  
  .IX Item "duration"
  The maximum duration of the output in seconds.
* **start\_frame**  
  .IX Item "start_frame"
  The number of the first frame that should be passed to the output.
* **end\_frame**  
  .IX Item "end_frame"
  The number of the first frame that should be dropped.

**start**, **end**, and **duration** are expressed as time
duration specifications; see
**the Time duration section in the ffmpeg-utils\|(1) manual**
for the accepted syntax.

Note that the first two sets of the start/end options and the **duration**
option look at the frame timestamp, while the _frame variants simply count the
frames that pass through the filter. Also note that this filter does not modify
the timestamps. If you wish for the output timestamps to start at zero, insert a
setpts filter after the trim filter.

If multiple start or end options are set, this filter tries to be greedy and
keep all the frames that match at least one of the specified constraints. To keep
only the part that matches all the constraints at once, chain multiple trim
filters.

The defaults are such that all the input is kept. So it is possible to set e.g.
just the end values to keep everything before the specified time.

Examples:

* ·  
  Drop everything except the second minute of input:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf trim=60:120
  .Ve
* ·  
  Keep only the first second:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf trim=duration=1
  .Ve

<a name="unpremultiply"></a>

### unpremultiply

.IX Subsection "unpremultiply"
Apply alpha unpremultiply effect to input video stream using first plane
of second stream as alpha.

Both streams must have same dimensions and same pixel format.

The filter accepts the following option:

* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied.
  By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.
  .Sp
  If the format has 1 or 2 components, then luma is bit 0.
  If the format has 3 or 4 components:
  for \s-1RGB\s0 formats bit 0 is green, bit 1 is blue and bit 2 is red;
  for \s-1YUV\s0 formats bit 0 is luma, bit 1 is chroma-U and bit 2 is chroma-V.
  If present, the alpha channel is always the last bit.
* **inplace**  
  .IX Item "inplace"
  Do not require 2nd input for processing, instead use alpha plane from input stream.

<a name="unsharp"></a>

### unsharp

.IX Subsection "unsharp"
Sharpen or blur the input video.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **luma_msize_x, lx**  
  .IX Item "luma_msize_x, lx"
  Set the luma matrix horizontal size. It must be an odd integer between
  3 and 23. The default value is 5.
* **luma_msize_y, ly**  
  .IX Item "luma_msize_y, ly"
  Set the luma matrix vertical size. It must be an odd integer between 3
  and 23. The default value is 5.
* **luma_amount, la**  
  .IX Item "luma_amount, la"
  Set the luma effect strength. It must be a floating point number, reasonable
  values lay between -1.5 and 1.5.
  .Sp
  Negative values will blur the input video, while positive values will
  sharpen it, a value of zero will disable the effect.
  .Sp
  Default value is 1.0.
* **chroma_msize_x, cx**  
  .IX Item "chroma_msize_x, cx"
  Set the chroma matrix horizontal size. It must be an odd integer
  between 3 and 23. The default value is 5.
* **chroma_msize_y, cy**  
  .IX Item "chroma_msize_y, cy"
  Set the chroma matrix vertical size. It must be an odd integer
  between 3 and 23. The default value is 5.
* **chroma_amount, ca**  
  .IX Item "chroma_amount, ca"
  Set the chroma effect strength. It must be a floating point number, reasonable
  values lay between -1.5 and 1.5.
  .Sp
  Negative values will blur the input video, while positive values will
  sharpen it, a value of zero will disable the effect.
  .Sp
  Default value is 0.0.

All parameters are optional and default to the equivalent of the
string '5:5:1.0:5:5:0.0'.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Apply strong luma sharpen effect:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          unsharp=luma_msize_x=7:luma_msize_y=7:luma_amount=2.5
  .Ve
* ·  
  Apply a strong blur of both luma and chroma parameters:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          unsharp=7:7:-2:7:7:-2
  .Ve

<a name="uspp"></a>

### uspp

.IX Subsection "uspp"
Apply ultra slow/simple postprocessing filter that compresses and decompresses
the image at several (or - in the case of **quality** level \f(CW8 - all)
shifts and average the results.

The way this differs from the behavior of spp is that uspp actually encodes &
decodes each case with libavcodec Snow, whereas spp uses a simplified intra only 8x8
\s-1DCT\s0 similar to \s-1MJPEG.\s0

The filter accepts the following options:

* **quality**  
  .IX Item "quality"
  Set quality. This option defines the number of levels for averaging. It accepts
  an integer in the range 0-8. If set to \f(CW0, the filter will have no
  effect. A value of \f(CW8 means the higher quality. For each increment of
  that value the speed drops by a factor of approximately 2.  Default value is
  \f(CW3.
* **qp**  
  .IX Item "qp"
  Force a constant quantization parameter. If not set, the filter will use the \s-1QP\s0
  from the video stream (if available).

<a name="vaguedenoiser"></a>

### vaguedenoiser

.IX Subsection "vaguedenoiser"
Apply a wavelet based denoiser.

It transforms each frame from the video input into the wavelet domain,
using Cohen-Daubechies-Feauveau 9/7. Then it applies some filtering to
the obtained coefficients. It does an inverse wavelet transform after.
Due to wavelet properties, it should give a nice smoothed result, and
reduced noise, without blurring picture features.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **threshold**  
  .IX Item "threshold"
  The filtering strength. The higher, the more filtered the video will be.
  Hard thresholding can use a higher threshold than soft thresholding
  before the video looks overfiltered. Default value is 2.
* **method**  
  .IX Item "method"
  The filtering method the filter will use.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **hard**  
      .IX Item "hard"
      All values under the threshold will be zeroed.
    * **soft**  
      .IX Item "soft"
      All values under the threshold will be zeroed. All values above will be
      reduced by the threshold.
    * **garrote**  
      .IX Item "garrote"
      Scales or nullifies coefficients - intermediary between (more) soft and
      (less) hard thresholding.
      .Sp
      Default is garrote.
* **nsteps**  
  .IX Item "nsteps"
  Number of times, the wavelet will decompose the picture. Picture can't
  be decomposed beyond a particular point (typically, 8 for a 640x480
  frame - as 2^9 = 512 &gt; 480). Valid values are integers between 1 and 32. Default value is 6.
* **percent**  
  .IX Item "percent"
  Partial of full denoising (limited coefficients shrinking), from 0 to 100. Default value is 85.
* **planes**  
  .IX Item "planes"
  A list of the planes to process. By default all planes are processed.

<a name="vectorscope"></a>

### vectorscope

.IX Subsection "vectorscope"
Display 2 color component values in the two dimensional graph (which is called
a vectorscope).

This filter accepts the following options:

* **mode, m**  
  .IX Item "mode, m"
  Set vectorscope mode.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **gray**  
      .IX Item "gray"
      Gray values are displayed on graph, higher brightness means more pixels have
      same component color value on location in graph. This is the default mode.
    * **color**  
      .IX Item "color"
      Gray values are displayed on graph. Surrounding pixels values which are not
      present in video frame are drawn in gradient of 2 color components which are
      set by option \f(CW`x\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`y\*(C'. The 3rd color component is static.
    * **color2**  
      .IX Item "color2"
      Actual color components values present in video frame are displayed on graph.
    * **color3**  
      .IX Item "color3"
      Similar as color2 but higher frequency of same values \f(CW`x\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`y\*(C'
      on graph increases value of another color component, which is luminance by
      default values of \f(CW`x\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`y\*(C'.
    * **color4**  
      .IX Item "color4"
      Actual colors present in video frame are displayed on graph. If two different
      colors map to same position on graph then color with higher value of component
      not present in graph is picked.
    * **color5**  
      .IX Item "color5"
      Gray values are displayed on graph. Similar to \f(CW`color\*(C' but with 3rd color
      component picked from radial gradient.
* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
  Set which color component will be represented on X-axis. Default is \f(CW1.
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  Set which color component will be represented on Y-axis. Default is \f(CW2.
* **intensity, i**  
  .IX Item "intensity, i"
  Set intensity, used by modes: gray, color, color3 and color5 for increasing brightness
  of color component which represents frequency of (X, Y) location in graph.
* **envelope, e**  
  .IX Item "envelope, e"
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      No envelope, this is default.
    * **instant**  
      .IX Item "instant"
      Instant envelope, even darkest single pixel will be clearly highlighted.
    * **peak**  
      .IX Item "peak"
      Hold maximum and minimum values presented in graph over time. This way you
      can still spot out of range values without constantly looking at vectorscope.
    * **peak+instant**  
      .IX Item "peak+instant"
      Peak and instant envelope combined together.
* **graticule, g**  
  .IX Item "graticule, g"
  Set what kind of graticule to draw.
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
    * **green**  
      .IX Item "green"
    * **color**  
      .IX Item "color"
* **opacity, o**  
  .IX Item "opacity, o"
  Set graticule opacity.
* **flags, f**  
  .IX Item "flags, f"
  Set graticule flags.
    * **white**  
      .IX Item "white"
      Draw graticule for white point.
    * **black**  
      .IX Item "black"
      Draw graticule for black point.
    * **name**  
      .IX Item "name"
      Draw color points short names.
* **bgopacity, b**  
  .IX Item "bgopacity, b"
  Set background opacity.
* **lthreshold, l**  
  .IX Item "lthreshold, l"
  Set low threshold for color component not represented on X or Y axis.
  Values lower than this value will be ignored. Default is 0.
  Note this value is multiplied with actual max possible value one pixel component
  can have. So for 8-bit input and low threshold value of 0.1 actual threshold
  is 0.1 * 255 = 25.
* **hthreshold, h**  
  .IX Item "hthreshold, h"
  Set high threshold for color component not represented on X or Y axis.
  Values higher than this value will be ignored. Default is 1.
  Note this value is multiplied with actual max possible value one pixel component
  can have. So for 8-bit input and high threshold value of 0.9 actual threshold
  is 0.9 * 255 = 230.
* **colorspace, c**  
  .IX Item "colorspace, c"
  Set what kind of colorspace to use when drawing graticule.
    * **auto**  
      .IX Item "auto"
    * **601**  
      .IX Item "601"
    * **709**  
      .IX Item "709"
      .Sp
      Default is auto.

<a name="vidstabdetect"></a>

### vidstabdetect

.IX Subsection "vidstabdetect"
Analyze video stabilization/deshaking. Perform pass 1 of 2, see
**vidstabtransform** for pass 2.

This filter generates a file with relative translation and rotation
transform information about subsequent frames, which is then used by
the **vidstabtransform** filter.

To enable compilation of this filter you need to configure FFmpeg with
\f(CW`--enable-libvidstab\*(C'.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **result**  
  .IX Item "result"
  Set the path to the file used to write the transforms information.
  Default value is _transforms.trf_.
* **shakiness**  
  .IX Item "shakiness"
  Set how shaky the video is and how quick the camera is. It accepts an
  integer in the range 1-10, a value of 1 means little shakiness, a
  value of 10 means strong shakiness. Default value is 5.
* **accuracy**  
  .IX Item "accuracy"
  Set the accuracy of the detection process. It must be a value in the
  range 1-15. A value of 1 means low accuracy, a value of 15 means high
  accuracy. Default value is 15.
* **stepsize**  
  .IX Item "stepsize"
  Set stepsize of the search process. The region around minimum is
  scanned with 1 pixel resolution. Default value is 6.
* **mincontrast**  
  .IX Item "mincontrast"
  Set minimum contrast. Below this value a local measurement field is
  discarded. Must be a floating point value in the range 0-1. Default
  value is 0.3.
* **tripod**  
  .IX Item "tripod"
  Set reference frame number for tripod mode.
  .Sp
  If enabled, the motion of the frames is compared to a reference frame
  in the filtered stream, identified by the specified number. The idea
  is to compensate all movements in a more-or-less static scene and keep
  the camera view absolutely still.
  .Sp
  If set to 0, it is disabled. The frames are counted starting from 1.
* **show**  
  .IX Item "show"
  Show fields and transforms in the resulting frames. It accepts an
  integer in the range 0-2. Default value is 0, which disables any
  visualization.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Use default values:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          vidstabdetect
  .Ve
* ·  
  Analyze strongly shaky movie and put the results in file
  _mytransforms.trf_:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          vidstabdetect=shakiness=10:accuracy=15:result="mytransforms.trf"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Visualize the result of internal transformations in the resulting
  video:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          vidstabdetect=show=1
  .Ve
* ·  
  Analyze a video with medium shakiness using **ffmpeg**:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i input -vf vidstabdetect=shakiness=5:show=1 dummy.avi
  .Ve

<a name="vidstabtransform"></a>

### vidstabtransform

.IX Subsection "vidstabtransform"
Video stabilization/deshaking: pass 2 of 2,
see **vidstabdetect** for pass 1.

Read a file with transform information for each frame and
apply/compensate them. Together with the **vidstabdetect**
filter this can be used to deshake videos. See also
&lt;**http://public.hronopik.de/vid.stab**&gt;. It is important to also use
the **unsharp** filter, see below.

To enable compilation of this filter you need to configure FFmpeg with
\f(CW`--enable-libvidstab\*(C'.

_Options_
.IX Subsection "Options"

* **input**  
  .IX Item "input"
  Set path to the file used to read the transforms. Default value is
  _transforms.trf_.
* **smoothing**  
  .IX Item "smoothing"
  Set the number of frames (value*2 + 1) used for lowpass filtering the
  camera movements. Default value is 10.
  .Sp
  For example a number of 10 means that 21 frames are used (10 in the
  past and 10 in the future) to smoothen the motion in the video. A
  larger value leads to a smoother video, but limits the acceleration of
  the camera (pan/tilt movements). 0 is a special case where a static
  camera is simulated.
* **optalgo**  
  .IX Item "optalgo"
  Set the camera path optimization algorithm.
  .Sp
  Accepted values are:
    * **gauss**  
      .IX Item "gauss"
      gaussian kernel low-pass filter on camera motion (default)
    * **avg**  
      .IX Item "avg"
      averaging on transformations
* **maxshift**  
  .IX Item "maxshift"
  Set maximal number of pixels to translate frames. Default value is -1,
  meaning no limit.
* **maxangle**  
  .IX Item "maxangle"
  Set maximal angle in radians (degree*PI/180) to rotate frames. Default
  value is -1, meaning no limit.
* **crop**  
  .IX Item "crop"
  Specify how to deal with borders that may be visible due to movement
  compensation.
  .Sp
  Available values are:
    * **keep**  
      .IX Item "keep"
      keep image information from previous frame (default)
    * **black**  
      .IX Item "black"
      fill the border black
* **invert**  
  .IX Item "invert"
  Invert transforms if set to 1. Default value is 0.
* **relative**  
  .IX Item "relative"
  Consider transforms as relative to previous frame if set to 1,
  absolute if set to 0. Default value is 0.
* **zoom**  
  .IX Item "zoom"
  Set percentage to zoom. A positive value will result in a zoom-in
  effect, a negative value in a zoom-out effect. Default value is 0 (no
  zoom).
* **optzoom**  
  .IX Item "optzoom"
  Set optimal zooming to avoid borders.
  .Sp
  Accepted values are:
    * **0**  
      .IX Item "0"
      disabled
    * **1**  
      .IX Item "1"
      optimal static zoom value is determined (only very strong movements
      will lead to visible borders) (default)
    * **2**  
      .IX Item "2"
      optimal adaptive zoom value is determined (no borders will be
      visible), see **zoomspeed**
      .Sp
      Note that the value given at zoom is added to the one calculated here.
* **zoomspeed**  
  .IX Item "zoomspeed"
  Set percent to zoom maximally each frame (enabled when
  **optzoom** is set to 2). Range is from 0 to 5, default value is
  0.25.
* **interpol**  
  .IX Item "interpol"
  Specify type of interpolation.
  .Sp
  Available values are:
    * **no**  
      .IX Item "no"
      no interpolation
    * **linear**  
      .IX Item "linear"
      linear only horizontal
    * **bilinear**  
      .IX Item "bilinear"
      linear in both directions (default)
    * **bicubic**  
      .IX Item "bicubic"
      cubic in both directions (slow)
* **tripod**  
  .IX Item "tripod"
  Enable virtual tripod mode if set to 1, which is equivalent to
  \f(CW`relative=0:smoothing=0\*(C'. Default value is 0.
  .Sp
  Use also \f(CW`tripod\*(C' option of **vidstabdetect**.
* **debug**  
  .IX Item "debug"
  Increase log verbosity if set to 1. Also the detected global motions
  are written to the temporary file _global\_motions.trf_. Default
  value is 0.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Use **ffmpeg** for a typical stabilization with default values:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i inp.mpeg -vf vidstabtransform,unsharp=5:5:0.8:3:3:0.4 inp_stabilized.mpeg
  .Ve
  .Sp
  Note the use of the **unsharp** filter which is always recommended.
* ·  
  Zoom in a bit more and load transform data from a given file:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          vidstabtransform=zoom=5:input="mytransforms.trf"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Smoothen the video even more:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          vidstabtransform=smoothing=30
  .Ve

<a name="vflip"></a>

### vflip

.IX Subsection "vflip"
Flip the input video vertically.

For example, to vertically flip a video with **ffmpeg**:

.Vb 1
        ffmpeg -i in.avi -vf "vflip" out.avi
.Ve

<a name="vfrdet"></a>

### vfrdet

.IX Subsection "vfrdet"
Detect variable frame rate video.

This filter tries to detect if the input is variable or constant frame rate.

At end it will output number of frames detected as having variable delta pts,
and ones with constant delta pts.
If there was frames with variable delta, than it will also show min and max delta
encountered.

<a name="vibrance"></a>

### vibrance

.IX Subsection "vibrance"
Boost or alter saturation.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **intensity**  
  .IX Item "intensity"
  Set strength of boost if positive value or strength of alter if negative value.
  Default is 0. Allowed range is from -2 to 2.
* **rbal**  
  .IX Item "rbal"
  Set the red balance. Default is 1. Allowed range is from -10 to 10.
* **gbal**  
  .IX Item "gbal"
  Set the green balance. Default is 1. Allowed range is from -10 to 10.
* **bbal**  
  .IX Item "bbal"
  Set the blue balance. Default is 1. Allowed range is from -10 to 10.
* **rlum**  
  .IX Item "rlum"
  Set the red luma coefficient.
* **glum**  
  .IX Item "glum"
  Set the green luma coefficient.
* **blum**  
  .IX Item "blum"
  Set the blue luma coefficient.

<a name="vignette"></a>

### vignette

.IX Subsection "vignette"
Make or reverse a natural vignetting effect.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **angle, a**  
  .IX Item "angle, a"
  Set lens angle expression as a number of radians.
  .Sp
  The value is clipped in the \f(CW`[0,PI/2]\*(C' range.
  .Sp
  Default value: \f(CW"PI/5"
* **x0**  
  .IX Item "x0"
* **y0**  
  .IX Item "y0"
  Set center coordinates expressions. Respectively \f(CW"w/2" and \f(CW"h/2"
  by default.
* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Set forward/backward mode.
  .Sp
  Available modes are:
    * **forward**  
      .IX Item "forward"
      The larger the distance from the central point, the darker the image becomes.
    * **backward**  
      .IX Item "backward"
      The larger the distance from the central point, the brighter the image becomes.
      This can be used to reverse a vignette effect, though there is no automatic
      detection to extract the lens **angle** and other settings (yet). It can
      also be used to create a burning effect.
      .Sp
      Default value is **forward**.
* **eval**  
  .IX Item "eval"
  Set evaluation mode for the expressions (**angle**, **x0**, **y0**).
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **init**  
      .IX Item "init"
      Evaluate expressions only once during the filter initialization.
    * **frame**  
      .IX Item "frame"
      Evaluate expressions for each incoming frame. This is way slower than the
      **init** mode since it requires all the scalers to be re-computed, but it
      allows advanced dynamic expressions.
      .Sp
      Default value is **init**.
* **dither**  
  .IX Item "dither"
  Set dithering to reduce the circular banding effects. Default is \f(CW1
  (enabled).
* **aspect**  
  .IX Item "aspect"
  Set vignette aspect. This setting allows one to adjust the shape of the vignette.
  Setting this value to the \s-1SAR\s0 of the input will make a rectangular vignetting
  following the dimensions of the video.
  .Sp
  Default is \f(CW`1/1\*(C'.

_Expressions_
.IX Subsection "Expressions"

The **alpha**, **x0** and **y0** expressions can contain the
following parameters.

* **w**  
  .IX Item "w"
* **h**  
  .IX Item "h"
  input width and height
* **n**  
  .IX Item "n"
  the number of input frame, starting from 0
* **pts**  
  .IX Item "pts"
  the \s-1PTS\s0 (Presentation TimeStamp) time of the filtered video frame, expressed in
  _\s-1TB\s0_ units, \s-1NAN\s0 if undefined
* **r**  
  .IX Item "r"
  frame rate of the input video, \s-1NAN\s0 if the input frame rate is unknown
* **t**  
  .IX Item "t"
  the \s-1PTS\s0 (Presentation TimeStamp) of the filtered video frame,
  expressed in seconds, \s-1NAN\s0 if undefined
* **tb**  
  .IX Item "tb"
  time base of the input video

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Apply simple strong vignetting effect:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          vignette=PI/4
  .Ve
* ·  
  Make a flickering vignetting:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          vignette=PI/4+random(1)*PI/50\*(Aq:eval=frame
  .Ve

<a name="vmafmotion"></a>

### vmafmotion

.IX Subsection "vmafmotion"
Obtain the average vmaf motion score of a video.
It is one of the component filters of \s-1VMAF.\s0

The obtained average motion score is printed through the logging system.

In the below example the input file _ref.mpg_ is being processed and score
is computed.

.Vb 1
        ffmpeg -i ref.mpg -lavfi vmafmotion -f null -
.Ve

<a name="vstack"></a>

### vstack

.IX Subsection "vstack"
Stack input videos vertically.

All streams must be of same pixel format and of same width.

Note that this filter is faster than using **overlay** and **pad** filter
to create same output.

The filter accept the following option:

* **inputs**  
  .IX Item "inputs"
  Set number of input streams. Default is 2.
* **shortest**  
  .IX Item "shortest"
  If set to 1, force the output to terminate when the shortest input
  terminates. Default value is 0.

<a name="w3fdif"></a>

### w3fdif

.IX Subsection "w3fdif"
Deinterlace the input video (w3fdif\*(R" stands for \*(L"Weston 3 Field
Deinterlacing Filter).

Based on the process described by Martin Weston for \s-1BBC R&D,\s0 and
implemented based on the de-interlace algorithm written by Jim
Easterbrook for \s-1BBC R&D,\s0 the Weston 3 field deinterlacing filter
uses filter coefficients calculated by \s-1BBC R&D.\s0

There are two sets of filter coefficients, so called simple\*(R":
and complex\*(R". Which set of filter coefficients is used can
be set by passing an optional parameter:

* **filter**  
  .IX Item "filter"
  Set the interlacing filter coefficients. Accepts one of the following values:
    * **simple**  
      .IX Item "simple"
      Simple filter coefficient set.
    * **complex**  
      .IX Item "complex"
      More-complex filter coefficient set.
      .Sp
      Default value is **complex**.
* **deint**  
  .IX Item "deint"
  Specify which frames to deinterlace. Accept one of the following values:
    * **all**  
      .IX Item "all"
      Deinterlace all frames,
    * **interlaced**  
      .IX Item "interlaced"
      Only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced.
      .Sp
      Default value is **all**.

<a name="waveform"></a>

### waveform

.IX Subsection "waveform"
Video waveform monitor.

The waveform monitor plots color component intensity. By default luminance
only. Each column of the waveform corresponds to a column of pixels in the
source video.

It accepts the following options:

* **mode, m**  
  .IX Item "mode, m"
  Can be either \f(CW`row\*(C', or \f(CW\*(C\`column\*(C'. Default is \f(CW\*(C\`column\*(C'.
  In row mode, the graph on the left side represents color component value 0 and
  the right side represents value = 255. In column mode, the top side represents
  color component value = 0 and bottom side represents value = 255.
* **intensity, i**  
  .IX Item "intensity, i"
  Set intensity. Smaller values are useful to find out how many values of the same
  luminance are distributed across input rows/columns.
  Default value is \f(CW0.04. Allowed range is [0, 1].
* **mirror, r**  
  .IX Item "mirror, r"
  Set mirroring mode. \f(CW0 means unmirrored, \f(CW1 means mirrored.
  In mirrored mode, higher values will be represented on the left
  side for \f(CW`row\*(C' mode and at the top for \f(CW\*(C\`column\*(C' mode. Default is
  \f(CW1 (mirrored).
* **display, d**  
  .IX Item "display, d"
  Set display mode.
  It accepts the following values:
    * **overlay**  
      .IX Item "overlay"
      Presents information identical to that in the \f(CW`parade\*(C', except
      that the graphs representing color components are superimposed directly
      over one another.
      .Sp
      This display mode makes it easier to spot relative differences or similarities
      in overlapping areas of the color components that are supposed to be identical,
      such as neutral whites, grays, or blacks.
    * **stack**  
      .IX Item "stack"
      Display separate graph for the color components side by side in
      \f(CW`row\*(C' mode or one below the other in \f(CW\*(C\`column\*(C' mode.
    * **parade**  
      .IX Item "parade"
      Display separate graph for the color components side by side in
      \f(CW`column\*(C' mode or one below the other in \f(CW\*(C\`row\*(C' mode.
      .Sp
      Using this display mode makes it easy to spot color casts in the highlights
      and shadows of an image, by comparing the contours of the top and the bottom
      graphs of each waveform. Since whites, grays, and blacks are characterized
      by exactly equal amounts of red, green, and blue, neutral areas of the picture
      should display three waveforms of roughly equal width/height. If not, the
      correction is easy to perform by making level adjustments the three waveforms.
      .Sp
      Default is \f(CW`stack\*(C'.
* **components, c**  
  .IX Item "components, c"
  Set which color components to display. Default is 1, which means only luminance
  or red color component if input is in \s-1RGB\s0 colorspace. If is set for example to
  7 it will display all 3 (if) available color components.
* **envelope, e**  
  .IX Item "envelope, e"
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      No envelope, this is default.
    * **instant**  
      .IX Item "instant"
      Instant envelope, minimum and maximum values presented in graph will be easily
      visible even with small \f(CW`step\*(C' value.
    * **peak**  
      .IX Item "peak"
      Hold minimum and maximum values presented in graph across time. This way you
      can still spot out of range values without constantly looking at waveforms.
    * **peak+instant**  
      .IX Item "peak+instant"
      Peak and instant envelope combined together.
* **filter, f**  
  .IX Item "filter, f"
    * **lowpass**  
      .IX Item "lowpass"
      No filtering, this is default.
    * **flat**  
      .IX Item "flat"
      Luma and chroma combined together.
    * **aflat**  
      .IX Item "aflat"
      Similar as above, but shows difference between blue and red chroma.
    * **xflat**  
      .IX Item "xflat"
      Similar as above, but use different colors.
    * **chroma**  
      .IX Item "chroma"
      Displays only chroma.
    * **color**  
      .IX Item "color"
      Displays actual color value on waveform.
    * **acolor**  
      .IX Item "acolor"
      Similar as above, but with luma showing frequency of chroma values.
* **graticule, g**  
  .IX Item "graticule, g"
  Set which graticule to display.
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      Do not display graticule.
    * **green**  
      .IX Item "green"
      Display green graticule showing legal broadcast ranges.
    * **orange**  
      .IX Item "orange"
      Display orange graticule showing legal broadcast ranges.
* **opacity, o**  
  .IX Item "opacity, o"
  Set graticule opacity.
* **flags, fl**  
  .IX Item "flags, fl"
  Set graticule flags.
    * **numbers**  
      .IX Item "numbers"
      Draw numbers above lines. By default enabled.
    * **dots**  
      .IX Item "dots"
      Draw dots instead of lines.
* **scale, s**  
  .IX Item "scale, s"
  Set scale used for displaying graticule.
    * **digital**  
      .IX Item "digital"
    * **millivolts**  
      .IX Item "millivolts"
    * **ire**  
      .IX Item "ire"
      .Sp
      Default is digital.
* **bgopacity, b**  
  .IX Item "bgopacity, b"
  Set background opacity.

<a name="weave-doubleweave"></a>

### weave, doubleweave

.IX Subsection "weave, doubleweave"
The \f(CW`weave\*(C' takes a field-based video input and join
each two sequential fields into single frame, producing a new double
height clip with half the frame rate and half the frame count.

The \f(CW`doubleweave\*(C' works same as \f(CW\*(C\`weave\*(C' but without
halving frame rate and frame count.

It accepts the following option:

* **first\_field**  
  .IX Item "first_field"
  Set first field. Available values are:
    * **top, t**  
      .IX Item "top, t"
      Set the frame as top-field-first.
    * **bottom, b**  
      .IX Item "bottom, b"
      Set the frame as bottom-field-first.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Interlace video using **select** and **separatefields** filter:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          separatefields,select=eq(mod(n,4),0)+eq(mod(n,4),3),weave
  .Ve

<a name="xbr"></a>

### xbr

.IX Subsection "xbr"
Apply the xBR high-quality magnification filter which is designed for pixel
art. It follows a set of edge-detection rules, see
&lt;**https://forums.libretro.com/t/xbr-algorithm-tutorial/123**&gt;.

It accepts the following option:

* **n**  
  .IX Item "n"
  Set the scaling dimension: \f(CW2 for \f(CW`2xBR\*(C', \f(CW3 for
  \f(CW`3xBR\*(C' and \f(CW4 for \f(CW\*(C\`4xBR\*(C'.
  Default is \f(CW3.

<a name="xstack"></a>

### xstack

.IX Subsection "xstack"
Stack video inputs into custom layout.

All streams must be of same pixel format.

The filter accept the following option:

* **inputs**  
  .IX Item "inputs"
  Set number of input streams. Default is 2.
* **layout**  
  .IX Item "layout"
  Specify layout of inputs.
  This option requires the desired layout configuration to be explicitly set by the user.
  This sets position of each video input in output. Each input
  is separated by '|'.
  The first number represents the column, and the second number represents the row.
  Numbers start at 0 and are separated by '_'. Optionally one can use wX and hX,
  where X is video input from which to take width or height.
  Multiple values can be used when separated by '+'. In such
  case values are summed together.
* **shortest**  
  .IX Item "shortest"
  If set to 1, force the output to terminate when the shortest input
  terminates. Default value is 0.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Display 4 inputs into 2x2 grid,
  note that if inputs are of different sizes unused gaps might appear,
  as not all of output video is used.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          xstack=inputs=4:layout=0_0|0_h0|w0_0|w0_h0
  .Ve
* ·  
  Display 4 inputs into 1x4 grid,
  note that if inputs are of different sizes unused gaps might appear,
  as not all of output video is used.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          xstack=inputs=4:layout=0_0|0_h0|0_h0+h1|0_h0+h1+h2
  .Ve
* ·  
  Display 9 inputs into 3x3 grid,
  note that if inputs are of different sizes unused gaps might appear,
  as not all of output video is used.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          xstack=inputs=9:layout=w3_0|w3_h0+h2|w3_h0|0_h4|0_0|w3+w1_0|0_h1+h2|w3+w1_h0|w3+w1_h1+h2
  .Ve

<a name="yadif"></a>

### yadif

.IX Subsection "yadif"
Deinterlace the input video (yadif\*(R" means \*(L"yet another deinterlacing
filter).

It accepts the following parameters:

* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  The interlacing mode to adopt. It accepts one of the following values:
    * **0, send\_frame**  
      .IX Item "0, send_frame"
      Output one frame for each frame.
    * **1, send\_field**  
      .IX Item "1, send_field"
      Output one frame for each field.
    * **2, send\_frame\_nospatial**  
      .IX Item "2, send_frame_nospatial"
      Like \f(CW`send\_frame\*(C', but it skips the spatial interlacing check.
    * **3, send\_field\_nospatial**  
      .IX Item "3, send_field_nospatial"
      Like \f(CW`send\_field\*(C', but it skips the spatial interlacing check.
      .Sp
      The default value is \f(CW`send\_frame\*(C'.
* **parity**  
  .IX Item "parity"
  The picture field parity assumed for the input interlaced video. It accepts one
  of the following values:
    * **0, tff**  
      .IX Item "0, tff"
      Assume the top field is first.
    * **1, bff**  
      .IX Item "1, bff"
      Assume the bottom field is first.
    * **-1, auto**  
      .IX Item "-1, auto"
      Enable automatic detection of field parity.
      .Sp
      The default value is \f(CW`auto\*(C'.
      If the interlacing is unknown or the decoder does not export this information,
      top field first will be assumed.
* **deint**  
  .IX Item "deint"
  Specify which frames to deinterlace. Accept one of the following
  values:
    * **0, all**  
      .IX Item "0, all"
      Deinterlace all frames.
    * **1, interlaced**  
      .IX Item "1, interlaced"
      Only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced.
      .Sp
      The default value is \f(CW`all\*(C'.

<a name="yadif_cuda"></a>

### yadif_cuda

.IX Subsection "yadif_cuda"
Deinterlace the input video using the **yadif** algorithm, but implemented
in \s-1CUDA\s0 so that it can work as part of a \s-1GPU\s0 accelerated pipeline with nvdec
and/or nvenc.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  The interlacing mode to adopt. It accepts one of the following values:
    * **0, send\_frame**  
      .IX Item "0, send_frame"
      Output one frame for each frame.
    * **1, send\_field**  
      .IX Item "1, send_field"
      Output one frame for each field.
    * **2, send\_frame\_nospatial**  
      .IX Item "2, send_frame_nospatial"
      Like \f(CW`send\_frame\*(C', but it skips the spatial interlacing check.
    * **3, send\_field\_nospatial**  
      .IX Item "3, send_field_nospatial"
      Like \f(CW`send\_field\*(C', but it skips the spatial interlacing check.
      .Sp
      The default value is \f(CW`send\_frame\*(C'.
* **parity**  
  .IX Item "parity"
  The picture field parity assumed for the input interlaced video. It accepts one
  of the following values:
    * **0, tff**  
      .IX Item "0, tff"
      Assume the top field is first.
    * **1, bff**  
      .IX Item "1, bff"
      Assume the bottom field is first.
    * **-1, auto**  
      .IX Item "-1, auto"
      Enable automatic detection of field parity.
      .Sp
      The default value is \f(CW`auto\*(C'.
      If the interlacing is unknown or the decoder does not export this information,
      top field first will be assumed.
* **deint**  
  .IX Item "deint"
  Specify which frames to deinterlace. Accept one of the following
  values:
    * **0, all**  
      .IX Item "0, all"
      Deinterlace all frames.
    * **1, interlaced**  
      .IX Item "1, interlaced"
      Only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced.
      .Sp
      The default value is \f(CW`all\*(C'.

<a name="zoompan"></a>

### zoompan

.IX Subsection "zoompan"
Apply Zoom & Pan effect.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **zoom, z**  
  .IX Item "zoom, z"
  Set the zoom expression. Default is 1.
* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  Set the x and y expression. Default is 0.
* **d**  
  .IX Item "d"
  Set the duration expression in number of frames.
  This sets for how many number of frames effect will last for
  single input image.
* **s**  
  .IX Item "s"
  Set the output image size, default is 'hd720'.
* **fps**  
  .IX Item "fps"
  Set the output frame rate, default is '25'.

Each expression can contain the following constants:

* **in_w, iw**  
  .IX Item "in_w, iw"
  Input width.
* **in_h, ih**  
  .IX Item "in_h, ih"
  Input height.
* **out_w, ow**  
  .IX Item "out_w, ow"
  Output width.
* **out_h, oh**  
  .IX Item "out_h, oh"
  Output height.
* **in**  
  .IX Item "in"
  Input frame count.
* **on**  
  .IX Item "on"
  Output frame count.
* **x**  
  .IX Item "x"
* **y**  
  .IX Item "y"
  Last calculated 'x' and 'y' position from 'x' and 'y' expression
  for current input frame.
* **px**  
  .IX Item "px"
* **py**  
  .IX Item "py"
  'x' and 'y' of last output frame of previous input frame or 0 when there was
  not yet such frame (first input frame).
* **zoom**  
  .IX Item "zoom"
  Last calculated zoom from 'z' expression for current input frame.
* **pzoom**  
  .IX Item "pzoom"
  Last calculated zoom of last output frame of previous input frame.
* **duration**  
  .IX Item "duration"
  Number of output frames for current input frame. Calculated from 'd' expression
  for each input frame.
* **pduration**  
  .IX Item "pduration"
  number of output frames created for previous input frame
* **a**  
  .IX Item "a"
  Rational number: input width / input height
* **sar**  
  .IX Item "sar"
  sample aspect ratio
* **dar**  
  .IX Item "dar"
  display aspect ratio

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Zoom-in up to 1.5 and pan at same time to some spot near center of picture:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          zoompan=z=min(zoom+0.0015,1.5)\*(Aq:d=700:x=\*(Aqif(gte(zoom,1.5),x,x+1/a)\*(Aq:y=\*(Aqif(gte(zoom,1.5),y,y+1)\*(Aq:s=640x360
  .Ve
* ·  
  Zoom-in up to 1.5 and pan always at center of picture:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          zoompan=z=min(zoom+0.0015,1.5)\*(Aq:d=700:x=\*(Aqiw/2-(iw/zoom/2)\*(Aq:y=\*(Aqih/2-(ih/zoom/2)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Same as above but without pausing:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          zoompan=z=min(max(zoom,pzoom)+0.0015,1.5)\*(Aq:d=1:x=\*(Aqiw/2-(iw/zoom/2)\*(Aq:y=\*(Aqih/2-(ih/zoom/2)\*(Aq
  .Ve

<a name="zscale"></a>

### zscale

.IX Subsection "zscale"
Scale (resize) the input video, using the z.lib library:
&lt;**https://github.com/sekrit-twc/zimg**&gt;. To enable compilation of this
filter, you need to configure FFmpeg with \f(CW`--enable-libzimg\*(C'.

The zscale filter forces the output display aspect ratio to be the same
as the input, by changing the output sample aspect ratio.

If the input image format is different from the format requested by
the next filter, the zscale filter will convert the input to the
requested format.

_Options_
.IX Subsection "Options"

The filter accepts the following options.

* **width, w**  
  .IX Item "width, w"
* **height, h**  
  .IX Item "height, h"
  Set the output video dimension expression. Default value is the input
  dimension.
  .Sp
  If the _width_ or _w_ value is 0, the input width is used for
  the output. If the _height_ or _h_ value is 0, the input height
  is used for the output.
  .Sp
  If one and only one of the values is -n with n &gt;= 1, the zscale filter
  will use a value that maintains the aspect ratio of the input image,
  calculated from the other specified dimension. After that it will,
  however, make sure that the calculated dimension is divisible by n and
  adjust the value if necessary.
  .Sp
  If both values are -n with n &gt;= 1, the behavior will be identical to
  both values being set to 0 as previously detailed.
  .Sp
  See below for the list of accepted constants for use in the dimension
  expression.
* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Set the video size. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
* **dither, d**  
  .IX Item "dither, d"
  Set the dither type.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * _none_  
      .IX Item "none"
    * _ordered_  
      .IX Item "ordered"
    * _random_  
      .IX Item "random"
    * _error\_diffusion_  
      .IX Item "error_diffusion"
      .Sp
      Default is none.
* **filter, f**  
  .IX Item "filter, f"
  Set the resize filter type.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * _point_  
      .IX Item "point"
    * _bilinear_  
      .IX Item "bilinear"
    * _bicubic_  
      .IX Item "bicubic"
    * _spline16_  
      .IX Item "spline16"
    * _spline36_  
      .IX Item "spline36"
    * _lanczos_  
      .IX Item "lanczos"
      .Sp
      Default is bilinear.
* **range, r**  
  .IX Item "range, r"
  Set the color range.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * _input_  
      .IX Item "input"
    * _limited_  
      .IX Item "limited"
    * _full_  
      .IX Item "full"
      .Sp
      Default is same as input.
* **primaries, p**  
  .IX Item "primaries, p"
  Set the color primaries.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * _input_  
      .IX Item "input"
    * _709_  
      .IX Item "709"
    * _unspecified_  
      .IX Item "unspecified"
    * _170m_  
      .IX Item "170m"
    * _240m_  
      .IX Item "240m"
    * _2020_  
      .IX Item "2020"
      .Sp
      Default is same as input.
* **transfer, t**  
  .IX Item "transfer, t"
  Set the transfer characteristics.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * _input_  
      .IX Item "input"
    * _709_  
      .IX Item "709"
    * _unspecified_  
      .IX Item "unspecified"
    * _601_  
      .IX Item "601"
    * _linear_  
      .IX Item "linear"
    * _2020\_10_  
      .IX Item "2020_10"
    * _2020\_12_  
      .IX Item "2020_12"
    * _smpte2084_  
      .IX Item "smpte2084"
    * _iec61966-2-1_  
      .IX Item "iec61966-2-1"
    * _arib-std-b67_  
      .IX Item "arib-std-b67"
      .Sp
      Default is same as input.
* **matrix, m**  
  .IX Item "matrix, m"
  Set the colorspace matrix.
  .Sp
  Possible value are:
    * _input_  
      .IX Item "input"
    * _709_  
      .IX Item "709"
    * _unspecified_  
      .IX Item "unspecified"
    * _470bg_  
      .IX Item "470bg"
    * _170m_  
      .IX Item "170m"
    * _2020\_ncl_  
      .IX Item "2020_ncl"
    * _2020\_cl_  
      .IX Item "2020_cl"
      .Sp
      Default is same as input.
* **rangein, rin**  
  .IX Item "rangein, rin"
  Set the input color range.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * _input_  
      .IX Item "input"
    * _limited_  
      .IX Item "limited"
    * _full_  
      .IX Item "full"
      .Sp
      Default is same as input.
* **primariesin, pin**  
  .IX Item "primariesin, pin"
  Set the input color primaries.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * _input_  
      .IX Item "input"
    * _709_  
      .IX Item "709"
    * _unspecified_  
      .IX Item "unspecified"
    * _170m_  
      .IX Item "170m"
    * _240m_  
      .IX Item "240m"
    * _2020_  
      .IX Item "2020"
      .Sp
      Default is same as input.
* **transferin, tin**  
  .IX Item "transferin, tin"
  Set the input transfer characteristics.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * _input_  
      .IX Item "input"
    * _709_  
      .IX Item "709"
    * _unspecified_  
      .IX Item "unspecified"
    * _601_  
      .IX Item "601"
    * _linear_  
      .IX Item "linear"
    * _2020\_10_  
      .IX Item "2020_10"
    * _2020\_12_  
      .IX Item "2020_12"
      .Sp
      Default is same as input.
* **matrixin, min**  
  .IX Item "matrixin, min"
  Set the input colorspace matrix.
  .Sp
  Possible value are:
    * _input_  
      .IX Item "input"
    * _709_  
      .IX Item "709"
    * _unspecified_  
      .IX Item "unspecified"
    * _470bg_  
      .IX Item "470bg"
    * _170m_  
      .IX Item "170m"
