    * _2020\_ncl_  
      .IX Item "2020_ncl"
    * _2020\_cl_  
      .IX Item "2020_cl"
* **chromal, c**  
  .IX Item "chromal, c"
  Set the output chroma location.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * _input_  
      .IX Item "input"
    * _left_  
      .IX Item "left"
    * _center_  
      .IX Item "center"
    * _topleft_  
      .IX Item "topleft"
    * _top_  
      .IX Item "top"
    * _bottomleft_  
      .IX Item "bottomleft"
    * _bottom_  
      .IX Item "bottom"
* **chromalin, cin**  
  .IX Item "chromalin, cin"
  Set the input chroma location.
  .Sp
  Possible values are:
    * _input_  
      .IX Item "input"
    * _left_  
      .IX Item "left"
    * _center_  
      .IX Item "center"
    * _topleft_  
      .IX Item "topleft"
    * _top_  
      .IX Item "top"
    * _bottomleft_  
      .IX Item "bottomleft"
    * _bottom_  
      .IX Item "bottom"
* **npl**  
  .IX Item "npl"
  Set the nominal peak luminance.

The values of the **w** and **h** options are expressions
containing the following constants:

* _in\_w_  
  .IX Item "in_w"
* _in\_h_  
  .IX Item "in_h"
  The input width and height
* _iw_  
  .IX Item "iw"
* _ih_  
  .IX Item "ih"
  These are the same as _in\_w_ and _in\_h_.
* _out\_w_  
  .IX Item "out_w"
* _out\_h_  
  .IX Item "out_h"
  The output (scaled) width and height
* _ow_  
  .IX Item "ow"
* _oh_  
  .IX Item "oh"
  These are the same as _out\_w_ and _out\_h_
* _a_  
  .IX Item "a"
  The same as _iw_ / _ih_
* _sar_  
  .IX Item "sar"
  input sample aspect ratio
* _dar_  
  .IX Item "dar"
  The input display aspect ratio. Calculated from \f(CW`(iw / ih) * sar\*(C'.
* _hsub_  
  .IX Item "hsub"
* _vsub_  
  .IX Item "vsub"
  horizontal and vertical input chroma subsample values. For example for the
  pixel format yuv422p\*(R" _hsub_ is 2 and _vsub_ is 1.
* _ohsub_  
  .IX Item "ohsub"
* _ovsub_  
  .IX Item "ovsub"
  horizontal and vertical output chroma subsample values. For example for the
  pixel format yuv422p\*(R" _hsub_ is 2 and _vsub_ is 1.

<a name="video-sources"></a>

# Video Sources

.IX Header "VIDEO SOURCES"
Below is a description of the currently available video sources.

<a name="buffer"></a>

### buffer

.IX Subsection "buffer"
Buffer video frames, and make them available to the filter chain.

This source is mainly intended for a programmatic use, in particular
through the interface defined in _libavfilter/vsrc\_buffer.h_.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **video\_size**  
  .IX Item "video_size"
  Specify the size (width and height) of the buffered video frames. For the
  syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
* **width**  
  .IX Item "width"
  The input video width.
* **height**  
  .IX Item "height"
  The input video height.
* **pix\_fmt**  
  .IX Item "pix_fmt"
  A string representing the pixel format of the buffered video frames.
  It may be a number corresponding to a pixel format, or a pixel format
  name.
* **time\_base**  
  .IX Item "time_base"
  Specify the timebase assumed by the timestamps of the buffered frames.
* **frame\_rate**  
  .IX Item "frame_rate"
  Specify the frame rate expected for the video stream.
* **pixel_aspect, sar**  
  .IX Item "pixel_aspect, sar"
  The sample (pixel) aspect ratio of the input video.
* **sws\_param**  
  .IX Item "sws_param"
  Specify the optional parameters to be used for the scale filter which
  is automatically inserted when an input change is detected in the
  input size or format.
* **hw\_frames\_ctx**  
  .IX Item "hw_frames_ctx"
  When using a hardware pixel format, this should be a reference to an
  AVHWFramesContext describing input frames.

For example:

.Vb 1
        buffer=width=320:height=240:pix_fmt=yuv410p:time_base=1/24:sar=1
.Ve

will instruct the source to accept video frames with size 320x240 and
with format yuv410p\*(R", assuming 1/24 as the timestamps timebase and
square pixels (1:1 sample aspect ratio).
Since the pixel format with name yuv410p\*(R" corresponds to the number 6
(check the enum AVPixelFormat definition in _libavutil/pixfmt.h_),
this example corresponds to:

.Vb 1
        buffer=size=320x240:pixfmt=6:time_base=1/24:pixel_aspect=1/1
.Ve

Alternatively, the options can be specified as a flat string, but this
syntax is deprecated:

_width_:_height_:_pix\_fmt_:_time\_base.num_:_time\_base.den_:_pixel\_aspect.num_:_pixel\_aspect.den_[:_sws\_param_]

<a name="cellauto"></a>

### cellauto

.IX Subsection "cellauto"
Create a pattern generated by an elementary cellular automaton.

The initial state of the cellular automaton can be defined through the
**filename** and **pattern** options. If such options are
not specified an initial state is created randomly.

At each new frame a new row in the video is filled with the result of
the cellular automaton next generation. The behavior when the whole
frame is filled is defined by the **scroll** option.

This source accepts the following options:

* **filename, f**  
  .IX Item "filename, f"
  Read the initial cellular automaton state, i.e. the starting row, from
  the specified file.
  In the file, each non-whitespace character is considered an alive
  cell, a newline will terminate the row, and further characters in the
  file will be ignored.
* **pattern, p**  
  .IX Item "pattern, p"
  Read the initial cellular automaton state, i.e. the starting row, from
  the specified string.
  .Sp
  Each non-whitespace character in the string is considered an alive
  cell, a newline will terminate the row, and further characters in the
  string will be ignored.
* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Set the video rate, that is the number of frames generated per second.
  Default is 25.
* **random_fill_ratio, ratio**  
  .IX Item "random_fill_ratio, ratio"
  Set the random fill ratio for the initial cellular automaton row. It
  is a floating point number value ranging from 0 to 1, defaults to
  1/PHI.
  .Sp
  This option is ignored when a file or a pattern is specified.
* **random_seed, seed**  
  .IX Item "random_seed, seed"
  Set the seed for filling randomly the initial row, must be an integer
  included between 0 and \s-1UINT32_MAX.\s0 If not specified, or if explicitly
  set to -1, the filter will try to use a good random seed on a best
  effort basis.
* **rule**  
  .IX Item "rule"
  Set the cellular automaton rule, it is a number ranging from 0 to 255.
  Default value is 110.
* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Set the size of the output video. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  .Sp
  If **filename** or **pattern** is specified, the size is set
  by default to the width of the specified initial state row, and the
  height is set to _width_ * \s-1PHI.\s0
  .Sp
  If **size** is set, it must contain the width of the specified
  pattern string, and the specified pattern will be centered in the
  larger row.
  .Sp
  If a filename or a pattern string is not specified, the size value
  defaults to 320x518\*(R" (used for a randomly generated initial state).
* **scroll**  
  .IX Item "scroll"
  If set to 1, scroll the output upward when all the rows in the output
  have been already filled. If set to 0, the new generated row will be
  written over the top row just after the bottom row is filled.
  Defaults to 1.
* **start_full, full**  
  .IX Item "start_full, full"
  If set to 1, completely fill the output with generated rows before
  outputting the first frame.
  This is the default behavior, for disabling set the value to 0.
* **stitch**  
  .IX Item "stitch"
  If set to 1, stitch the left and right row edges together.
  This is the default behavior, for disabling set the value to 0.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Read the initial state from _pattern_, and specify an output of
  size 200x400.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          cellauto=f=pattern:s=200x400
  .Ve
* ·  
  Generate a random initial row with a width of 200 cells, with a fill
  ratio of 2/3:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          cellauto=ratio=2/3:s=200x200
  .Ve
* ·  
  Create a pattern generated by rule 18 starting by a single alive cell
  centered on an initial row with width 100:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          cellauto=p=@s=100x400:full=0:rule=18
  .Ve
* ·  
  Specify a more elaborated initial pattern:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          cellauto=p=@@ @ @@\*(Aq:s=100x400:full=0:rule=18
  .Ve

<a name="coreimagesrc"></a>

### coreimagesrc

.IX Subsection "coreimagesrc"
Video source generated on \s-1GPU\s0 using Apple's CoreImage \s-1API\s0 on \s-1OSX.\s0

This video source is a specialized version of the **coreimage** video filter.
Use a core image generator at the beginning of the applied filterchain to
generate the content.

The coreimagesrc video source accepts the following options:

* **list\_generators**  
  .IX Item "list_generators"
  List all available generators along with all their respective options as well as
  possible minimum and maximum values along with the default values.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          list_generators=true
  .Ve
* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Specify the size of the sourced video. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  The default value is \f(CW`320x240\*(C'.
* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Specify the frame rate of the sourced video, as the number of frames
  generated per second. It has to be a string in the format
  _frame\_rate\_num_/_frame\_rate\_den_, an integer number, a floating point
  number or a valid video frame rate abbreviation. The default value is
  25\*(R".
* **sar**  
  .IX Item "sar"
  Set the sample aspect ratio of the sourced video.
* **duration, d**  
  .IX Item "duration, d"
  Set the duration of the sourced video. See
  **the Time duration section in the ffmpeg-utils\|(1) manual**
  for the accepted syntax.
  .Sp
  If not specified, or the expressed duration is negative, the video is
  supposed to be generated forever.

Additionally, all options of the **coreimage** video filter are accepted.
A complete filterchain can be used for further processing of the
generated input without CPU-HOST transfer. See **coreimage** documentation
and examples for details.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Use CIQRCodeGenerator to create a \s-1QR\s0 code for the FFmpeg homepage,
  given as complete and escaped command-line for Apple's standard bash shell:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -f lavfi -i coreimagesrc=s=100x100:filter=CIQRCodeGenerator@inputMessage=https\e\e\e\e\e://FFmpeg.org/@inputCorrectionLevel=H -frames:v 1 QRCode.png
  .Ve
  .Sp
  This example is equivalent to the QRCode example of **coreimage** without the
  need for a nullsrc video source.

<a name="mandelbrot"></a>

### mandelbrot

.IX Subsection "mandelbrot"
Generate a Mandelbrot set fractal, and progressively zoom towards the
point specified with _start\_x_ and _start\_y_.

This source accepts the following options:

* **end\_pts**  
  .IX Item "end_pts"
  Set the terminal pts value. Default value is 400.
* **end\_scale**  
  .IX Item "end_scale"
  Set the terminal scale value.
  Must be a floating point value. Default value is 0.3.
* **inner**  
  .IX Item "inner"
  Set the inner coloring mode, that is the algorithm used to draw the
  Mandelbrot fractal internal region.
  .Sp
  It shall assume one of the following values:
    * **black**  
      .IX Item "black"
      Set black mode.
    * **convergence**  
      .IX Item "convergence"
      Show time until convergence.
    * **mincol**  
      .IX Item "mincol"
      Set color based on point closest to the origin of the iterations.
    * **period**  
      .IX Item "period"
      Set period mode.
      .Sp
      Default value is _mincol_.
* **bailout**  
  .IX Item "bailout"
  Set the bailout value. Default value is 10.0.
* **maxiter**  
  .IX Item "maxiter"
  Set the maximum of iterations performed by the rendering
  algorithm. Default value is 7189.
* **outer**  
  .IX Item "outer"
  Set outer coloring mode.
  It shall assume one of following values:
    * **iteration\_count**  
      .IX Item "iteration_count"
      Set iteration cound mode.
    * **normalized\_iteration\_count**  
      .IX Item "normalized_iteration_count"
      set normalized iteration count mode.
      .Sp
      Default value is _normalized\_iteration\_count_.
* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Set frame rate, expressed as number of frames per second. Default
  value is 25\*(R".
* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Set frame size. For the syntax of this option, check the Video
  size section in the ffmpeg-utils manual. Default value is \*(L"640x480\*(R".
* **start\_scale**  
  .IX Item "start_scale"
  Set the initial scale value. Default value is 3.0.
* **start\_x**  
  .IX Item "start_x"
  Set the initial x position. Must be a floating point value between
  -100 and 100. Default value is -0.743643887037158704752191506114774.
* **start\_y**  
  .IX Item "start_y"
  Set the initial y position. Must be a floating point value between
  -100 and 100. Default value is -0.131825904205311970493132056385139.

<a name="mptestsrc"></a>

### mptestsrc

.IX Subsection "mptestsrc"
Generate various test patterns, as generated by the MPlayer test filter.

The size of the generated video is fixed, and is 256x256.
This source is useful in particular for testing encoding features.

This source accepts the following options:

* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Specify the frame rate of the sourced video, as the number of frames
  generated per second. It has to be a string in the format
  _frame\_rate\_num_/_frame\_rate\_den_, an integer number, a floating point
  number or a valid video frame rate abbreviation. The default value is
  25\*(R".
* **duration, d**  
  .IX Item "duration, d"
  Set the duration of the sourced video. See
  **the Time duration section in the ffmpeg-utils\|(1) manual**
  for the accepted syntax.
  .Sp
  If not specified, or the expressed duration is negative, the video is
  supposed to be generated forever.
* **test, t**  
  .IX Item "test, t"
  Set the number or the name of the test to perform. Supported tests are:
    * **dc\_luma**  
      .IX Item "dc_luma"
    * **dc\_chroma**  
      .IX Item "dc_chroma"
    * **freq\_luma**  
      .IX Item "freq_luma"
    * **freq\_chroma**  
      .IX Item "freq_chroma"
    * **amp\_luma**  
      .IX Item "amp_luma"
    * **amp\_chroma**  
      .IX Item "amp_chroma"
    * **cbp**  
      .IX Item "cbp"
    * **mv**  
      .IX Item "mv"
    * **ring1**  
      .IX Item "ring1"
    * **ring2**  
      .IX Item "ring2"
    * **all**  
      .IX Item "all"
      .Sp
      Default value is all\*(R", which will cycle through the list of all tests.

Some examples:

.Vb 1
        mptestsrc=t=dc_luma
.Ve

will generate a dc_luma\*(R" test pattern.

<a name="frei0r_src"></a>

### frei0r_src

.IX Subsection "frei0r_src"
Provide a frei0r source.

To enable compilation of this filter you need to install the frei0r
header and configure FFmpeg with \f(CW`--enable-frei0r\*(C'.

This source accepts the following parameters:

* **size**  
  .IX Item "size"
  The size of the video to generate. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
* **framerate**  
  .IX Item "framerate"
  The framerate of the generated video. It may be a string of the form
  _num_/_den_ or a frame rate abbreviation.
* **filter\_name**  
  .IX Item "filter_name"
  The name to the frei0r source to load. For more information regarding frei0r and
  how to set the parameters, read the **frei0r** section in the video filters
  documentation.
* **filter\_params**  
  .IX Item "filter_params"
  A '|'-separated list of parameters to pass to the frei0r source.

For example, to generate a frei0r partik0l source with size 200x200
and frame rate 10 which is overlaid on the overlay filter main input:

.Vb 1
        frei0r_src=size=200x200:framerate=10:filter_name=partik0l:filter_params=1234 [overlay]; [in][overlay] overlay
.Ve

<a name="life"></a>

### life

.IX Subsection "life"
Generate a life pattern.

This source is based on a generalization of John Conway's life game.

The sourced input represents a life grid, each pixel represents a cell
which can be in one of two possible states, alive or dead. Every cell
interacts with its eight neighbours, which are the cells that are
horizontally, vertically, or diagonally adjacent.

At each interaction the grid evolves according to the adopted rule,
which specifies the number of neighbor alive cells which will make a
cell stay alive or born. The **rule** option allows one to specify
the rule to adopt.

This source accepts the following options:

* **filename, f**  
  .IX Item "filename, f"
  Set the file from which to read the initial grid state. In the file,
  each non-whitespace character is considered an alive cell, and newline
  is used to delimit the end of each row.
  .Sp
  If this option is not specified, the initial grid is generated
  randomly.
* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Set the video rate, that is the number of frames generated per second.
  Default is 25.
* **random_fill_ratio, ratio**  
  .IX Item "random_fill_ratio, ratio"
  Set the random fill ratio for the initial random grid. It is a
  floating point number value ranging from 0 to 1, defaults to 1/PHI.
  It is ignored when a file is specified.
* **random_seed, seed**  
  .IX Item "random_seed, seed"
  Set the seed for filling the initial random grid, must be an integer
  included between 0 and \s-1UINT32_MAX.\s0 If not specified, or if explicitly
  set to -1, the filter will try to use a good random seed on a best
  effort basis.
* **rule**  
  .IX Item "rule"
  Set the life rule.
  .Sp
  A rule can be specified with a code of the kind "S_\s-1NS\s0_/B_\s-1NB\s0_",
  where _\s-1NS\s0_ and _\s-1NB\s0_ are sequences of numbers in the range 0-8,
  _\s-1NS\s0_ specifies the number of alive neighbor cells which make a
  live cell stay alive, and _\s-1NB\s0_ the number of alive neighbor cells
  which make a dead cell to become alive (i.e. to born\*(R").
  s\*(R" and \*(L"b\*(R" can be used in place of \*(L"S\*(R" and \*(L"B\*(R", respectively.
  .Sp
  Alternatively a rule can be specified by an 18-bits integer. The 9
  high order bits are used to encode the next cell state if it is alive
  for each number of neighbor alive cells, the low order bits specify
  the rule for borning\*(R" new cells. Higher order bits encode for an
  higher number of neighbor cells.
  For example the number 6153 = \f(CW`(12&lt;&lt;9)+9\*(C' specifies a stay alive
  rule of 12 and a born rule of 9, which corresponds to S23/B03\*(R".
  .Sp
  Default value is S23/B3\*(R", which is the original Conway's game of life
  rule, and will keep a cell alive if it has 2 or 3 neighbor alive
  cells, and will born a new cell if there are three alive cells around
  a dead cell.
* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Set the size of the output video. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  .Sp
  If **filename** is specified, the size is set by default to the
  same size of the input file. If **size** is set, it must contain
  the size specified in the input file, and the initial grid defined in
  that file is centered in the larger resulting area.
  .Sp
  If a filename is not specified, the size value defaults to 320x240\*(R"
  (used for a randomly generated initial grid).
* **stitch**  
  .IX Item "stitch"
  If set to 1, stitch the left and right grid edges together, and the
  top and bottom edges also. Defaults to 1.
* **mold**  
  .IX Item "mold"
  Set cell mold speed. If set, a dead cell will go from **death\_color** to
  **mold\_color** with a step of **mold**. **mold** can have a
  value from 0 to 255.
* **life\_color**  
  .IX Item "life_color"
  Set the color of living (or new born) cells.
* **death\_color**  
  .IX Item "death_color"
  Set the color of dead cells. If **mold** is set, this is the first color
  used to represent a dead cell.
* **mold\_color**  
  .IX Item "mold_color"
  Set mold color, for definitely dead and moldy cells.
  .Sp
  For the syntax of these 3 color options, check the Color\*(R" section in the
  ffmpeg-utils manual.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Read a grid from _pattern_, and center it on a grid of size
  300x300 pixels:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          life=f=pattern:s=300x300
  .Ve
* ·  
  Generate a random grid of size 200x200, with a fill ratio of 2/3:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          life=ratio=2/3:s=200x200
  .Ve
* ·  
  Specify a custom rule for evolving a randomly generated grid:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          life=rule=S14/B34
  .Ve
* ·  
  Full example with slow death effect (mold) using **ffplay**:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffplay -f lavfi life=s=300x200:mold=10:r=60:ratio=0.1:death_color=#C83232:life_color=#00ff00,scale=1200:800:flags=16
  .Ve

<a name="allrgb-allyuv-color-haldclutsrc-nullsrc-pal75bars-pal100bars-rgbtestsrc-smptebars-smptehdbars-testsrc-testsrc2-yuvtestsrc"></a>

### allrgb, allyuv, color, haldclutsrc, nullsrc, pal75bars, pal100bars, rgbtestsrc, smptebars, smptehdbars, testsrc, testsrc2, yuvtestsrc

.IX Subsection "allrgb, allyuv, color, haldclutsrc, nullsrc, pal75bars, pal100bars, rgbtestsrc, smptebars, smptehdbars, testsrc, testsrc2, yuvtestsrc"
The \f(CW`allrgb\*(C' source returns frames of size 4096x4096 of all rgb colors.

The \f(CW`allyuv\*(C' source returns frames of size 4096x4096 of all yuv colors.

The \f(CW`color\*(C' source provides an uniformly colored input.

The \f(CW`haldclutsrc\*(C' source provides an identity Hald \s-1CLUT.\s0 See also
**haldclut** filter.

The \f(CW`nullsrc\*(C' source returns unprocessed video frames. It is
mainly useful to be employed in analysis / debugging tools, or as the
source for filters which ignore the input data.

The \f(CW`pal75bars\*(C' source generates a color bars pattern, based on
\s-1EBU PAL\s0 recommendations with 75% color levels.

The \f(CW`pal100bars\*(C' source generates a color bars pattern, based on
\s-1EBU PAL\s0 recommendations with 100% color levels.

The \f(CW`rgbtestsrc\*(C' source generates an \s-1RGB\s0 test pattern useful for
detecting \s-1RGB\s0 vs \s-1BGR\s0 issues. You should see a red, green and blue
stripe from top to bottom.

The \f(CW`smptebars\*(C' source generates a color bars pattern, based on
the \s-1SMPTE\s0 Engineering Guideline \s-1EG 1-1990.\s0

The \f(CW`smptehdbars\*(C' source generates a color bars pattern, based on
the \s-1SMPTE RP 219-2002.\s0

The \f(CW`testsrc\*(C' source generates a test video pattern, showing a
color pattern, a scrolling gradient and a timestamp. This is mainly
intended for testing purposes.

The \f(CW`testsrc2\*(C' source is similar to testsrc, but supports more
pixel formats instead of just \f(CW`rgb24\*(C'. This allows using it as an
input for other tests without requiring a format conversion.

The \f(CW`yuvtestsrc\*(C' source generates an \s-1YUV\s0 test pattern. You should
see a y, cb and cr stripe from top to bottom.

The sources accept the following parameters:

* **level**  
  .IX Item "level"
  Specify the level of the Hald \s-1CLUT,\s0 only available in the \f(CW`haldclutsrc\*(C'
  source. A level of \f(CW`N\*(C' generates a picture of \f(CW\*(C\`N*N*N\*(C' by \f(CW\*(C\`N*N*N\*(C'
  pixels to be used as identity matrix for 3D lookup tables. Each component is
  coded on a \f(CW`1/(N*N)\*(C' scale.
* **color, c**  
  .IX Item "color, c"
  Specify the color of the source, only available in the \f(CW`color\*(C'
  source. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Color\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Specify the size of the sourced video. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  The default value is \f(CW`320x240\*(C'.
  .Sp
  This option is not available with the \f(CW`allrgb\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`allyuv\*(C', and
  \f(CW`haldclutsrc\*(C' filters.
* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Specify the frame rate of the sourced video, as the number of frames
  generated per second. It has to be a string in the format
  _frame\_rate\_num_/_frame\_rate\_den_, an integer number, a floating point
  number or a valid video frame rate abbreviation. The default value is
  25\*(R".
* **duration, d**  
  .IX Item "duration, d"
  Set the duration of the sourced video. See
  **the Time duration section in the ffmpeg-utils\|(1) manual**
  for the accepted syntax.
  .Sp
  If not specified, or the expressed duration is negative, the video is
  supposed to be generated forever.
* **sar**  
  .IX Item "sar"
  Set the sample aspect ratio of the sourced video.
* **alpha**  
  .IX Item "alpha"
  Specify the alpha (opacity) of the background, only available in the
  \f(CW`testsrc2\*(C' source. The value must be between 0 (fully transparent) and
  255 (fully opaque, the default).
* **decimals, n**  
  .IX Item "decimals, n"
  Set the number of decimals to show in the timestamp, only available in the
  \f(CW`testsrc\*(C' source.
  .Sp
  The displayed timestamp value will correspond to the original
  timestamp value multiplied by the power of 10 of the specified
  value. Default value is 0.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Generate a video with a duration of 5.3 seconds, with size
  176x144 and a frame rate of 10 frames per second:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          testsrc=duration=5.3:size=qcif:rate=10
  .Ve
* ·  
  The following graph description will generate a red source
  with an opacity of 0.2, with size qcif\*(R" and a frame rate of 10
  frames per second:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          color=c=red@0.2:s=qcif:r=10
  .Ve
* ·  
  If the input content is to be ignored, \f(CW`nullsrc\*(C' can be used. The
  following command generates noise in the luminance plane by employing
  the \f(CW`geq\*(C' filter:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          nullsrc=s=256x256, geq=random(1)*255:128:128
  .Ve

_Commands_
.IX Subsection "Commands"

The \f(CW`color\*(C' source supports the following commands:

* **c, color**  
  .IX Item "c, color"
  Set the color of the created image. Accepts the same syntax of the
  corresponding **color** option.

<a name="openclsrc"></a>

### openclsrc

.IX Subsection "openclsrc"
Generate video using an OpenCL program.

* **source**  
  .IX Item "source"
  OpenCL program source file.
* **kernel**  
  .IX Item "kernel"
  Kernel name in program.
* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Size of frames to generate.  This must be set.
* **format**  
  .IX Item "format"
  Pixel format to use for the generated frames.  This must be set.
* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Number of frames generated every second.  Default value is '25'.

For details of how the program loading works, see the **program\_opencl**
filter.

Example programs:

* ·  
  Generate a colour ramp by setting pixel values from the position of the pixel
  in the output image.  (Note that this will work with all pixel formats, but
  the generated output will not be the same.)
  .Sp
  .Vb 4
          _\|_kernel void ramp(_\|_write_only image2d_t dst,
                             unsigned int index)
          {
              int2 loc = (int2)(get_global_id(0), get_global_id(1));
          
              float4 val;
              val.xy = val.zw = convert_float2(loc) / convert_float2(get_image_dim(dst));
          
              write_imagef(dst, loc, val);
          }
  .Ve
* ·  
  Generate a Sierpinski carpet pattern, panning by a single pixel each frame.
  .Sp
  .Vb 4
          _\|_kernel void sierpinski_carpet(_\|_write_only image2d_t dst,
                                          unsigned int index)
          {
              int2 loc = (int2)(get_global_id(0), get_global_id(1));
          
              float4 value = 0.0f;
              int x = loc.x + index;
              int y = loc.y + index;
              while (x &gt; 0 || y &gt; 0) {
                  if (x % 3 == 1 && y % 3 == 1) {
                      value = 1.0f;
                      break;
                  }
                  x /= 3;
                  y /= 3;
              }
          
              write_imagef(dst, loc, value);
          }
  .Ve

<a name="video-sinks"></a>

# Video Sinks

.IX Header "VIDEO SINKS"
Below is a description of the currently available video sinks.

<a name="buffersink"></a>

### buffersink

.IX Subsection "buffersink"
Buffer video frames, and make them available to the end of the filter
graph.

This sink is mainly intended for programmatic use, in particular
through the interface defined in _libavfilter/buffersink.h_
or the options system.

It accepts a pointer to an AVBufferSinkContext structure, which
defines the incoming buffers' formats, to be passed as the opaque
parameter to \f(CW`avfilter\_init\_filter\*(C' for initialization.

<a name="nullsink"></a>

### nullsink

.IX Subsection "nullsink"
Null video sink: do absolutely nothing with the input video. It is
mainly useful as a template and for use in analysis / debugging
tools.

<a name="multimedia-filters"></a>

# Multimedia Filters

.IX Header "MULTIMEDIA FILTERS"
Below is a description of the currently available multimedia filters.

<a name="abitscope"></a>

### abitscope

.IX Subsection "abitscope"
Convert input audio to a video output, displaying the audio bit scope.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Set frame rate, expressed as number of frames per second. Default
  value is 25\*(R".
* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Specify the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  Default value is \f(CW`1024x256\*(C'.
* **colors**  
  .IX Item "colors"
  Specify list of colors separated by space or by '|' which will be used to
  draw channels. Unrecognized or missing colors will be replaced
  by white color.

<a name="ahistogram"></a>

### ahistogram

.IX Subsection "ahistogram"
Convert input audio to a video output, displaying the volume histogram.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **dmode**  
  .IX Item "dmode"
  Specify how histogram is calculated.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **single**  
      .IX Item "single"
      Use single histogram for all channels.
    * **separate**  
      .IX Item "separate"
      Use separate histogram for each channel.
      .Sp
      Default is \f(CW`single\*(C'.
* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Set frame rate, expressed as number of frames per second. Default
  value is 25\*(R".
* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Specify the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  Default value is \f(CW`hd720\*(C'.
* **scale**  
  .IX Item "scale"
  Set display scale.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **log**  
      .IX Item "log"
      logarithmic
    * **sqrt**  
      .IX Item "sqrt"
      square root
    * **cbrt**  
      .IX Item "cbrt"
      cubic root
    * **lin**  
      .IX Item "lin"
      linear
    * **rlog**  
      .IX Item "rlog"
      reverse logarithmic
      .Sp
      Default is \f(CW`log\*(C'.
* **ascale**  
  .IX Item "ascale"
  Set amplitude scale.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **log**  
      .IX Item "log"
      logarithmic
    * **lin**  
      .IX Item "lin"
      linear
      .Sp
      Default is \f(CW`log\*(C'.
* **acount**  
  .IX Item "acount"
  Set how much frames to accumulate in histogram.
  Defauls is 1. Setting this to -1 accumulates all frames.
* **rheight**  
  .IX Item "rheight"
  Set histogram ratio of window height.
* **slide**  
  .IX Item "slide"
  Set sonogram sliding.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **replace**  
      .IX Item "replace"
      replace old rows with new ones.
    * **scroll**  
      .IX Item "scroll"
      scroll from top to bottom.
      .Sp
      Default is \f(CW`replace\*(C'.

<a name="aphasemeter"></a>

### aphasemeter

.IX Subsection "aphasemeter"
Measures phase of input audio, which is exported as metadata \f(CW`lavfi.aphasemeter.phase\*(C',
representing mean phase of current audio frame. A video output can also be produced and is
enabled by default. The audio is passed through as first output.

Audio will be rematrixed to stereo if it has a different channel layout. Phase value is in
range \f(CW`[-1, 1]\*(C' where \f(CW\*(C\`-1\*(C' means left and right channels are completely out of phase
and \f(CW1 means channels are in phase.

The filter accepts the following options, all related to its video output:

* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Set the output frame rate. Default value is \f(CW25.
* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Set the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  Default value is \f(CW`800x400\*(C'.
* **rc**  
  .IX Item "rc"
* **gc**  
  .IX Item "gc"
* **bc**  
  .IX Item "bc"
  Specify the red, green, blue contrast. Default values are \f(CW2,
  \f(CW7 and \f(CW1.
  Allowed range is \f(CW`[0, 255]\*(C'.
* **mpc**  
  .IX Item "mpc"
  Set color which will be used for drawing median phase. If color is
  \f(CW`none\*(C' which is default, no median phase value will be drawn.
* **video**  
  .IX Item "video"
  Enable video output. Default is enabled.

<a name="avectorscope"></a>

### avectorscope

.IX Subsection "avectorscope"
Convert input audio to a video output, representing the audio vector
scope.

The filter is used to measure the difference between channels of stereo
audio stream. A monoaural signal, consisting of identical left and right
signal, results in straight vertical line. Any stereo separation is visible
as a deviation from this line, creating a Lissajous figure.
If the straight (or deviation from it) but horizontal line appears this
indicates that the left and right channels are out of phase.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **mode, m**  
  .IX Item "mode, m"
  Set the vectorscope mode.
  .Sp
  Available values are:
    * **lissajous**  
      .IX Item "lissajous"
      Lissajous rotated by 45 degrees.
    * **lissajous\_xy**  
      .IX Item "lissajous_xy"
      Same as above but not rotated.
    * **polar**  
      .IX Item "polar"
      Shape resembling half of circle.
      .Sp
      Default value is **lissajous**.
* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Set the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  Default value is \f(CW`400x400\*(C'.
* **rate, r**  
  .IX Item "rate, r"
  Set the output frame rate. Default value is \f(CW25.
* **rc**  
  .IX Item "rc"
* **gc**  
  .IX Item "gc"
* **bc**  
  .IX Item "bc"
* **ac**  
  .IX Item "ac"
  Specify the red, green, blue and alpha contrast. Default values are \f(CW40,
  \f(CW160, \f(CW80 and \f(CW255.
  Allowed range is \f(CW`[0, 255]\*(C'.
* **rf**  
  .IX Item "rf"
* **gf**  
  .IX Item "gf"
* **bf**  
  .IX Item "bf"
* **af**  
  .IX Item "af"
  Specify the red, green, blue and alpha fade. Default values are \f(CW15,
  \f(CW10, \f(CW5 and \f(CW5.
  Allowed range is \f(CW`[0, 255]\*(C'.
* **zoom**  
  .IX Item "zoom"
  Set the zoom factor. Default value is \f(CW1. Allowed range is \f(CW`[0, 10]\*(C'.
  Values lower than _1_ will auto adjust zoom factor to maximal possible value.
* **draw**  
  .IX Item "draw"
  Set the vectorscope drawing mode.
  .Sp
  Available values are:
    * **dot**  
      .IX Item "dot"
      Draw dot for each sample.
    * **line**  
      .IX Item "line"
      Draw line between previous and current sample.
      .Sp
      Default value is **dot**.
* **scale**  
  .IX Item "scale"
  Specify amplitude scale of audio samples.
  .Sp
  Available values are:
    * **lin**  
      .IX Item "lin"
      Linear.
    * **sqrt**  
      .IX Item "sqrt"
      Square root.
    * **cbrt**  
      .IX Item "cbrt"
      Cubic root.
    * **log**  
      .IX Item "log"
      Logarithmic.
* **swap**  
  .IX Item "swap"
  Swap left channel axis with right channel axis.
* **mirror**  
  .IX Item "mirror"
  Mirror axis.
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      No mirror.
    * **x**  
      .IX Item "x"
      Mirror only x axis.
    * **y**  
      .IX Item "y"
      Mirror only y axis.
    * **xy**  
      .IX Item "xy"
      Mirror both axis.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Complete example using **ffplay**:
  .Sp
  .Vb 2
          ffplay -f lavfi amovie=input.mp3, asplit [a][out1];
                       [a] avectorscope=zoom=1.3:rc=2:gc=200:bc=10:rf=1:gf=8:bf=7 [out0]
  .Ve

<a name="bench-abench"></a>

### bench, abench

.IX Subsection "bench, abench"
Benchmark part of a filtergraph.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **action**  
  .IX Item "action"
  Start or stop a timer.
  .Sp
  Available values are:
    * **start**  
      .IX Item "start"
      Get the current time, set it as frame metadata (using the key
      \f(CW`lavfi.bench.start\_time\*(C'), and forward the frame to the next filter.
    * **stop**  
      .IX Item "stop"
      Get the current time and fetch the \f(CW`lavfi.bench.start\_time\*(C' metadata from
      the input frame metadata to get the time difference. Time difference, average,
      maximum and minimum time (respectively \f(CW`t\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avg\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`max\*(C' and
      \f(CW`min\*(C') are then printed. The timestamps are expressed in seconds.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Benchmark **selectivecolor** filter:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          bench=start,selectivecolor=reds=-.2 .12 -.49,bench=stop
  .Ve

<a name="concat"></a>

### concat

.IX Subsection "concat"
Concatenate audio and video streams, joining them together one after the
other.

The filter works on segments of synchronized video and audio streams. All
segments must have the same number of streams of each type, and that will
also be the number of streams at output.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **n**  
  .IX Item "n"
  Set the number of segments. Default is 2.
* **v**  
  .IX Item "v"
  Set the number of output video streams, that is also the number of video
  streams in each segment. Default is 1.
* **a**  
  .IX Item "a"
  Set the number of output audio streams, that is also the number of audio
  streams in each segment. Default is 0.
* **unsafe**  
  .IX Item "unsafe"
  Activate unsafe mode: do not fail if segments have a different format.

The filter has _v_+_a_ outputs: first _v_ video outputs, then
_a_ audio outputs.

There are _n_x(_v_+_a_) inputs: first the inputs for the first
segment, in the same order as the outputs, then the inputs for the second
segment, etc.

Related streams do not always have exactly the same duration, for various
reasons including codec frame size or sloppy authoring. For that reason,
related synchronized streams (e.g. a video and its audio track) should be
concatenated at once. The concat filter will use the duration of the longest
stream in each segment (except the last one), and if necessary pad shorter
audio streams with silence.

For this filter to work correctly, all segments must start at timestamp 0.

All corresponding streams must have the same parameters in all segments; the
filtering system will automatically select a common pixel format for video
streams, and a common sample format, sample rate and channel layout for
audio streams, but other settings, such as resolution, must be converted
explicitly by the user.

Different frame rates are acceptable but will result in variable frame rate
at output; be sure to configure the output file to handle it.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Concatenate an opening, an episode and an ending, all in bilingual version
  (video in stream 0, audio in streams 1 and 2):
  .Sp
  .Vb 4
          ffmpeg -i opening.mkv -i episode.mkv -i ending.mkv -filter_complex \e
            [0:0] [0:1] [0:2] [1:0] [1:1] [1:2] [2:0] [2:1] [2:2]
             concat=n=3:v=1:a=2 [v] [a1] [a2] \e
            -map [v]\*(Aq -map \*(Aq[a1]\*(Aq -map \*(Aq[a2]\*(Aq output.mkv
  .Ve
* ·  
  Concatenate two parts, handling audio and video separately, using the
  (a)movie sources, and adjusting the resolution:
  .Sp
  .Vb 3
          movie=part1.mp4, scale=512:288 [v1] ; amovie=part1.mp4 [a1] ;
          movie=part2.mp4, scale=512:288 [v2] ; amovie=part2.mp4 [a2] ;
          [v1] [v2] concat [outv] ; [a1] [a2] concat=v=0:a=1 [outa]
  .Ve
  .Sp
  Note that a desync will happen at the stitch if the audio and video streams
  do not have exactly the same duration in the first file.

_Commands_
.IX Subsection "Commands"

This filter supports the following commands:

* **next**  
  .IX Item "next"
  Close the current segment and step to the next one

<a name="drawgraph-adrawgraph"></a>

### drawgraph, adrawgraph

.IX Subsection "drawgraph, adrawgraph"
Draw a graph using input video or audio metadata.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **m1**  
  .IX Item "m1"
  Set 1st frame metadata key from which metadata values will be used to draw a graph.
* **fg1**  
  .IX Item "fg1"
  Set 1st foreground color expression.
* **m2**  
  .IX Item "m2"
  Set 2nd frame metadata key from which metadata values will be used to draw a graph.
* **fg2**  
  .IX Item "fg2"
  Set 2nd foreground color expression.
* **m3**  
  .IX Item "m3"
  Set 3rd frame metadata key from which metadata values will be used to draw a graph.
* **fg3**  
  .IX Item "fg3"
  Set 3rd foreground color expression.
* **m4**  
  .IX Item "m4"
  Set 4th frame metadata key from which metadata values will be used to draw a graph.
* **fg4**  
  .IX Item "fg4"
  Set 4th foreground color expression.
* **min**  
  .IX Item "min"
  Set minimal value of metadata value.
* **max**  
  .IX Item "max"
  Set maximal value of metadata value.
* **bg**  
  .IX Item "bg"
  Set graph background color. Default is white.
* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Set graph mode.
  .Sp
  Available values for mode is:
    * **bar**  
      .IX Item "bar"
    * **dot**  
      .IX Item "dot"
    * **line**  
      .IX Item "line"
      .Sp
      Default is \f(CW`line\*(C'.
* **slide**  
  .IX Item "slide"
  Set slide mode.
  .Sp
  Available values for slide is:
    * **frame**  
      .IX Item "frame"
      Draw new frame when right border is reached.
    * **replace**  
      .IX Item "replace"
      Replace old columns with new ones.
    * **scroll**  
      .IX Item "scroll"
      Scroll from right to left.
    * **rscroll**  
      .IX Item "rscroll"
      Scroll from left to right.
    * **picture**  
      .IX Item "picture"
      Draw single picture.
      .Sp
      Default is \f(CW`frame\*(C'.
* **size**  
  .IX Item "size"
  Set size of graph video. For the syntax of this option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  The default value is \f(CW`900x256\*(C'.
  .Sp
  The foreground color expressions can use the following variables:
    * **\s-1MIN\s0**  
      .IX Item "MIN"
      Minimal value of metadata value.
    * **\s-1MAX\s0**  
      .IX Item "MAX"
      Maximal value of metadata value.
    * **\s-1VAL\s0**  
      .IX Item "VAL"
      Current metadata key value.
      .Sp
      The color is defined as 0xAABBGGRR.

Example using metadata from **signalstats** filter:

.Vb 1
        signalstats,drawgraph=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:min=0:max=255
.Ve

Example using metadata from **ebur128** filter:

.Vb 1
        ebur128=metadata=1,adrawgraph=lavfi.r128.M:min=-120:max=5
.Ve

<a name="ebur128"></a>

### ebur128

.IX Subsection "ebur128"
\s-1EBU R128\s0 scanner filter. This filter takes an audio stream as input and outputs
it unchanged. By default, it logs a message at a frequency of 10Hz with the
Momentary loudness (identified by \f(CW`M\*(C'), Short-term loudness (\f(CW\*(C\`S\*(C'),
Integrated loudness (\f(CW`I\*(C') and Loudness Range (\f(CW\*(C\`LRA\*(C').

The filter also has a video output (see the _video_ option) with a real
time graph to observe the loudness evolution. The graphic contains the logged
message mentioned above, so it is not printed anymore when this option is set,
unless the verbose logging is set. The main graphing area contains the
short-term loudness (3 seconds of analysis), and the gauge on the right is for
the momentary loudness (400 milliseconds), but can optionally be configured
to instead display short-term loudness (see _gauge_).

The green area marks a  +/- 1LU target range around the target loudness
(-23LUFS by default, unless modified through _target_).

More information about the Loudness Recommendation \s-1EBU R128\s0 on
&lt;**http://tech.ebu.ch/loudness**&gt;.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **video**  
  .IX Item "video"
  Activate the video output. The audio stream is passed unchanged whether this
  option is set or no. The video stream will be the first output stream if
  activated. Default is \f(CW0.
* **size**  
  .IX Item "size"
  Set the video size. This option is for video only. For the syntax of this
  option, check the
  **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  Default and minimum resolution is \f(CW`640x480\*(C'.
* **meter**  
  .IX Item "meter"
  Set the \s-1EBU\s0 scale meter. Default is \f(CW9. Common values are \f(CW9 and
  \f(CW18, respectively for \s-1EBU\s0 scale meter +9 and \s-1EBU\s0 scale meter +18. Any
  other integer value between this range is allowed.
* **metadata**  
  .IX Item "metadata"
  Set metadata injection. If set to \f(CW1, the audio input will be segmented
  into 100ms output frames, each of them containing various loudness information
  in metadata.  All the metadata keys are prefixed with \f(CW`lavfi.r128.\*(C'.
  .Sp
  Default is \f(CW0.
* **framelog**  
  .IX Item "framelog"
  Force the frame logging level.
  .Sp
  Available values are:
    * **info**  
      .IX Item "info"
      information logging level
    * **verbose**  
      .IX Item "verbose"
      verbose logging level
      .Sp
      By default, the logging level is set to _info_. If the **video** or
      the **metadata** options are set, it switches to _verbose_.
* **peak**  
  .IX Item "peak"
  Set peak mode(s).
  .Sp
  Available modes can be cumulated (the option is a \f(CW`flag\*(C' type). Possible
  values are:
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      Disable any peak mode (default).
    * **sample**  
      .IX Item "sample"
      Enable sample-peak mode.
      .Sp
      Simple peak mode looking for the higher sample value. It logs a message
      for sample-peak (identified by \f(CW`SPK\*(C').
    * **true**  
      .IX Item "true"
      Enable true-peak mode.
      .Sp
      If enabled, the peak lookup is done on an over-sampled version of the input
      stream for better peak accuracy. It logs a message for true-peak.
      (identified by \f(CW`TPK\*(C') and true-peak per frame (identified by \f(CW\*(C\`FTPK\*(C').
      This mode requires a build with \f(CW`libswresample\*(C'.
* **dualmono**  
  .IX Item "dualmono"
  Treat mono input files as dual mono\*(R". If a mono file is intended for playback
  on a stereo system, its \s-1EBU R128\s0 measurement will be perceptually incorrect.
  If set to \f(CW`true\*(C', this option will compensate for this effect.
  Multi-channel input files are not affected by this option.
* **panlaw**  
  .IX Item "panlaw"
  Set a specific pan law to be used for the measurement of dual mono files.
  This parameter is optional, and has a default value of -3.01dB.
* **target**  
  .IX Item "target"
  Set a specific target level (in \s-1LUFS\s0) used as relative zero in the visualization.
  This parameter is optional and has a default value of -23LUFS as specified
  by \s-1EBU R128.\s0 However, material published online may prefer a level of -16LUFS
  (e.g. for use with podcasts or video platforms).
* **gauge**  
  .IX Item "gauge"
  Set the value displayed by the gauge. Valid values are \f(CW`momentary\*(C' and s
  \f(CW`shortterm\*(C'. By default the momentary value will be used, but in certain
  scenarios it may be more useful to observe the short term value instead (e.g.
  live mixing).
* **scale**  
  .IX Item "scale"
  Sets the display scale for the loudness. Valid parameters are \f(CW`absolute\*(C'
  (in \s-1LUFS\s0) or \f(CW`relative\*(C' (\s-1LU\s0) relative to the target. This only affects the
  video output, not the summary or continuous log output.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Real-time graph using **ffplay**, with a \s-1EBU\s0 scale meter +18:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffplay -f lavfi -i "amovie=input.mp3,ebur128=video=1:meter=18 [out0][out1]"
  .Ve
* ·  
  Run an analysis with **ffmpeg**:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -nostats -i input.mp3 -filter_complex ebur128 -f null -
  .Ve

<a name="interleave-ainterleave"></a>

### interleave, ainterleave

.IX Subsection "interleave, ainterleave"
Temporally interleave frames from several inputs.

\f(CW`interleave\*(C' works with video inputs, \f(CW\*(C\`ainterleave\*(C' with audio.

These filters read frames from several inputs and send the oldest
queued frame to the output.

Input streams must have well defined, monotonically increasing frame
timestamp values.

In order to submit one frame to output, these filters need to enqueue
at least one frame for each input, so they cannot work in case one
input is not yet terminated and will not receive incoming frames.

For example consider the case when one input is a \f(CW`select\*(C' filter
which always drops input frames. The \f(CW`interleave\*(C' filter will keep
reading from that input, but it will never be able to send new frames
to output until the input sends an end-of-stream signal.

Also, depending on inputs synchronization, the filters will drop
frames in case one input receives more frames than the other ones, and
the queue is already filled.

These filters accept the following options:

* **nb_inputs, n**  
  .IX Item "nb_inputs, n"
  Set the number of different inputs, it is 2 by default.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Interleave frames belonging to different streams using **ffmpeg**:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i bambi.avi -i pr0n.mkv -filter_complex "[0:v][1:v] interleave" out.avi
  .Ve
* ·  
  Add flickering blur effect:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          select=if(gt(random(0), 0.2), 1, 2)\*(Aq:n=2 [tmp], boxblur=2:2, [tmp] interleave
  .Ve

<a name="metadata-ametadata"></a>

### metadata, ametadata

.IX Subsection "metadata, ametadata"
Manipulate frame metadata.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Set mode of operation of the filter.
  .Sp
  Can be one of the following:
    * **select**  
      .IX Item "select"
      If both \f(CW`value\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`key\*(C' is set, select frames
      which have such metadata. If only \f(CW`key\*(C' is set, select
      every frame that has such key in metadata.
    * **add**  
      .IX Item "add"
      Add new metadata \f(CW`key\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`value\*(C'. If key is already available
      do nothing.
    * **modify**  
      .IX Item "modify"
      Modify value of already present key.
    * **delete**  
      .IX Item "delete"
      If \f(CW`value\*(C' is set, delete only keys that have such value.
      Otherwise, delete key. If \f(CW`key\*(C' is not set, delete all metadata values in
      the frame.
    * **print**  
      .IX Item "print"
      Print key and its value if metadata was found. If \f(CW`key\*(C' is not set print all
      metadata values available in frame.
* **key**  
  .IX Item "key"
  Set key used with all modes. Must be set for all modes except \f(CW`print\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`delete\*(C'.
* **value**  
  .IX Item "value"
  Set metadata value which will be used. This option is mandatory for
  \f(CW`modify\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`add\*(C' mode.
* **function**  
  .IX Item "function"
  Which function to use when comparing metadata value and \f(CW`value\*(C'.
  .Sp
  Can be one of following:
    * **same\_str**  
      .IX Item "same_str"
      Values are interpreted as strings, returns true if metadata value is same as \f(CW`value\*(C'.
    * **starts\_with**  
      .IX Item "starts_with"
      Values are interpreted as strings, returns true if metadata value starts with
      the \f(CW`value\*(C' option string.
    * **less**  
      .IX Item "less"
      Values are interpreted as floats, returns true if metadata value is less than \f(CW`value\*(C'.
    * **equal**  
      .IX Item "equal"
      Values are interpreted as floats, returns true if \f(CW`value\*(C' is equal with metadata value.
    * **greater**  
      .IX Item "greater"
      Values are interpreted as floats, returns true if metadata value is greater than \f(CW`value\*(C'.
    * **expr**  
      .IX Item "expr"
      Values are interpreted as floats, returns true if expression from option \f(CW`expr\*(C'
      evaluates to true.
* **expr**  
  .IX Item "expr"
  Set expression which is used when \f(CW`function\*(C' is set to \f(CW\*(C\`expr\*(C'.
  The expression is evaluated through the eval \s-1API\s0 and can contain the following
  constants:
    * **\s-1VALUE1\s0**  
      .IX Item "VALUE1"
      Float representation of \f(CW`value\*(C' from metadata key.
    * **\s-1VALUE2\s0**  
      .IX Item "VALUE2"
      Float representation of \f(CW`value\*(C' as supplied by user in \f(CW\*(C\`value\*(C' option.
* **file**  
  .IX Item "file"
  If specified in \f(CW`print\*(C' mode, output is written to the named file. Instead of
  plain filename any writable url can be specified. Filename \`\`-'' is a shorthand
  for standard output. If \f(CW`file\*(C' option is not set, output is written to the log
  with \s-1AV_LOG_INFO\s0 loglevel.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Print all metadata values for frames with key \f(CW`lavfi.signalstats.YDIF\*(C' with values
  between 0 and 1.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          signalstats,metadata=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YDIF:value=0:function=expr:expr=between(VALUE1,0,1)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Print silencedetect output to file _metadata.txt_.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          silencedetect,ametadata=mode=print:file=metadata.txt
  .Ve
* ·  
  Direct all metadata to a pipe with file descriptor 4.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          metadata=mode=print:file=pipe\e:4\*(Aq
  .Ve

<a name="perms-aperms"></a>

### perms, aperms

.IX Subsection "perms, aperms"
Set read/write permissions for the output frames.

These filters are mainly aimed at developers to test direct path in the
following filter in the filtergraph.

The filters accept the following options:

* **mode**  
  .IX Item "mode"
  Select the permissions mode.
  .Sp
  It accepts the following values:
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      Do nothing. This is the default.
    * **ro**  
      .IX Item "ro"
      Set all the output frames read-only.
    * **rw**  
      .IX Item "rw"
      Set all the output frames directly writable.
    * **toggle**  
      .IX Item "toggle"
      Make the frame read-only if writable, and writable if read-only.
    * **random**  
      .IX Item "random"
      Set each output frame read-only or writable randomly.
* **seed**  
  .IX Item "seed"
  Set the seed for the _random_ mode, must be an integer included between
  \f(CW0 and \f(CW`UINT32\_MAX\*(C'. If not specified, or if explicitly set to
  \f(CW`-1\*(C', the filter will try to use a good random seed on a best effort
  basis.

Note: in case of auto-inserted filter between the permission filter and the
following one, the permission might not be received as expected in that
following filter. Inserting a **format** or **aformat** filter before the
perms/aperms filter can avoid this problem.

<a name="realtime-arealtime"></a>

### realtime, arealtime

.IX Subsection "realtime, arealtime"
Slow down filtering to match real time approximately.

These filters will pause the filtering for a variable amount of time to
match the output rate with the input timestamps.
They are similar to the **re** option to \f(CW`ffmpeg\*(C'.

They accept the following options:

* **limit**  
  .IX Item "limit"
  Time limit for the pauses. Any pause longer than that will be considered
  a timestamp discontinuity and reset the timer. Default is 2 seconds.

<a name="select-aselect"></a>

### select, aselect

.IX Subsection "select, aselect"
Select frames to pass in output.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **expr, e**  
  .IX Item "expr, e"
  Set expression, which is evaluated for each input frame.
  .Sp
  If the expression is evaluated to zero, the frame is discarded.
  .Sp
  If the evaluation result is negative or NaN, the frame is sent to the
  first output; otherwise it is sent to the output with index
  \f(CW`ceil(val)-1\*(C', assuming that the input index starts from 0.
  .Sp
  For example a value of \f(CW1.2 corresponds to the output with index
  \f(CW`ceil(1.2)-1 = 2-1 = 1\*(C', that is the second output.
* **outputs, n**  
  .IX Item "outputs, n"
  Set the number of outputs. The output to which to send the selected
  frame is based on the result of the evaluation. Default value is 1.

The expression can contain the following constants:

* **n**  
  .IX Item "n"
  The (sequential) number of the filtered frame, starting from 0.
* **selected\_n**  
  .IX Item "selected_n"
  The (sequential) number of the selected frame, starting from 0.
* **prev\_selected\_n**  
  .IX Item "prev_selected_n"
  The sequential number of the last selected frame. It's \s-1NAN\s0 if undefined.
* **\s-1TB\s0**  
  .IX Item "TB"
  The timebase of the input timestamps.
* **pts**  
  .IX Item "pts"
  The \s-1PTS\s0 (Presentation TimeStamp) of the filtered video frame,
  expressed in _\s-1TB\s0_ units. It's \s-1NAN\s0 if undefined.
* **t**  
  .IX Item "t"
  The \s-1PTS\s0 of the filtered video frame,
  expressed in seconds. It's \s-1NAN\s0 if undefined.
* **prev\_pts**  
  .IX Item "prev_pts"
  The \s-1PTS\s0 of the previously filtered video frame. It's \s-1NAN\s0 if undefined.
* **prev\_selected\_pts**  
  .IX Item "prev_selected_pts"
  The \s-1PTS\s0 of the last previously filtered video frame. It's \s-1NAN\s0 if undefined.
* **prev\_selected\_t**  
  .IX Item "prev_selected_t"
  The \s-1PTS\s0 of the last previously selected video frame, expressed in seconds. It's \s-1NAN\s0 if undefined.
* **start\_pts**  
  .IX Item "start_pts"
  The \s-1PTS\s0 of the first video frame in the video. It's \s-1NAN\s0 if undefined.
* **start\_t**  
  .IX Item "start_t"
  The time of the first video frame in the video. It's \s-1NAN\s0 if undefined.
* **pict\_type** _(video only)_  
  .IX Item "pict_type (video only)"
  The type of the filtered frame. It can assume one of the following
  values:
    * **I**  
      .IX Item "I"
    * **P**  
      .IX Item "P"
    * **B**  
      .IX Item "B"
    * **S**  
      .IX Item "S"
    * **\s-1SI\s0**  
      .IX Item "SI"
    * **\s-1SP\s0**  
      .IX Item "SP"
    * **\s-1BI\s0**  
      .IX Item "BI"
* **interlace\_type** _(video only)_  
  .IX Item "interlace_type (video only)"
  The frame interlace type. It can assume one of the following values:
    * **\s-1PROGRESSIVE\s0**  
      .IX Item "PROGRESSIVE"
      The frame is progressive (not interlaced).
    * **\s-1TOPFIRST\s0**  
      .IX Item "TOPFIRST"
      The frame is top-field-first.
    * **\s-1BOTTOMFIRST\s0**  
      .IX Item "BOTTOMFIRST"
      The frame is bottom-field-first.
* **consumed\_sample\_n** _(audio only)_  
  .IX Item "consumed_sample_n (audio only)"
  the number of selected samples before the current frame
* **samples\_n** _(audio only)_  
  .IX Item "samples_n (audio only)"
  the number of samples in the current frame
* **sample\_rate** _(audio only)_  
  .IX Item "sample_rate (audio only)"
  the input sample rate
* **key**  
  .IX Item "key"
  This is 1 if the filtered frame is a key-frame, 0 otherwise.
* **pos**  
  .IX Item "pos"
  the position in the file of the filtered frame, -1 if the information
  is not available (e.g. for synthetic video)
* **scene** _(video only)_  
  .IX Item "scene (video only)"
  value between 0 and 1 to indicate a new scene; a low value reflects a low
  probability for the current frame to introduce a new scene, while a higher
  value means the current frame is more likely to be one (see the example below)
* **concatdec\_select**  
  .IX Item "concatdec_select"
  The concat demuxer can select only part of a concat input file by setting an
  inpoint and an outpoint, but the output packets may not be entirely contained
  in the selected interval. By using this variable, it is possible to skip frames
  generated by the concat demuxer which are not exactly contained in the selected
  interval.
  .Sp
  This works by comparing the frame pts against the _lavf.concat.start\_time_
  and the _lavf.concat.duration_ packet metadata values which are also
  present in the decoded frames.
  .Sp
  The _concatdec\_select_ variable is -1 if the frame pts is at least
  start_time and either the duration metadata is missing or the frame pts is less
  than start_time + duration, 0 otherwise, and NaN if the start_time metadata is
  missing.
  .Sp
  That basically means that an input frame is selected if its pts is within the
  interval set by the concat demuxer.

The default value of the select expression is 1\*(R".

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Select all frames in input:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          select
  .Ve
  .Sp
  The example above is the same as:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          select=1
  .Ve
* ·  
  Skip all frames:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          select=0
  .Ve
* ·  
  Select only I-frames:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          select=eq(pict_type\e,I)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Select one frame every 100:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          select=not(mod(n\e,100))\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Select only frames contained in the 10-20 time interval:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          select=between(t\e,10\e,20)
  .Ve
* ·  
  Select only I-frames contained in the 10-20 time interval:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          select=between(t\e,10\e,20)*eq(pict_type\e,I)
  .Ve
* ·  
  Select frames with a minimum distance of 10 seconds:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          select=isnan(prev_selected_t)+gte(t-prev_selected_t\e,10)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Use aselect to select only audio frames with samples number &gt; 100:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          aselect=gt(samples_n\e,100)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Create a mosaic of the first scenes:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -i video.avi -vf select=gt(scene\e,0.4)\*(Aq,scale=160:120,tile -frames:v 1 preview.png
  .Ve
  .Sp
  Comparing _scene_ against a value between 0.3 and 0.5 is generally a sane
  choice.
* ·  
  Send even and odd frames to separate outputs, and compose them:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          select=n=2:e=mod(n, 2)+1\*(Aq [odd][even]; [odd] pad=h=2*ih [tmp]; [tmp][even] overlay=y=h
  .Ve
* ·  
  Select useful frames from an ffconcat file which is using inpoints and
  outpoints but where the source files are not intra frame only.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          ffmpeg -copyts -vsync 0 -segment_time_metadata 1 -i input.ffconcat -vf select=concatdec_select -af aselect=concatdec_select output.avi
  .Ve

<a name="sendcmd-asendcmd"></a>

### sendcmd, asendcmd

.IX Subsection "sendcmd, asendcmd"
Send commands to filters in the filtergraph.

These filters read commands to be sent to other filters in the
filtergraph.

\f(CW`sendcmd\*(C' must be inserted between two video filters,
\f(CW`asendcmd\*(C' must be inserted between two audio filters, but apart
from that they act the same way.

The specification of commands can be provided in the filter arguments
with the _commands_ option, or in a file specified by the
_filename_ option.

These filters accept the following options:

* **commands, c**  
  .IX Item "commands, c"
  Set the commands to be read and sent to the other filters.
* **filename, f**  
  .IX Item "filename, f"
  Set the filename of the commands to be read and sent to the other
  filters.

_Commands syntax_
.IX Subsection "Commands syntax"

A commands description consists of a sequence of interval
specifications, comprising a list of commands to be executed when a
particular event related to that interval occurs. The occurring event
is typically the current frame time entering or leaving a given time
interval.

An interval is specified by the following syntax:

.Vb 1
        &lt;START&gt;[-&lt;END&gt;] &lt;COMMANDS&gt;;
.Ve

The time interval is specified by the _\s-1START\s0_ and _\s-1END\s0_ times.
_\s-1END\s0_ is optional and defaults to the maximum time.

The current frame time is considered within the specified interval if
it is included in the interval [_\s-1START\s0_, _\s-1END\s0_), that is when
the time is greater or equal to _\s-1START\s0_ and is lesser than
_\s-1END\s0_.

_\s-1COMMANDS\s0_ consists of a sequence of one or more command
specifications, separated by ,\*(R", relating to that interval.  The
syntax of a command specification is given by:

.Vb 1
        [&lt;FLAGS&gt;] &lt;TARGET&gt; &lt;COMMAND&gt; &lt;ARG&gt;
.Ve

_\s-1FLAGS\s0_ is optional and specifies the type of events relating to
the time interval which enable sending the specified command, and must
be a non-null sequence of identifier flags separated by +\*(R" or \*(L"|\*(R" and
enclosed between [\*(R" and \*(L"]\*(R".

The following flags are recognized:

* **enter**  
  .IX Item "enter"
  The command is sent when the current frame timestamp enters the
  specified interval. In other words, the command is sent when the
  previous frame timestamp was not in the given interval, and the
  current is.
* **leave**  
  .IX Item "leave"
  The command is sent when the current frame timestamp leaves the
  specified interval. In other words, the command is sent when the
  previous frame timestamp was in the given interval, and the
  current is not.

If _\s-1FLAGS\s0_ is not specified, a default value of \f(CW`[enter]\*(C' is
assumed.

_\s-1TARGET\s0_ specifies the target of the command, usually the name of
the filter class or a specific filter instance name.

_\s-1COMMAND\s0_ specifies the name of the command for the target filter.

_\s-1ARG\s0_ is optional and specifies the optional list of argument for
the given _\s-1COMMAND\s0_.

Between one interval specification and another, whitespaces, or
sequences of characters starting with \f(CW`#\*(C' until the end of line,
are ignored and can be used to annotate comments.

A simplified \s-1BNF\s0 description of the commands specification syntax
follows:

.Vb 6
        &lt;COMMAND_FLAG&gt;  ::= "enter" | "leave"
        &lt;COMMAND_FLAGS&gt; ::= &lt;COMMAND_FLAG&gt; [(+|"|")&lt;COMMAND_FLAG&gt;]
        &lt;COMMAND&gt;       ::= ["[" &lt;COMMAND_FLAGS&gt; "]"] &lt;TARGET&gt; &lt;COMMAND&gt; [&lt;ARG&gt;]
        &lt;COMMANDS&gt;      ::= &lt;COMMAND&gt; [,&lt;COMMANDS&gt;]
        &lt;INTERVAL&gt;      ::= &lt;START&gt;[-&lt;END&gt;] &lt;COMMANDS&gt;
        &lt;INTERVALS&gt;     ::= &lt;INTERVAL&gt;[;&lt;INTERVALS&gt;]
.Ve

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Specify audio tempo change at second 4:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          asendcmd=c=4.0 atempo tempo 1.5\*(Aq,atempo
  .Ve
* ·  
  Target a specific filter instance:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          asendcmd=c=4.0 atempo@my tempo 1.5\*(Aq,atempo@my
  .Ve
* ·  
  Specify a list of drawtext and hue commands in a file.
  .Sp
  .Vb 3
          # show text in the interval 5-10
          5.0-10.0 [enter] drawtext reinit fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:text=hello world\*(Aq,
                   [leave] drawtext reinit fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:text=\*(Aq;
          
          # desaturate the image in the interval 15-20
          15.0-20.0 [enter] hue s 0,
                    [enter] drawtext reinit fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:text=nocolor\*(Aq,
                    [leave] hue s 1,
                    [leave] drawtext reinit fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:text=color\*(Aq;
          
          # apply an exponential saturation fade-out effect, starting from time 25
          25 [enter] hue s exp(25-t)
  .Ve
  .Sp
  A filtergraph allowing to read and process the above command list
  stored in a file _test.cmd_, can be specified with:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          sendcmd=f=test.cmd,drawtext=fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:text=\*(Aq,hue
  .Ve

<a name="setpts-asetpts"></a>

### setpts, asetpts

.IX Subsection "setpts, asetpts"
Change the \s-1PTS\s0 (presentation timestamp) of the input frames.

\f(CW`setpts\*(C' works on video frames, \f(CW\*(C\`asetpts\*(C' on audio frames.

This filter accepts the following options:

* **expr**  
  .IX Item "expr"
  The expression which is evaluated for each frame to construct its timestamp.

The expression is evaluated through the eval \s-1API\s0 and can contain the following
constants:

* **\s-1FRAME_RATE, FR\s0**  
  .IX Item "FRAME_RATE, FR"
  frame rate, only defined for constant frame-rate video
* **\s-1PTS\s0**  
  .IX Item "PTS"
  The presentation timestamp in input
* **N**  
  .IX Item "N"
  The count of the input frame for video or the number of consumed samples,
  not including the current frame for audio, starting from 0.
* **\s-1NB\_CONSUMED\_SAMPLES\s0**  
  .IX Item "NB_CONSUMED_SAMPLES"
  The number of consumed samples, not including the current frame (only
  audio)
* **\s-1NB_SAMPLES, S\s0**  
  .IX Item "NB_SAMPLES, S"
  The number of samples in the current frame (only audio)
* **\s-1SAMPLE_RATE, SR\s0**  
  .IX Item "SAMPLE_RATE, SR"
  The audio sample rate.
* **\s-1STARTPTS\s0**  
  .IX Item "STARTPTS"
  The \s-1PTS\s0 of the first frame.
* **\s-1STARTT\s0**  
  .IX Item "STARTT"
  the time in seconds of the first frame
* **\s-1INTERLACED\s0**  
  .IX Item "INTERLACED"
  State whether the current frame is interlaced.
* **T**  
  .IX Item "T"
  the time in seconds of the current frame
* **\s-1POS\s0**  
  .IX Item "POS"
  original position in the file of the frame, or undefined if undefined
  for the current frame
* **\s-1PREV\_INPTS\s0**  
  .IX Item "PREV_INPTS"
  The previous input \s-1PTS.\s0
* **\s-1PREV\_INT\s0**  
  .IX Item "PREV_INT"
  previous input time in seconds
* **\s-1PREV\_OUTPTS\s0**  
  .IX Item "PREV_OUTPTS"
  The previous output \s-1PTS.\s0
* **\s-1PREV\_OUTT\s0**  
  .IX Item "PREV_OUTT"
  previous output time in seconds
* **\s-1RTCTIME\s0**  
  .IX Item "RTCTIME"
  The wallclock (\s-1RTC\s0) time in microseconds. This is deprecated, use **time**\|(0)
  instead.
* **\s-1RTCSTART\s0**  
  .IX Item "RTCSTART"
  The wallclock (\s-1RTC\s0) time at the start of the movie in microseconds.
* **\s-1TB\s0**  
  .IX Item "TB"
  The timebase of the input timestamps.

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Start counting \s-1PTS\s0 from zero
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          setpts=PTS-STARTPTS
  .Ve
* ·  
  Apply fast motion effect:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          setpts=0.5*PTS
  .Ve
* ·  
  Apply slow motion effect:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          setpts=2.0*PTS
  .Ve
* ·  
  Set fixed rate of 25 frames per second:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          setpts=N/(25*TB)
  .Ve
* ·  
  Set fixed rate 25 fps with some jitter:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          setpts=1/(25*TB) * (N + 0.05 * sin(N*2*PI/25))\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Apply an offset of 10 seconds to the input \s-1PTS:\s0
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          setpts=PTS+10/TB
  .Ve
* ·  
  Generate timestamps from a live source\*(R" and rebase onto the current timebase:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          setpts=(RTCTIME - RTCSTART) / (TB * 1000000)\*(Aq
  .Ve
* ·  
  Generate timestamps by counting samples:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          asetpts=N/SR/TB
  .Ve

<a name="setrange"></a>

### setrange

.IX Subsection "setrange"
Force color range for the output video frame.

The \f(CW`setrange\*(C' filter marks the color range property for the
output frames. It does not change the input frame, but only sets the
corresponding property, which affects how the frame is treated by
following filters.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **range**  
  .IX Item "range"
  Available values are:
    * **auto**  
      .IX Item "auto"
      Keep the same color range property.
    * **unspecified, unknown**  
      .IX Item "unspecified, unknown"
      Set the color range as unspecified.
    * **limited, tv, mpeg**  
      .IX Item "limited, tv, mpeg"
      Set the color range as limited.
    * **full, pc, jpeg**  
      .IX Item "full, pc, jpeg"
      Set the color range as full.

<a name="settb-asettb"></a>

### settb, asettb

.IX Subsection "settb, asettb"
Set the timebase to use for the output frames timestamps.
It is mainly useful for testing timebase configuration.

It accepts the following parameters:

* **expr, tb**  
  .IX Item "expr, tb"
  The expression which is evaluated into the output timebase.

The value for **tb** is an arithmetic expression representing a
rational. The expression can contain the constants \s-1AVTB\*(R"\s0 (the default
timebase), intb\*(R" (the input timebase) and \*(L"sr\*(R" (the sample rate,
audio only). Default value is intb\*(R".

_Examples_
.IX Subsection "Examples"

* ·  
  Set the timebase to 1/25:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          settb=expr=1/25
  .Ve
* ·  
  Set the timebase to 1/10:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          settb=expr=0.1
  .Ve
* ·  
  Set the timebase to 1001/1000:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          settb=1+0.001
  .Ve
* ·  
  Set the timebase to 2*intb:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          settb=2*intb
  .Ve
* ·  
  Set the default timebase value:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          settb=AVTB
  .Ve

<a name="showcqt"></a>

### showcqt

.IX Subsection "showcqt"
Convert input audio to a video output representing frequency spectrum
logarithmically using Brown-Puckette constant Q transform algorithm with
direct frequency domain coefficient calculation (but the transform itself
is not really constant Q, instead the Q factor is actually variable/clamped),
with musical tone scale, from E0 to D#10.

The filter accepts the following options:

* **size, s**  
  .IX Item "size, s"
  Specify the video size for the output. It must be even. For the syntax of this option,
  check the **Video size\*(R" section in the ffmpeg-utils manual**.
  Default value is \f(CW`1920x1080\*(C'.
* **fps, rate, r**  
  .IX Item "fps, rate, r"
  Set the output frame rate. Default value is \f(CW25.
* **bar\_h**  
  .IX Item "bar_h"
  Set the bargraph height. It must be even. Default value is \f(CW`-1\*(C' which
  computes the bargraph height automatically.
* **axis\_h**  
  .IX Item "axis_h"
  Set the axis height. It must be even. Default value is \f(CW`-1\*(C' which computes
  the axis height automatically.
* **sono\_h**  
  .IX Item "sono_h"
  Set the sonogram height. It must be even. Default value is \f(CW`-1\*(C' which
  computes the sonogram height automatically.
* **fullhd**  
  .IX Item "fullhd"
  Set the fullhd resolution. This option is deprecated, use _size_, _s_
  instead. Default value is \f(CW1.
* **sono_v, volume**  
  .IX Item "sono_v, volume"
  Specify the sonogram volume expression. It can contain variables:
    * **bar\_v**  
      .IX Item "bar_v"
      the _bar\_v_ evaluated expression
    * **frequency, freq, f**  
      .IX Item "frequency, freq, f"
      the frequency where it is evaluated
    * **timeclamp, tc**  
      .IX Item "timeclamp, tc"
      the value of _timeclamp_ option
      .Sp
      and functions:
    * **a\_weighting(f)**  
      .IX Item "a_weighting(f)"
      A-weighting of equal loudness
    * **b\_weighting(f)**  
      .IX Item "b_weighting(f)"
      B-weighting of equal loudness
    * **c\_weighting(f)**  
      .IX Item "c_weighting(f)"
      C-weighting of equal loudness.
      .Sp
      Default value is \f(CW16.
* **bar_v, volume2**  
  .IX Item "bar_v, volume2"
  Specify the bargraph volume expression. It can contain variables:
    * **sono\_v**  
      .IX Item "sono_v"
      the _sono\_v_ evaluated expression
    * **frequency, freq, f**  
      .IX Item "frequency, freq, f"
      the frequency where it is evaluated
    * **timeclamp, tc**  
      .IX Item "timeclamp, tc"
      the value of _timeclamp_ option
      .Sp
      and functions:
    * **a\_weighting(f)**  
      .IX Item "a_weighting(f)"
      A-weighting of equal loudness
    * **b\_weighting(f)**  
      .IX Item "b_weighting(f)"
      B-weighting of equal loudness
    * **c\_weighting(f)**  
      .IX Item "c_weighting(f)"
      C-weighting of equal loudness.
      .Sp
      Default value is \f(CW`sono\_v\*(C'.
* **sono_g, gamma**  
  .IX Item "sono_g, gamma"
  Specify the sonogram gamma. Lower gamma makes the spectrum more contrast,
  higher gamma makes the spectrum having more range. Default value is \f(CW3.
  Acceptable range is \f(CW`[1, 7]\*(C'.
* **bar_g, gamma2**  
  .IX Item "bar_g, gamma2"
  Specify the bargraph gamma. Default value is \f(CW1. Acceptable range is
  \f(CW`[1, 7]\*(C'.
* **bar\_t**  
  .IX Item "bar_t"
  Specify the bargraph transparency level. Lower value makes the bargraph sharper.
  Default value is \f(CW1. Acceptable range is \f(CW`[0, 1]\*(C'.
* **timeclamp, tc**  
  .IX Item "timeclamp, tc"
  Specify the transform timeclamp. At low frequency, there is trade-off between
  accuracy in time domain and frequency domain. If timeclamp is lower,
  event in time domain is represented more accurately (such as fast bass drum),
  otherwise event in frequency domain is represented more accurately
  (such as bass guitar). Acceptable range is \f(CW`[0.002, 1]\*(C'. Default value is \f(CW0.17.
* **attack**  
  .IX Item "attack"
  Set attack time in seconds. The default is \f(CW0 (disabled). Otherwise, it
  limits future samples by applying asymmetric windowing in time domain, useful
  when low latency is required. Accepted range is \f(CW`[0, 1]\*(C'.
* **basefreq**  
  .IX Item "basefreq"
  Specify the transform base frequency. Default value is \f(CW20.01523126408007475,
  which is frequency 50 cents below E0. Acceptable range is \f(CW`[10, 100000]\*(C'.
* **endfreq**  
  .IX Item "endfreq"
  Specify the transform end frequency. Default value is \f(CW20495.59681441799654,
  which is frequency 50 cents above D#10. Acceptable range is \f(CW`[10, 100000]\*(C'.
* **coeffclamp**  
  .IX Item "coeffclamp"
  This option is deprecated and ignored.
* **tlength**  
  .IX Item "tlength"
  Specify the transform length in time domain. Use this option to control accuracy
  trade-off between time domain and frequency domain at every frequency sample.
  It can contain variables:
    * **frequency, freq, f**  
      .IX Item "frequency, freq, f"
      the frequency where it is evaluated
    * **timeclamp, tc**  
      .IX Item "timeclamp, tc"
      the value of _timeclamp_ option.
      .Sp
      Default value is \f(CW`384*tc/(384+tc*f)\*(C'.
* **count**  
  .IX Item "count"
  Specify the transform count for every video frame. Default value is \f(CW6.
  Acceptable range is \f(CW`[1, 30]\*(C'.
* **fcount**  
  .IX Item "fcount"
  Specify the transform count for every single pixel. Default value is \f(CW0,
  which makes it computed automatically. Acceptable range is \f(CW`[0, 10]\*(C'.
* **fontfile**  
  .IX Item "fontfile"
  Specify font file for use with freetype to draw the axis. If not specified,
  use embedded font. Note that drawing with font file or embedded font is not
  implemented with custom _basefreq_ and _endfreq_, use _axisfile_
  option instead.
* **font**  
  .IX Item "font"
  Specify fontconfig pattern. This has lower priority than _fontfile_.
  The : in the pattern may be replaced by | to avoid unnecessary escaping.
* **fontcolor**  
  .IX Item "fontcolor"
  Specify font color expression. This is arithmetic expression that should return
  integer value 0xRRGGBB. It can contain variables:
    * **frequency, freq, f**  
      .IX Item "frequency, freq, f"
      the frequency where it is evaluated
    * **timeclamp, tc**  
      .IX Item "timeclamp, tc"
      the value of _timeclamp_ option
      .Sp
      and functions:
    * **midi(f)**  
      .IX Item "midi(f)"
      midi number of frequency f, some midi numbers: E0(16), C1(24), C2(36), A4(69)
    * **r(x), g(x), b(x)**  
      .IX Item "r(x), g(x), b(x)"
      red, green, and blue value of intensity x.
      .Sp
      Default value is \f(CW`st(0, (midi(f)-59.5)/12);
